Business Manager, Financial Planning & Operations (Copilot, Apps, and Platform, CTO Exec Office)

The Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) CTO organization is hiring a Business Manager to join its Executive Office. This role manages people, non-people, and discretionary budgets and provides reporting and insights that help leaders make informed workforce and investment decisions. It works closely with the Chief of Staff, CTO, leadership team, Finance, HR, Global Talent Acquisition, Procurement, engineering leaders, purchase-order owners, and administrative partners.

The role combines horizontal and vertical responsibilities. It contributes to CAP CTO financial governance, workforce practices, reporting, AI-enabled process improvement, and cross-team initiatives, while supporting aligned leadership teams with their workforce and budget portfolios. Day to day, the work moves between financial analysis, data reconciliation, leadership reporting, workforce and funding actions, partner problem-solving, and support for organizational transitions.

This opportunity is well suited to someone with strong financial and analytical judgment, exceptional organization and attention to detail, discretion with sensitive information, and the ability to create clarity when information is incomplete. Success means leaders have reliable workforce and budget information, risks and choices are communicated early, actions close on time, and recurring work becomes simpler and more scalable.

This role is based in Redmond, WA and is designated as an onsite position. While the formal requirement is a minimum of three days per week in the office, the team typically works onsite approximately four days per week, flexing based on business priorities, collaboration needs, customer engagements, and key milestones.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

Resource Allocation and Workforce Planning

The Business Manager coordinates resource allocation and workforce planning for CAP CTO and aligned leadership teams. It is responsible for consolidating inputs, developing scenarios within established priorities, maintaining source-of-truth data, executing approved allocation decisions, tracking actions through implementation, and communicating risks and options; it consults Finance, HR, Global Talent Acquisition, and managers and keeps leaders informed. The outcome is accurate workforce information, timely execution, and resources aligned to approved priorities.

People Budget, Headcount, and Backfill Management

The role manages funded headcount and position-number reconciliation, hiring and backfill plans, university and intern hiring inputs, transfers, mobility, location actions, workforce forecasts, and related system updates. It applies established CAP and corporate guidance, coordinates required approvals, and executes defined aspects of reorganizations, organization-design changes, workforce transfers, and resource reallocations through data preparation, workback plans, stakeholder coordination, system actions, and implementation tracking. The outcome is headcount that reflects approved plans and workforce changes that complete accurately and on time.

Non-People and Discretionary Budget Management

The role manages non-people and discretionary budgets across vendors, purchase orders, cloud and GPU capacity, AI token spend, and related investments. It is responsible for targets, controls, forecasts, audits, and regular reviews; it consults Finance, Procurement, engineering, and purchase-order owners to resolve variance, identify course corrections, and develop options for leaders. The outcome is disciplined spend and investment aligned to the highest-value work.

Reporting, Insights, and Decision Support

The role delivers regular and ad hoc reporting on workforce, spend, forecasts, and investment performance. It identifies trends, risks, opportunities, and available choices and translates them into clear insights and recommendations; it consults relevant partners and keeps the Chief of Staff and leadership team informed. The outcome is shared understanding, earlier action, and clear follow-through on decisions.

The role also partners with the leadership team on planning activities and business reviews that directly relate to its portfolio, coordinates with corporate planning processes, reviews privacy and compliance requirements, and supports continuity of business operations during periods of change or special circumstances.

Organizational Health and Change

The role supports the workforce-related dimensions of organizational health, including org hygiene, workforce and geographic mix, compliance training, and employee signals that affect workforce or investment decisions. It partners with HR and designated owners to apply company guidance, define actions and communications, and track progress, including during organizational transitions. The outcome is a healthy workforce plan, clear follow-through on organizational priorities, and continuity through change.

AI-First Operating Practices

The role helps transform the portfolio of recurring workforce and budget-management work using AI. It is responsible for identifying manual work, building centralized tooling and automated workflows with clear guardrails and exception paths, measuring improvements in speed, cost, quality, and effort, and sharing proven prompts, skills, and practices across the Business Management community. Over time this work is expected to reduce Business Management support needs further down in the organization, while human expertise, relationships, judgment, and accountability remain central.

 

What Will Help You Succeed

  • Strong analytical and financial judgment, with the ability to move from accurate execution to forecasting, scenario analysis, and clear recommendations.

  • Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, deadlines, and stakeholders.

  • The ability to build trusted relationships across Finance, HR, Procurement, and Business Support, and to present a clear point of view.

  • Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive employee, organizational, and compensation-adjacent information.

  • Experience building or improving AI-enabled workflows that enhance human expertise and produce measurable business value.



Qualifications

    • OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

    • OR Bachelor's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 8+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years experience in financial management, business planning, budget management, business or operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles.
  • Demonstrated organizational experience, managing multiple projects with different deliverables and timelines simultaneously.
  • Ability to create and maintain positive relationships, influence and collaborate internally and externally.
  • Experience leveraging AI tools and processes.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate details and data into clear strategy for leadership and varied audiences.

This role goes beyond traditional DBA responsibilities. You will shape how the service designs, uses, operates, and evolves its databases at scale—partnering closely with software engineers, SREs, and architects to drive durable reliability and performance improvements.Success in this role is measured by service‑level impact, technical influence, and long‑term reliability outcomes, not by task execution alone.



Responsibilities

Database Reliability, Performance, and Scale Own the availability, durability, and performance of large‑scale Azure SQL databases supporting a production Azure service.Lead deep performance tuning efforts, including query plan analysis, indexing strategies, concurrency control, stored procedure optimization, and workload isolation.Diagnose and resolve complex issues such as deadlocks, blocking, resource contention, latency spikes, memory pressure, and failover behaviors.Define and drive capacity planning models, performance guardrails, and growth readiness strategies.

Engineering Partnership and Architectural Influence Partner with software engineers and architects to influence how the service uses Azure SQL, including schema design, access patterns, transaction boundaries, and consistency models.Review and guide database‑related design proposals with a focus on long‑term reliability, operability, scalability, and cost efficiency.Advocate for engineering solutions that reduce ongoing operational burden and eliminate repetitive manual work.

Observability and Proactive Health Define and evolve deep Azure SQL telemetry, including latency, throughput, waits, failures, saturation signals, and early‑warning indicators.Use data to proactively identify reliability risks, performance regressions, and emerging capacity constraints.Partner with SREs to integrate database health signals into service‑level monitoring and reliability models.

Incident Response and Root Cause OwnershipServe as the database technical authority during live‑site incidents and on‑call rotations.Lead root cause analysis for database‑related outages and reliability events. 

Reliability Fundamentals and Reuse Identify and reduce database technical debt to improve maintainability, predictability, and operational simplicity.Build reusable tooling, automation, and standards that improve database operations across the service.Share best practices, documentation, and learnings to raise the reliability bar beyond your immediate team.

Overview

As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT) - Night Shift, you will stage, set up and perform hardware deployments. In addition, you will also perform troubleshooting and diagnostics on equipment, as well as perform hardware decommissions for simple changes and refreshes following Standard Operating Procedures. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your understanding of Data Center standard processes and procedures, develop mentoring skills while providing guidance to peers, familiarizing yourself with security and data management procedures, and accelerate your career growth in the process.

 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

 

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.



Responsibilities

Datacenter Operations

 

  • Demonstrates an applied understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Demonstrates a fundamental understanding of the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment.

 

  • Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.

 

  • Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.

 

  • Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type independently. Provides guidance and/or assists less experienced technicians with complex tickets or tasks, and appropriately escalates challenging or complex tickets to more experienced technicians as needed.

 

Datacenter Work Environment

 

  • Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or established reporting methods.

 

  • Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

 

  • Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

 

  • Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

 

  • Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work. Provides, responds to, and encourages providing feedback regarding on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams.

 

  • Participates in daily safety briefings. Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, complies with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), completes required Task Hazard Analysis (THAs), and uses appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, taking proactive action to alert others of safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in regular cadence proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.

 

Managing Service

 

  • Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

 

  • Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.

 

  • Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.

 

  • Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.

 

Service Delivery

 

  • Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.

 

  • Develops and employs an effective execution order strategy for assigned tasks. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.

 

  • Performs diagnostics and troubleshooting and/or leverages standard procedures to quickly and efficiently identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption.   • Directly performs decommissions, simple changes (e.g., memory upgrades, OS rebuilds) and refreshes of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, and server equipment, following standard procedures with minimal guidance. Overview

We are looking for a Principal AI Architect to help define, build, and scale the evaluation systems that shape the future of AI products. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, applied science, product architecture, and AI evaluation. The ideal candidate has deep technical judgment, strong systems thinking, hands-on experience evaluating LLMs, and the ability to translate emerging AI capabilities into reliable product experiences. 

This role is especially important for agentic AI systems, where product behavior is often nondeterministic, context-dependent, and difficult to evaluate with traditional testing alone. The person in this role will help teams build a deep understanding of how agents behave, where they succeed, where they fail, which gaps matter most, and where those gaps should be addressed: in prompts, tools, orchestration, retrieval, ranking, product UX, safety systems, or core code. 

The Principal AI Architect will make AI product quality measurable, actionable, and deeply integrated into how teams build and ship. They will help teams evaluate product direction before code is complete, validate quality before launch, and continuously measure performance after release. 

They will give teams confidence in how agentic systems behave, where nondeterminism creates risk, which gaps matter, and where to address them. Their work will ensure that evaluation is not an afterthought, but a core part of the product lifecycle, engineering system, and release decision process. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Define the technical vision and architecture for AI, LLM, RAG, and agent evaluation systems across the product lifecycle.
  • Design evaluation frameworks that assess product quality before implementation is complete, during development, at launch, and post-ship.
  • Build an understanding of how nondeterministic agentic systems behave across tasks, users, contexts, tools, and product surfaces.
  • Identify behavioral gaps, failure modes, model limitations, retrieval issues, orchestration defects, and product-quality risks before they become customer-impacting issues.
  • Determine where issues should be addressed across the system: model behavior, prompts, tool use, search and retrieval, ranking, grounding, orchestration, UX, policy, telemetry, or product code.
  • Partner with engineering, applied science, and data science teams to bring ML, DS, LLM, RAG, and agent evaluation methods directly into product codebases and development workflows.
  • Integrate evals into build pipelines, release gates, experimentation systems, and engineering workflows so evaluation becomes a standard part of how products are built and shipped.
  • Make evaluation results easy to access, interpret, and act on through dashboards, scorecards, quality reports, and product-health views.
  • Build systems that connect product telemetry, offline evaluation, human judgment, automated evals, experimentation, RAG quality, agent behavior, and customer-quality signals.
  • Understand and evaluate enterprise search, RAG, grounding, indexing, ranking, permissions, freshness, and relevance systems for products such as Copilot.
  • Translate ambiguous product goals into measurable evaluation strategies, success criteria, timelines, and technical plans.
  • Drive architecture decisions across components, services, data pipelines, model interfaces, search systems, retrieval layers, evaluation harnesses, dashboards, and reporting systems.
  • Work with product leaders to prioritize evaluation investments and align them with product milestones and release decisions.
  • Mentor senior engineers and applied scientists on building reliable, scalable, and reusable evaluation infrastructure.
  • Stay current with LLM evaluation methods, agentic systems, RAG evaluation, benchmark design, prompt/model behavior, experimentation, and responsible AI practices.
  • In this role, you will help evaluate products before the code is fully ready, before launch, and after they ship.
  • You will work across product, engineering, applied science, and data science teams to bring rigorous LLM, RAG, agent, and AI evaluation practices into the product lifecycle.
  • You will help IC3 and partner teams understand whether AI systems are working as intended, where they fail, how they improve, and what it takes to ship them responsibly at scale.

Security represents the most critical priorities for our customers in a world awash in digital threats, regulatory scrutiny, and estate complexity. Microsoft Security aspires to make the world a safer place for all. We want to reshape security and empower every user, customer, and developer with a security cloud that protects them with end to end, simplified solutions. The Microsoft Security organization accelerates Microsoft’s mission and bold ambitions to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers’ heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world.


Attackers attempt to create billions of bot accounts daily on Microsoft platforms to perform phishing, spam and a variety of attacks. Attackers also run International Revenue Share Fraud (IRSF) against any public voice/SMS services. Our team builds both detections and blocking mechanisms against all the above attacks, in particular, focusing on fighting fraud. We constantly investigate the most advanced nation state attacks, and understand the latest techniques deployed by the most sophisticated attackers. We develop detections through training machine learning models, using threat intelligence signals as input, aggregated across entire Internet. We build state of the art machine learning platform for both training, deployment and monitoring. Our machine learning models protect billions of Microsoft users in real-time. With this team, you get a chance to learn new technology in AI, security, and distributed system design. We have experts in all these 3 areas to help you grow. Overview

As a Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

 

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

 

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays. 



Responsibilities

Critical Environment Culture

 

  • Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.

 

  • Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

 

  • Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

 

  • May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

 

Equipment and Systems Maintenance

 

  • Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.

 

  • Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.

 

  • Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.

 

  • Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.

 

  • Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.

 

Equipment and Systems Operations

 

  • Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometimes minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.

 

  • Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.

 

  • Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.

 

  • Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.

 

Working Conditions

 

  • Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

 

  • As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.

 

  • As indicated above, have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays

 

Other:

 

  • Embodies our culture and values


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

 

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.

 

  • 3+ years work/applied learning experience in mechanical, manufacturing, automotive, electrical, controls, data center, or related fields OR equivalent experience.

 

  • Ability speak, write and understand fluent English 

 

Background Check Requirements:

 


Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

 

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

 

While not required, we also look for the following Preferred Qualifications:

 

  • 4+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.

Orchestrate demand, supply, and sales alignment to deliver solid sell-in/sell-through outcomes, while improving channel efficiency, inventory health, and operational scalability. Overview

As a Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs). 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications. 

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide. 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day. 

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
 
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties


Responsibilities

Critical Environment Culture

  • May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
  • Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
  • Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
  • Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
  • Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs maintenance tasks and repairs that can be performed with minimal oversight. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees maintenance tasks within a single discipline or area of expertise. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance with established mastery of maintaining systems of a specific discipline.
  • Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
  • Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.
  • Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Equipment and Systems Operations
  • Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
  • Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
  • Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
  • Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Other
  • Embody our culture and values

    • OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 10+ years mission critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.

Responsibilities

  • Lead project-level schedule coordination and updates, including IMS maintenance, forecast adjustments, variance commentary, and alignment with site execution status. 

  • Develop, maintain, and update the project Integrated Master Schedule covering design, permitting, procurement, construction, commissioning, and readiness milestones. 

  • Own GC schedule management for assigned project(s), including weekly schedule review meetings, monthly schedule submissions, lookahead reviews, schedule narratives, progress validation, and action tracking. 

  • Support contractor baseline schedule development and evaluation during pre-construction, ensuring alignment with program guidance, requirements, project milestones, sequencing, and execution strategy. 

  • Validate GC schedule updates against field progress through site walks, GC inputs, actual start / finish dates, progress quantities, and milestone evidence. 

  • Analyze schedule performance by tracking critical path, float consumption, logic quality, forecast movement, schedule health, resource loading, resource curves, and schedule variance trends. 

  • Identify schedule risks, blockers, potential delays, and missed commitments, then document and communicate them through risk registers, weekly reporting, health reviews, and project forums. 

  • Conduct initial review and support validation of Time Impact Analyses (TIAs), EOT requests, delay narratives, and schedule change impacts before escalation to the Sub-Regional Planning Lead and internal stakeholders. 

  • Assess impacts of design changes, procurement / long-lead equipment delays, permitting constraints, commissioning constraints, construction sequencing changes, and labor / resource issues. 

  • Develop recovery schedule options, mitigation scenarios, and what-if analysis to support project decision-making and schedule optimization. 

  • Produce weekly and monthly schedule reports, including schedule status, milestone performance, lookahead risks, variance root cause, mitigation actions, and required stakeholder decisions. 

  • Support baseline management and change control throughout the project lifecycle by maintaining schedule assumptions, basis of schedule, change narratives, and decision records. 

  • Facilitate collaborative planning, pull planning, and lookahead sessions with GC and site teams to improve field coordination and execution readiness. 

  • Escalate risks, repeated schedule quality issues, missing GC submissions, or stakeholder blockers to the Sub-Regional Planning Lead with clear facts, options, and recommendations.

Additional or preferred qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
  • 7+ years experience working on data center projects.
  • Primavera P6 capability and understanding of CPM scheduling methodology. 

  • Experience maintaining construction project schedules and performing weekly / monthly schedule updates. 

     

  • Experience working with contractors, site teams, engineering, procurement, commissioning, and project controls stakeholders. 

     

  • Ability to prepare clear schedule narratives, variance commentary, risk updates, and forecast explanations.

The Windows Servicing Delivery (WSD) organization is responsible for delivering protected, productive, and predictable servicing experiences for Windows customers around the world. Overview

About AIx Design & Research 

If you're curious, creative, and excited by how AI is reshaping the practice of design, we'd love to work with you! The AI Experiences Design & Research team is a community of designers, researchers, and makers reimagining how people interact with technology. We design across Microsoft's AI-powered experiences, including Copilot, Edge, Bing, MSN, and emerging products, creating end-to-end journeys that span devices, platforms, and contexts. We're looking for people who embrace experimentation, use new tools to expand what's possible, and aren't afraid to move beyond traditional design boundaries. Together, we're building experiences that make AI more useful, intuitive, and delightful for billions of people around the world. Join us as we reimagine not only the products people use, but the future of design itself!  

The opportunity 

We’re looking for a hands-on design engineer who thinks like an artist and builds for the browser. On the Copilot Design team at Microsoft, you’ll originate a distinctive visual point of view and turn it into expressive, useful interactive experiences. Composition, typography, light, material, timing and physical behavior are part of your design vocabulary; JavaScript, shaders and real-time rendering are part of your medium. 

This is a specialist role for someone who can invent the experience and code it, not only implement a finished design. You’ll work across artistic exploration and production engineering, balancing surprise and delight with clarity, accessibility and responsiveness. The work asks for both ambition and restraint: know when motion makes an interaction more understandable, and when a quieter experience serves people better. 



Responsibilities
 
  • Conceive, sketch in code and refine distinctive interactive experiences. Make artistic decisions about composition, typography, light, material, rhythm and physical behavior, then test how those choices work in a real interface. 

  • Create code-driven motion, custom shaders and procedural or generative visuals that respond to user input and product state. Design coherent transitions and behaviors, not just isolated effects. 

  • Explore useful assistant interactions such as activity and progress, transitions, interruption and feedback. These are illustrative opportunities to investigate, not a commitment to a particular product roadmap. 

  • Develop production-ready components and partner with product engineering on integration, testing and maintenance. Carry the visual intent through implementation, including state changes, edge cases and graceful degradation. 

  • Turn successful explorations into reusable motion and graphics primitives, components and tools. Document the artistic and technical choices so other designers and engineers can extend the work without losing its character. 

  • Profile CPU and GPU work, frame time, memory, loading and input responsiveness. Build accessible, reduced-motion and non-GPU alternatives, and validate behavior across browsers, devices and different levels of graphics capability. 

  • Set a high creative and technical craft bar while staying hands-on. Mentor through critique and code review, explain trade-offs clearly and help partners choose purposeful expression over unnecessary spectacle. 



Qualifications
 

We value demonstrated craft and ownership, whether developed through professional roles, independent practice, open-source work or self-directed learning. Equivalent practical experience and nontraditional paths are welcome. The specialist capabilities below matter more than having used every tool in a particular stack. 

Required skills:

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Graphic Design, Product Design, Visual Design, Human Computer Interaction, or related field AND 4+ years experience working in product or service design and/or shipping production code
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Graphic Design, Product Design, Visual Design, Human Computer Interaction, or related field AND 6+ years experience working in product or service design and/or shipping production code
    • OR 8+ years experience working in product or service design and/or shipping production code
    • OR equivalent experience. 

Preferred Skills & Experience:

  • A portfolio showing original artistic direction and the ability to originate, develop and iterate visual ideas in code. You can explain why your choices in composition, typography, light, material and motion serve the experience. 

  • Strong hands-on coded motion and interaction design, including timing, easing, sequencing, spring or physics-based behavior, and responsive or interruptible transitions. Motion is a core craft, not a finishing layer. 

  • Hands-on real-time browser graphics using WebGL or WebGPU, including writing and adapting custom shaders. You understand rendering fundamentals well enough to shape the result, debug it and explain the trade-offs; GLSL or WGSL are examples of relevant shader languages. 

  • Strong JavaScript/TypeScript and contemporary browser engineering skills, including component architecture, asynchronous state, input handling, responsive interfaces and code review. You can integrate a graphics experience into a maintained product, not only a standalone demo. 

  • Experience profiling and improving browser rendering, loading, memory and input responsiveness. You can preserve visual intent while meeting accessibility needs, honoring reduced motion and providing reliable non-GPU paths across browsers and devices. 

  • Demonstrated ownership of ambiguous work from creative direction through delivery, with clear communication and effective design–engineering partnership. You welcome critique, make sound trade-offs and help others raise their artistic and technical craft.

  • Libraries are flexible. Three.js, React Three Fiber, GSAP and Motion are examples of useful tools, not a checklist. We care about the ideas you originate, your depth in motion and real-time graphics, and the quality of the browser experience you deliver.
  • Deeper WebGPU, compute or GPU profiling experience, including rendering pipelines, simulations or techniques for efficient procedural and generative graphics.
  • Experience building reusable motion or graphics systems, authoring tools or creative workflows that other people adopt and can maintain.
  • Experience designing for AI or assistant experiences, especially making complex or changing states understandable. An AI-specific background is welcome, not required.
  • A practice of sharing craft through thoughtful technical writing, creative coding experiments, open-source contributions, teaching or mentorship.

Microsoft AI is looking for engineers to build the compute infrastructure powering frontier-model development. The Compute Orchestration & Scheduling team owns cluster orchestration, workload scheduling, resource allocation, quota management, and the systems that enable fast initialization and reliable fault recovery on next-generation GPU supercomputers. 

Our team prepares infrastructure for the next generation of distributed training and inference across multiple locations and a rapidly growing fleet of accelerators, including NVIDIA Grace Blackwell, Vera Rubin, and AMD GPU platforms, alongside the CPU, network, and storage systems they depend on. 

Key challenges include topology-aware placement, large-scale distributed training, fast and reliable initialization of training runtimes, rapid recovery for long-running AI jobs, observability into cluster behavior, and improved utilization across increasingly large and diverse accelerator fleet. Better scheduling efficiency and platform reliability translate directly into more effective compute for AI research and products. 

You will work closely with researchers, model engineers, hardware architects, and infrastructure teams to turn frontier-model requirements into scalable platform capabilities. We value engineers who navigate ambiguity, remove roadblocks, and deliver improvements to users quickly and iteratively.

  • Develop and tune the compute infrastructure stack allocating NVIDIA Grace Blackwell (GB) and Vera Rubin (VR) resources to AI workloads. 

  • Scale GPU clusters across hardware generations to thousands of accelerators and beyond. 

  • Use operational data and workload insights to inform the compute (GPU and CPU) roadmap for large-scale AI research. 

  • Partner with model-development teams to improve the infrastructure used to train and serve AI models.

  • Experience with Ray, Kubernetes, Kueue, Volcano, or another AI-focused system for scheduling, scaling, or fault tolerance is especially relevant.

The Channel Leader is expected to scale through managers, develop proven leaders and empower strategic professionals to independently lead significant businesses, strategic partners and complex sales motions.Success requires the ability to operate simultaneously as a Sales Leader, People Leader and Ecosystem Leader, translating strategy into measurable customer and commercial outcomes.



Responsibilities

1. Lead the ASEAN and Korea Channel Business

Own the overall channel strategy, business performance and execution across ASEAN and Korea.Set clear sales priorities and translate regional ambitions into country, segment and partner execution plans.Drive sustainable growth through partners across cloud, AI, Copilot and the broader Microsoft portfolio.Identify growth opportunities and performance gaps using customer, partner, pipeline and business insights.Maintain clear accountability for execution, taking corrective action when performance is off plan.

2. Provide Strategic Sales Leadership

Operate as a proven Sales Leader, creating a high-performance sales culture centered on customer outcomes, pipeline, conversion and growth.Establish clear commercial priorities and ensure teams translate strategy into actionable sales motions.Drive disciplined pipeline management, including pipeline creation, progression, conversion and deal execution.Maintain appropriate executive focus on the largest opportunities, growth accelerators and business risks.Coach leaders and experienced sellers on deal strategy, partner orchestration and executive engagement.Connect partner capability and capacity directly to customer opportunities and sales priorities.Build a culture of sales excellence, rigor, speed and accountability, balancing short-term performance with sustainable long-term growth.

3. Lead Leaders and Develop a High-Performing Organization

Lead an organization comprising people managers and experienced individual contributors, with differentiated leadership appropriate to both populations.Act as a true manager of managers, setting direction and outcomes while empowering leaders to run their businesses and develop their teams.Coach managers to strengthen their own sales leadership, talent development and execution capabilities.Empower experienced individual contributors with significant ownership of strategic partners, businesses and transformational initiatives.Build a strategic succession pipeline and actively develop the next generation of sales and channel leaders.Create an inclusive, high-accountability culture where leaders and individuals understand what they own and are empowered to deliver.

4. Accelerate Partner-Led Sales Growth

Make the partner ecosystem an integrated part of the ASEAN and Korea sales engine.Drive partner-led customer acquisition, expansion, renewal and upsell.Accelerate priority motions across CSP, Azure, Security, AI and Copilot.Increase partner capability and capacity to sell, deploy and drive customer value from Microsoft solutions.Build repeatable sales motions that can scale across markets, customer segments and partners.Identify ecosystem coverage gaps and address them through development of existing partners, recruitment of new partners or evolution of business models.

5. Lead Strategic Partner Relationships

Serve as executive sponsor for the most important partner relationships across ASEAN and Korea.Engage CEOs and key partner executives on joint growth strategy, customer opportunity, investment, economics and execution.Build joint business plans with clear commercial outcomes, priorities and accountability.Challenge partners to increase their investment, capabilities, customer reach and execution against shared opportunities.Balance strategic relationship development with rigorous accountability for measurable business impact.

6. Orchestrate Customer and Partner Sales Execution

Partner closely with Corporate, SMB, Enterprise, Solution Area and Customer Success leadership to create one integrated sales motion.Ensure partners are incorporated early into account, territory and opportunity planning where they can accelerate customer outcomes.Connect the right partner capabilities to the right customer opportunities.Drive clarity of roles between direct and partner-led sales teams, reducing friction and increasing execution velocity.Mobilize the broader organization around strategic opportunities requiring cross-functional and cross-market orchestration.

7. Run the Business with Precision

Establish a rigorous operating rhythm across geographies, teams and strategic partners.Use data and business insights to determine where leadership intervention will have the greatest impact.Drive accountability around pipeline, conversion, customer acquisition, partner contribution, consumption and growth.Maintain clear inspection of business performance while avoiding unnecessary operational complexity.Differentiate between structural market challenges and execution gaps and act decisively on both.Ensure resources and leadership attention are concentrated on the highest-value opportunities. 

 

Leadership Expectations

The ASEAN and Korea Channel Leader is expected to demonstrate the ability to:

Lead through leaders
Scale impact by setting clear outcomes, empowering managers and holding the leadership organization accountable.

Lead senior talent
Create an environment where experienced individual contributors have the autonomy, executive access and accountability to deliver substantial business outcomes.

Lead sales
Create pipeline, accelerate opportunities, drive conversion and establish a culture of consistent sales execution.

Lead the business
Understand the numbers, identify opportunities and risks early and translate insights into action.

Lead the ecosystem
Understand partner economics and business models and translate Microsoft priorities into compelling growth opportunities for partners.

Lead across boundaries
Influence customer, sales, engineering, marketing and operational organizations without relying on organizational authority.

Lead executive relationships
Build credibility with C-suite partner executives, customers and key internal stakeholders.

Lead transformation
Evolve the partner sales model for the AI and cloud era, evolving established practices and creating new paths to scale. 



Qualifications

Required/minimum qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Business Operations, Computer Science or a related field AND 10+ years experience in partner management, sales, business development, or partner channel development in the technology industry or related experience OR equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years people management experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Business Administration, Business Science, or an Advanced Degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) or a related field AND 12+ years experience in partner management, sales, business development, or partner channel development in the technology industry or related experience OR equivalent experience.
  • 8+ years people management experience.

 

The successful candidate should bring:

  • Significant experienced sales, channel, partner or commercial leadership experience in technology, cloud or a comparable complex industry.Demonstrated success owning and growing a substantial sales or commercial business.
  • Proven experience leading organizations through other people managers, as well as directly leading experienced individual contributors.
  • Proven track record of building pipeline, driving complex sales execution and delivering commercial outcomes across multiple markets.
  • Experience building or transforming partner ecosystems and indirect sales models.
  • Excel in understanding of partner economics, incentives, profitability and go-to-market models.
  • Executive-level communication, relationship building and influencing capabilities.
  • Ability to operate successfully across diverse cultures, markets and levels of business maturity.
  • Good analytical and commercial judgment coupled with the ability to make decisions and execute with speed.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop leaders, build succession and create high-performing, inclusive organizations.

Overview 

As a Data Center Technician Manager, you will lead and develop a team of Data Center Technicians supporting Microsoft’s datacenter operations in Thailand. 

You will be responsible for technician team performance, workforce readiness, operational execution, service quality, safety, security, compliance, and continuous improvement. The role requires strong people leadership together with practical experience managing IT operations involving enterprise and high-performance computing servers, network equipment, fiber-optic and copper cabling, and related IT equipment. 

You will collaborate with local, regional, and global Microsoft teams, as well as service partners, vendors, landlords, and colocation providers, to deliver safe, secure, reliable, and high-quality datacenter operations. 

This position requires full-time onsite work in Chonburi, Thailand. 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations + Innovation organization powers the infrastructure and foundational technologies supporting Microsoft’s online services. Our culture is grounded in respect, integrity, accountability, inclusion, and a growth mindset. 



Responsibilities

People Leadership 

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Data Center Technicians, creating a safe, inclusive, accountable, and high-performing team culture. 

  • Establish clear responsibilities, priorities, performance expectations, and operational standards. 

  • Manage workforce planning, workload allocation, technician capability, training, performance, development, and operational readiness. 

  • Support recruitment, onboarding, technical qualification, career development, recognition, and retention. 

  • Identify capability gaps and implement appropriate coaching, cross-training, and development actions. 

IT Operations and Service Delivery 

  • Manage daily datacenter IT operations involving enterprise and high-performance computing servers, network equipment, fiber-optic and copper cabling, and related IT equipment and accessories. 

  • Plan, prioritize, assign, and monitor work based on business priorities, service risks, workforce capability, and resource availability. 

  • Manage ticket queues, workloads, backlogs, handovers, and escalations to support timely and predictable service delivery. 

  • Oversee hardware installation, deployment, diagnostics, break-fix, cabling, inventory, asset handling, and equipment decommissioning. 

  • Ensure compliance with approved procedures, runbooks, change controls, safety requirements, quality standards, and documentation requirements. 

  • Monitor KPIs, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), quality results, backlog health, and recurring issues, and drive corrective and continuous-improvement actions. 

Safety, Security, and Incident Management 

  • Promote a strong safety culture and ensure employees and vendors comply with Microsoft, regulatory, customer, and site-specific safety, security, access, and operational requirements. 

  • Ensure risk assessments, Personal Protective Equipment, work controls, and Stop Work Authority are understood and applied. 

  • Lead and coordinate technician response to operational events and incidents, including resource mobilization, onsite actions, escalation, evidence collection, and factual status reporting. 

  • Support incident management, root-cause analysis, lessons learned, and corrective and preventive actions. 

  • Ensure effective handover and continuity for unresolved incidents, high-risk activities, blocked work, and outstanding actions. 

Stakeholder and Vendor Management 

  • Collaborate with Critical Environment, Logistics, Security, Safety, Engineering, Deployment, Project, Asset Management, Supply Chain, and regional datacenter operations teams. 

  • Coordinate with service partners, vendors, landlords, and colocation providers to support effective site operations. 

  • Manage vendor-resource readiness, work schedules, scope alignment, site access, execution quality, and compliance. 

  • Identify operational, resource, vendor, safety, quality, or service risks and engage the appropriate stakeholders for resolution. 

  • Communicate operational status, risks, dependencies, decisions, and required support clearly to local, regional, and global stakeholders. 

Operational Excellence 

  • Maintain readiness of technician staffing, training, tools, procedures, systems access, vendor support, and operational documentation. 

  • Identify recurring operational issues, execution defects, process gaps, and improvement opportunities. 

  • Lead or support root-cause analysis, process improvement, standardization, and operational-excellence initiatives. 

  • Share lessons learned and effective practices with other datacenter locations and regional teams. 

  • Embody Microsoft’s culture and values. 

 



Qualifications

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related technical discipline. 

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in IT operations, including at least 5 years managing technical operations or IT service-delivery teams in an enterprise, datacenter, high-performance computing, or other mission-critical environment. 

  • Demonstrated management experience covering enterprise and high-performance computing servers, network equipment, fiber-optic and copper cabling, and associated IT equipment and accessories. 

  • Strong people-management experience, including workforce planning, workload assignment, coaching, capability development, performance management, and operational escalation. 

  • Practical technical knowledge of enterprise servers, network equipment, racks, structured cabling, fiber-optic infrastructure, hardware diagnostics, break-fix, deployment, and decommissioning. 

  • Experience managing performance through KPIs, SLAs, ticket queues, backlogs, quality results, and corrective actions. 

  • Experience working in a production, mission-critical, or 24x7 operational environment. 

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate incident response, cross-functional activities, operational risks, and escalations. 

  • Strong stakeholder- and vendor-management skills with the ability to resolve execution blockers and drive actions to closure. 

  • Fluent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate effectively with local, regional, and global stakeholders. 

  • Ability and willingness to work full-time onsite at Microsoft datacenter locations in Chonburi, Thailand. 

  • Ability to support business-critical incidents and operational escalations outside standard business hours when required.
