Overview

As a Microsoft Data Center Project Manager, you will lead and manage the end-to-end delivery of large-scale datacenter IT infrastructure projects supporting the build-out, onboarding, and operationalization of new datacenter capacity in Thailand. 

The primary focus of this role is IT project management, including large-scale server deployment, network infrastructure implementation, datacenter rack and enclosure deployment, structured copper and fiber-optic cabling, storage and physical IT infrastructure, technology refreshes, capacity expansion, migrations, and decommissioning. 

You will create, manage, and communicate end-to-end project plans and be accountable for delivering assigned projects safely, securely, on time, within approved scope and budget, and in accordance with Microsoft quality and compliance requirements. 

You will also coordinate planned project execution and preventive maintenance activities within live IT production environments. You will ensure that appropriate risk controls, mitigation measures, contingency plans, and rollback or recovery arrangements are established to prevent or minimize service interruption. 

You will collaborate with Engineering, Datacenter Operations, Deployment, Network, Critical Environment, Security, Logistics, Supply Chain, Asset Management, and regional infrastructure teams. You will also coordinate with suppliers, service partners, contractors, landlords, and colocation providers to identify dependencies, manage risks, remove delivery obstacles, and successfully transition completed projects into operations. 

This position requires full-time onsite work in Chonburi, Thailand. 



Responsibilities

End-to-End IT Project Delivery 

  • Create, manage, and communicate end-to-end project plans for large-scale datacenter IT infrastructure projects. 

  • Manage project scope, schedules, milestones, budgets, resources, dependencies, risks, issues, changes, quality requirements, acceptance criteria, and closure. 

  • Deliver projects involving:  

  • Large-scale server deployment 

  • Enterprise and datacenter network infrastructure implementation 

  • Datacenter racks and enclosures 

  • Storage and physical IT infrastructure 

  • Structured copper and fiber-optic cabling 

  • Capacity expansion and infrastructure upgrades 

  • Equipment migrations and technology refreshes 

  • Infrastructure and equipment decommissioning 

  • Conduct regular project reviews and check-ins to monitor progress, delivery quality, risks, issues, dependencies, and required actions. 

  • Identify project gaps and obstacles, establish mitigation or recovery actions, and escalate through the appropriate channels when required. 

  • Ensure projects are completed safely, securely, on time, within approved scope and budget, and with the required level of quality. 

  • Maintain accurate project plans, schedules, risk and issue registers, decision logs, change records, status reports, acceptance evidence, and closure documentation. 

  • Ensure completed projects meet agreed acceptance criteria and are successfully handed over to the responsible operations teams. 

Technical and Operational Coordination 

  • Translate technical and business requirements into executable project plans, work packages, resource requirements, milestones, and acceptance criteria. 

  • Coordinate planned activities, including project execution, infrastructure deployment, upgrades, migrations, technology refreshes, testing, and preventive maintenance affecting datacenter IT systems and infrastructure. 

  • Develop and validate implementation plans, Methods of Procedure, risk assessments, maintenance windows, technical dependencies, communication plans, contingency measures, and rollback or recovery arrangements before execution. 

  • Coordinate technical dependencies involving servers, storage, network equipment, racks, structured cabling, fiber-optic infrastructure, logistics, assets, power, cooling, security, access, and operational readiness. 

  • Work with Engineering, Datacenter Operations, Deployment, Network, Critical Environment, Security, Logistics, Supply Chain, Asset Management, DC Build Managers, and regional infrastructure teams to assess potential impacts on the IT production environment. 

  • Ensure appropriate mitigation and operational controls are established to prevent or minimize:  

  • Service interruption 

  • Equipment impact 

  • Capacity constraints 

  • Availability risks 

  • Other adverse impacts on the IT production environment 

  • Confirm that required resources, approvals, access, tools, materials, technical support, escalation paths, and recovery arrangements are available before planned work begins. 

  • Coordinate implementation activities within live, production, or mission-critical datacenter environments and monitor execution against the approved plan. 

  • Ensure project and preventive maintenance activities follow approved designs, Methods of Procedure, change controls, safety requirements, security controls, quality standards, and operational requirements.

Overview

At Microsoft, our mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Within Frontier Industry Advisory, part of Microsoft Frontier Company, Industry Advisors are a strategic lever for differentiated growth: driving net-new opportunity, co-innovation, and industry-led transformation for the world’s most influential customers.

As a Media & Entertainment Industry Advisor on the Telecommunications and Media team, you will serve as an industry authority and trusted advisor to executive decision-makers at Microsoft’s most strategic Media & Entertainment customers, across advertising, publishing, streaming, and content & media in the United States. You will shape early-stage demand by translating customer priorities into industry-specific use cases, business scenarios, and multi-year transformation roadmaps, leading with AI to help customers optimize operations, reinvent content creation, and unlock new monetization models.

Operating with a high degree of autonomy and influence, you will guide early-stage opportunities, nurture executive relationships that generate new business, and orchestrate account teams and partners to convert industry vision into pipeline and commercial outcomes. As an industry thought leader, you will continuously deepen your expertise, represent Microsoft at the most senior levels, and raise the capability of the teams around you through your insight.

As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.



Responsibilities

Industry Thought Leadership & Executive Engagement

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to C-level and business-unit executives across Media & Entertainment, shaping AI and digital transformation strategy.
  • Lead executive conversations grounded in industry transformation principles, optimizing operations, redefining content creation, and unlocking monetization.
  • Engage stakeholders beyond IT (content, editorial, production, marketing, advertising, and monetization leaders) using persona-based industry narratives.
  • Represent Microsoft as an industry authority at executive briefings, industry events, and customer forums.

Demand Generation & Pipeline Creation

  • Lead early-stage opportunity development through industry-led insights, use cases, and scenario-based selling.
  • Originate and qualify high-value transformation opportunities, prioritizing scalable, repeatable Media & Entertainment use cases.
  • Create demand across key verticals, content creation & production, streaming & distribution, audience engagement, and advertising & monetization.
  • Generate opportunities through co-innovation, outbound partner collaboration, and executive engagement.

Industry-Led Account Planning

  • Act as the industry subject-matter expert within account teams, aligning strategy to customer business priorities and Microsoft’s industry point of view.
  • Translate customer priorities into multi-year transformation roadmaps and a qualified pipeline.
  • Partner with account teams and specialists to shape opportunities and drive execution from strategy through delivery.

Co-Innovation & Partner Ecosystem Leadership

  • Drive co-innovation with software vendors, systems integrators, and Media & Entertainment industry partners to design and scale differentiated solutions.
  • Lead outbound partner engagements to create and accelerate opportunities aligned to customer needs.
  • Identify ecosystem gaps and influence partner strategy to meet emerging industry needs across the media value chain.

AI & Digital Transformation Leadership

  • Champion AI-first transformation scenarios, including AI-powered content creation and production workflows; media supply-chain optimization and AI-driven automation; real-time personalization and audience engagement; and data-driven monetization and advertising intelligence.
  • Help customers move from early experiments to enterprise-scale, responsible AI adoption and real business value, keeping human creativity and judgment at the center.

Field Enablement & Industry Leadership

  • Translate Media & Entertainment insight into actionable guidance for sales and technical teams.
  • Mentor colleagues and contribute to skilling and readiness across the organization.
  • Share industry insight, competitive intelligence, and customer feedback to influence product, marketing, and strategy teams.


Qualifications

Required / minimum qualifications

  • Master’s Degree in Business, Technology, Media/Communications, Engineering, or a related field AND 5+ years of customer-facing experience in the Media & Entertainment industry (advertising, publishing, streaming, content/media) or in industry-focused consulting, digital strategy, or transformation roles serving these sectors
    • OR Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Technology, Media/Communications, Engineering, or a related field AND 7+ years of customer-facing experience in the Media & Entertainment industry (advertising, publishing, streaming, content/media) or in industry-focused consulting, digital strategy, or transformation roles serving these sectors
    • OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Experience and fluency with AI translation - demonstrate deep awareness of how the media ecosystem works end to end, how content is created, produced, distributed, monetized, measured, and experienced. Ability to translate that industry context into practical AI scenarios that matter to business leaders, from creative workflows and production efficiency to audience engagement, advertising effectiveness, rights, data, and new revenue models.
  • Experience in the Media & Entertainment value chain - from content creation, production, rights, distribution, and audience engagement to advertising, monetization, and measurement - with the ability to translate that knowledge into credible AI-led customer scenarios.
  • Experience with establishing C-suite and business-unit relationships at strategic Media & Entertainment customers, with a proven ability to engage and influence senior decision-makers.
  • Recognized industry thought leadership and a strong personal brand in the Media & Entertainment market.
  • Broad media value-chain fluency and experience with AI translation skills, able to engage across studios, broadcasters, publishers, streamers, sports, advertising, and agencies without being limited to one sub-sector; understands how AI can reshape creative workflows, production operations, distribution, monetization, audience engagement, and business models.
  • 12+ years of Media & Entertainment industry or industry-consulting experience with increasing scope and influence.
  • Proven success driving complex, enterprise-scale digital transformation initiatives.
  • 5+ years of leadership or influence experience (formal or matrixed) guiding cross-functional teams.
  • Experienced in AI, data platforms, and cloud-based transformation, with the ability to translate them into industry outcomes.
  • Track record of partner-ecosystem development, cross-regional collaboration, and building strategic narratives that drive consensus across complex organizations.

As an Applied Science PhD Intern at Microsoft, you will be at the forefront of technological innovation, working collaboratively to bring research to life in our products and services. You'll gain expertise in cutting-edge research areas, apply advanced concepts to real-world needs, and use state-of-the-art tools to make a tangible impact on product quality and business outcomes. You'll contribute to the creation of intelligent solutions through data analysis, modeling, machine learning, and/or AI, LLM, SLM and agent, ensuring our products remain at the leading edge of innovation.  

As an intern at Microsoft, you’re stepping into a world of real impact from day one. You’ll collaborate with global teams on meaningful projects, explore cutting-edge technologies like AI, and kick start your career while doing it. With a strong focus on learning and development, this is your opportunity to grow your skills, build community, and shape your future—all while being supported every step of the way.   

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate and empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

  • Analyze and improve performance of advanced algorithms on large-scale datasets and cutting-edge research in machine intelligence and machine learning applications. 

  • Think through the product scenarios and goals, identify key challenges, then fit the scenario asks into Machine Learning (ML) tasks, design experimental process for iteration and optimization. 

  • Implement prototypes of scalable systems in AI applications. 
    Gain an understanding of a broad area of research and applicable research techniques, as well as a basic knowledge of industry trends and share your knowledge with immediate team members. 

  • Prepare data to be used for analysis by reviewing criteria that reflect quality and technical constraints. Reviews data and suggests data to be included and excluded and be able to describe actions taken to address data quality problems. 

  • Assist with the development of usable datasets for modeling purposes and support the scaling of feature ideation and data preparation. 

  • Help take cleaned data and adapt for machine learning purposes, under the direction of a senior team member

  • Currently pursuing a Doctorate Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field.

  • Must have at least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internship.

Overview

Microsoft Cloud Operations and Innovation (CO+I) underpins Microsoft’s global cloud infrastructure, driving the innovation, planning, design, construction, and operation of one of the largest data center fleets in the world. We are seeking an exceptional Principal Applied Scientist to join the Data Center Applied AI team. In this role, you will play a pivotal role in advancing and integrating cutting‑edge, multimodal agentic AI systems into core tools and operational workflows that power Microsoft’s data centers. Your work will drive operational efficiency at scale and help advance Microsoft’s mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more through intelligent, multimodal AI agents.

As a Principal Applied Scientistt, you will bridge state‑of‑the‑art AI research with production‑grade engineering, delivering agent architectures that are reliable, secure, scalable, observable, and measurable. You will collaborate closely with Business and Engineering to build and deploy agentic capabilities across workflow automation, information retrieval, retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG), tool and function calling, long‑horizon task execution, and multi‑agent orchestration.

This role blends deep AI and applied science expertise with strong engineering judgment, operational rigor, and a bias for action. Success requires end‑to‑end ownership, a growth mindset, and strong customer empathy. Join us to shape the future of agentic AI for data center operations at global scale.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We work with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize shared goals—guided by our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to foster an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.



Responsibilities
  • Advance Applied AI Research to Improve Quality and Reliability
    • Apply deep expertise in Generative AI, deep learning, NLP, and multimodal models to translate cutting-edge research into high-impact, production-ready AI solutions.
    • Design and execute experiments that measurably improve agent planning, memory, grounding, reasoning, and long‑horizon task completion.
    • Perform lightweight fine‑tuning (e.g., LoRA and related techniques) on multimodal and large multimodal language models—to improve entity recognition, reasoning accuracy, and response quality.
    • Implement state‑of‑the‑art approaches using foundation models, advanced prompt engineering, RAG, knowledge graphs, and multi‑agent architectures, complemented by classical ML techniques where appropriate.
  • Build and Ship Scalable Agentic AI Systems
    • Architect and implement end‑to‑end agent workflows that decompose user intent into executable plans, intelligently select and invoke tools, and recover gracefully from errors and edge cases.
    • Rapidly prototype solutions and partner with engineering teams to drive production deployment, including debugging live systems and building AIOps workflows.
    • Use data and telemetry to identify AI quality gaps, generate insights, and deliver proofs of concept that apply research innovations to real‑world operational challenges.
    • Design robust multi‑step reasoning and tool‑use strategies, including function calling, code execution, APIs, and secure connectors, with strong safety and reliability guardrails.
    • Drive production excellence across latency, reliability, cost efficiency, observability, monitoring, and safe fallback behaviors.
  • Own Evaluation, Metrics, and Iteration Loops
    • Define task‑level evaluation metrics for agentic behavior, including success rate, tool‑call accuracy, step efficiency, hallucination rate, safety violations, time‑to‑completion, and user satisfaction.
    • Build and maintain offline and online evaluation pipelines, including:
      • Golden datasets, scenario simulators, and regression test suites
      • Human‑in‑the‑loop evaluation frameworks and rubric design
      • A/B experimentation and telemetry‑driven iteration loops
  • Collaborate Across Disciplines and Lead Technical Execution
    • Partner with business and engineering stakeholders to translate requirements into clear technical specifications, research plans, and delivery milestones.
    • Lead design reviews and influence engineering decisions across agent frameworks, model integration, and system architecture.
    • Mentor and support other applied scientists and engineers, raising the bar for applied AI execution and production quality

    • OR Doctorate in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
    • OR equivalent experience

  • PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, NLP, or related field,OR MS with significant experience delivering production‑grade AI systems.
  • 10+ years of hands‑on experience applying NLP, and/or LLMs to real‑world production problems.
  • Strong foundation in Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, deep learning, and modern NLP.

  • Experience with parameter‑efficient fine‑tuning techniques (e.g., LoRA) for LLMs or multimodal models.
  • Hands‑on experience building agentic or tool‑augmented LLM systems, including function calling, planners, and API/tool integration.
  • Experience with advanced RAG architectures, such as hybrid retrieval, reranking, grounding, and citation strategies.
  • Strong AIOps depth, including quality drift detection, alerting, rollback, and telemetry‑driven optimization.
  • Experience optimizing systems for latency, reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency at enterprise scale.
  • Prior experience working on mission‑critical or large‑scale enterprise AI systems.
  • Demonstrated mentorship or technical leadership within applied science or engineering teams.

Microsoft’s Azure Data engineering team is leading the transformation of analytics in the world of data with products like databases, data integration, big data analytics, messaging & real-time analytics, and business intelligence. Join us to make powerful data experiences feel intuitive, trustworthy, and connected, while helping shape what’s next for AI-powered design.  

​We do not just value differences or different perspectives. We seek them out and invite them in so we can tap into the collective power of everyone in the company. As a result, our customers are better served.

As a Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work non-rotational 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.



Responsibilities

Critical Environment Culture

  • Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.

Equipment and Systems Maintenance

  • Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
  • Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
  • Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
  • Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
  • Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.

Equipment and Systems Operations

  • Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
  • Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
  • Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
  • Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.

Physical Requirements (Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles)

  • Occasional climbing of ladders.
  • Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps.
  • Prolonged standing.
  • Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg.
  • Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device.
  • Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
  • Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

Working Conditions

  • Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
  • As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
  • As indicated above, have the ability to work non-rotational 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays. 

Other

  • Embodies our culture and values.

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.  
  • 1+ year(s) mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience. 

Other Requirements

This role requires the ability to meet Microsoft, customer, and/or government security screening requirements. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

Overview

Artificial intelligence is driving fundamental changes in the scale and architecture of cloud infrastructure. Networks must grow faster and carry substantially more capacity while becoming simpler to deploy, easier to automate and more resilient to failure. Meeting those requirements means reconsidering how routing, optics, network hardware and software come together as a system.


Azure Global Networking designs, builds, operates and evolves the network that connects Microsoft's datacenters to each other and to the world. You will join a team working on the next generation of that infrastructure, where packet and optical networking, hardware and software disaggregation, automation and new approaches to physical network engineering are increasingly converging.

As a Principal Cloud Network Engineer, you will drive the creation and adoption of technologies, protocols and solutions that define reliable, secure, scalable, cost-effective and high-performance network architectures. You will work across organizations to solve ambiguous, multi-layer engineering problems and influence architectural decisions spanning network topology, routing, hardware, optics, automation, telemetry and operations.

You will help develop architectures that make capacity easier to introduce while reducing shared dependencies and containing failures within clearly defined failure domains. You will take ideas from architectural principles and experimentation through engineering validation, production deployment and operational learning, maintaining accountability for how those designs behave in the live network.

This opportunity will allow you to shape hyperscale network architecture for artificial intelligence-driven infrastructure, work deeply across Software for Open Networking in the Cloud (SONiC), merchant-silicon hardware, disaggregated networking, optical technologies including Optical Circuit Switching (OCS), and advance automation and artificial intelligence-assisted network engineering. You will provide technical leadership across teams while remaining directly connected to the production network and the engineering challenges that emerge at global scale.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Drive the creation and adoption of technologies, protocols and solutions that define reliable, secure, scalable, cost-effective and high-performance large-scale network architectures and designs.
  • Work across multiple teams and organizations to develop network architectures, lead architecture and design reviews, and drive technical decisions across functionality, performance, scale, reliability, operations, security and cost.
  • Develop and drive new approaches that address fundamental weaknesses in network architecture, processes, tooling and engineering capabilities before they result in customer or business impact, using automation and infrastructure as code to enable improvements at scale.
  • Provide end-to-end technical leadership across packet and optical networking, hardware, device operating systems, telemetry and automation, while influencing internal engineering teams, technology suppliers and other partners.
  • Design and advance automated network testing, validation, telemetry and analytics that identify failures and regressions earlier, improve troubleshooting at scale and explore the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to network operations.
  • Lead the diagnosis and root-cause analysis of complex, multi-layer live-site issues, use production and telemetry data to identify systemic problems, and translate those learnings into durable improvements in network architecture, automation and engineering practices.
  • Participate in and lead on-call duties for production incidents, provide technical leadership through complex incidents, and mentor and coach engineers in network architecture, engineering, DevOps and live-site practices. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Doctorate Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design, development, and automation
    • OR Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design, development, and automation
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design, development, and automation 
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Advanced technical experience defining, designing, developing or operating large-scale network architectures and taking major network solutions from architecture through validation and production deployment.
  • Experience with Software-Defined Networking (SDN), controller-based networking or centrally orchestrated traffic-engineering systems, including the programming and operation of network forwarding paths, tunnels or routing state.
  • Deep experience with network architecture and routing technologies, including Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), Intermediate System to Intermediate System (IS-IS), Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS), Segment Routing or comparable large-scale routing and traffic-engineering technologies.
  • Experience designing for the interaction between centralized network control and distributed router control planes, including convergence, fallback routing, failure handling, state consistency and failure-domain isolation.
  • Experience developing or influencing network automation, infrastructure as code, telemetry, testing or validation systems used to safely deploy and operate network infrastructure at scale.
  • Experience providing technical leadership during complex, multi-layer production incidents and translating operational findings into durable improvements in architecture, software, hardware, automation or engineering standards. 

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role.
  • These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: 
    • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctorate Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design, development, and automation
    • OR Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design, development, and automation
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design, development, and automation
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Experience delivering network designs into production and experience with live site accountability for a network.
  • Experience developing quality management programs.
  • Experience applying AI agent based systems to network engineering or operations, such as detecting anomalies, diagnosing complex failures, analyzing telemetry, identifying systemic design or operational weaknesses, validating network behavior, or developing automated remediation approaches.
  • Experience delivering large-scale network architectures into production with live-site accountability and technical leadership for complex production networks.
  • Demonstrated ability to research and evaluate emerging networking, hardware, software and Artificial Intelligence technologies and translate relevant innovations into practical architectural or operational improvements

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Sales Excellence Transformation & Change Leadership

AI-Enabled Insights & Analytics

Overview

Air Gapped Cloud (AGC) | Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I)

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) is the team that builds and operates the global datacenter infrastructure that powers Microsoft’s cloud services. Within CO+I, Air Gapped Cloud (AGC) extends these capabilities to highly secure, specialized environments, aligning strategy, delivery, and operations to meet mission-critical customer requirements.

 

Role Summary

The AGC Senior Business Manager serves as an operational integrator across CO+I AGC, connecting leaders, teams, priorities, and operating mechanisms so the organization functions as one system. This role provides horizontal support across Strategy & Planning, Delivery & Execution, and DC Operations teams, closes functional gaps, improves handoffs, and keeps decisions connected to execution.

 

This role builds and sustains the organization’s operating model through Rhythm of Business (ROB), governance, performance reporting, budgeting, workforce planning, executive communications, and business data management. The Senior Business Manager applies systems thinking to anticipate downstream impacts, resolve friction across organizational boundaries, and design scalable mechanisms that improve end-to-end performance. A successful candidate in this role sets a high bar for first-pass quality and ensures analyses, reports, communications, and decision materials are accurate, complete, and leadership-ready before review.



Responsibilities

Business Operations & Governance

  • Owns and continuously improves the AGC Rhythm of Business, including leadership, business, finance, staffing, town halls, and planning forums.
  • Establishes governance, reporting, decision, and information-management standards that enable consistent execution across the organization.
  • Drives discipline through action tracking, escalation management, leadership follow-up, and closure of cross-team dependencies.
  • Coordinates organization-wide priorities and operating dependencies so commitments remain connected from decision through delivery.

Strategic Planning & Organizational Effectiveness

  • Partners with AGC leadership to translate strategy into organizational priorities, operating plans, staffing models, goals, and measurable outcomes.
  • Identifies downstream impacts, cross-functional dependencies, weak handoffs, and organizational risks.
  • Mobilizes accountable owners to resolve gaps, simplify processes, and implement scalable improvements across construction, operations, supply chain, engineering, cost management, and business strategy.

Performance Management & Reporting

  • Owns executive reporting, performance reviews, KPIs, scorecards, dashboards, and business intelligence processes.
  • Maintains a reliable single source of truth by consolidating organizational data and ensuring metrics are accurate, timely, consistent, and decision ready.
  • Sets and models high standards for analyses, reports, and leadership materials, reducing rework and accelerating decisions.

Financial & Resource Management

  • Leads budget planning, forecasting, submissions, variance analysis, and financial reporting across discretionary, vendor, morale, and operational spend.
  • Partners with Finance to align spending and resource allocation with organizational priorities.
  • Supports vendor and contract planning and develops business cases for headcount, vendor support, and strategic investments.

Workforce Planning & Organizational Management

  • Leads headcount governance, workforce planning, hiring prioritization, staffing reviews, and onboarding coordination.
  • Maintains organizational health metrics, role architecture, title hygiene, and workforce data integrity.
  • Partners with HR, Recruiting, and leadership to support organizational growth and talent priorities.

Executive Communications & Engagement

  • Develops leadership communications, executive presentations, briefing materials, strategic narratives, Town Halls, newsletters, and organizational updates.
  • Manages stakeholder communication across organizational levels and ensures messages are clear, consistent, and action-oriented.
  • Supports employee engagement, onboarding, and culture initiatives.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serves as the operational integrator across AGC and partner teams and creates continuity where ownership, processes, or handoffs span functions.
  • Translates shared priorities into coordinated plans, clear ownership, decision paths, and sustained follow-through.
  • Anticipates support needs, engages the right leaders and resources, and prevents critical work from falling between organizational boundaries.
  • Leads cross-functional initiatives that improve performance, operating maturity, resilience, and scalability.
 

Accountability

The Senior Business Manager is accountable for:

  • Effectiveness and continuity of organization-wide operating rhythms, governance, and cross-functional execution
  • Quality, accuracy, timeliness, and decision usefulness of executive reporting and communications
  • Closure of organizational gaps, dependencies, actions, escalations, and risks
  • Alignment of budgets, workforce plans, and resources to strategic priorities
  • Reliable business and workforce data, standardized processes, and scalable operating mechanisms
 

Authority

  • Establish and standardize governance, planning, reporting, communication, and information-management requirements.
  • Require timely participation and complete, accurate inputs from contributors to organizational operating processes.
  • Escalate operational risks, misalignments, quality issues, and blockers to leadership.
  • Recommend resource allocation, staffing priorities, and process improvements.
  • Drive alignment across business functions and leadership teams.

The CSAM is an early-in-career Customer Success Account Manager who delivers standardized customer success outcomes spanning executive partnership, solution health, cloud adoption, and AI acceleration activities. These CSAMs act within a pod model.

Working under the direction of senior CSAMs and a Manager, the CSAM operates within a defined pod covering a shared portfolio of accounts. The role contributes to portfolio-level intelligence, execution orchestration, and reactive signal aggregation – reducing context-switching for senior CSAMs and accelerating customer outcomes.

This is a talent-engine role: CSAMs are AI-first, customer-facing from month three, and grow through structured cohorts and community.



Responsibilities

Executive partnership and execution

  • Execute standardized executive partnership, solution health, cloud adoption, and AI acceleration tasks under direct guidance from senior CSAMs or CSU leaders.
  • Support agent and Copilot adoption motions across assigned pod accounts.
  • Complete assigned activities accurately and on time; escalate exceptions rather than independently diagnose them.

Portfolio-level intelligence and preparation

  • Maintain deep, current account context across the pod’s defined portfolio.
  • Synthesize account signals into “what’s changed / what matters now”
  • Detect risks, upcoming deliveries, upcoming milestones, and open threads.
  • Detect portfolio patterns such as recurring blockers across multiple accounts.

Execution orchestration (not delivery)

  • Track delivery and milestone progress with partners and CSAs on behalf of senior CSAMs.
  • Map dependencies across workloads and milestones.
  • Proactively flag drift before the customer raises it.
  • Coordinate remediation follow-ups across internal teams.

Reactive signal aggregation

  • Monitor reactive support signals – case volume, aging, repeat drivers – across the pod portfolio.
  • Aggregate reactive trends into portfolio-level views and surface early warnings of escalation risk.
  • Track follow-through on Support, IM, and Service Manager commitments; chase stalled internal owners.
  • Distill reactive noise into CSAM-ready insights, not raw data.

Operating model

  • Operate within a pod model covering a shared portfolio of accounts.
  • Work under direct oversight of the Manager and senior CSAMs assigned to the pod.
  • Limit interactions to task execution and information capture; executive partnership and account governance is led by the senior CSAM.

Example Activities

Activities below are illustrative, not exhaustive. The same executive priorities apply because the role is still a CSAM.

Strengthen Customer Health

  • Maintain running summaries of reactive health per account for CSAM pre-briefs.
  • Surface repeat incident patterns and systemic drivers.
  • Translate reactive trends into Customer Health Recommendation inputs.
  • Flag candidates for proactive Success Programs and remediation focus.

Accelerate Cloud Adoption

  • Track deliveries that support adoption milestones and usage signals across pod accounts.
  • Coordinate with delivery partners and CSAs on adoption commitments.
  • Prepare adoption inputs for CSDRs and executive discussions.

Advance AI Transformation

  • Monitor agent and Copilot adoption velocity across the pod.
  • Aggregate AI transformation blockers and opportunities into portfolio views.
  • Support readiness for AI-related Success Program intake.

Earn Customer Trust Every Day (Executive Partnership & Planning)

  • Reduce CSAM context-switching by owning “what needs attention this week” across pod accounts.
  • Drive follow-up actions after reports, reviews, and assessments.
  • Keep execution honest on dates, owners, and readiness.

Overview 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. With a growth mindset at our core, we keep learning, make decisions starting from what matters most to our customers, and pursue excellence—creating innovative technology that impacts people around the world. 

Account Management provides proposals and guidance on services and solutions, and acts as the hub that connects internal and external resources to orchestrate collaboration. Through creating new opportunities and driving demand generation, we expand market share and accelerate digital transformation by translating industry and business scenarios into Microsoft solutions. In long-term relationships with assigned customers, we lead executive-level dialogues as a trusted advisor to CxO-level technical and business decision-makers, articulating strategic value. We also gather customer insights and, leveraging established architecture approaches, clarify the path and required resources to deliver on agreed commitments. 

 

 

Enterprise Commercial Organization 

The Enterprise Commercial organization partners mid- to long-term with enterprise customers—including our most strategic accounts—to lead business growth and transformation. This position sits within the Industrial & Manufacturing business group and will be responsible for 2–4 major customers in the discrete manufacturing segment. You will engage directly with customer executives such as the CEO/CIO/CTO/BDM to address global and enterprise-wide management and business challenges, and drive everything from shaping a transformation roadmap using Microsoft technology to proposing and executing it. By collaborating with internal specialist teams and partners, you will influence decision-making in large-scale accounts and lead transformations that create meaningful impact on industry and society—one of the key attractions of this role.

Responsibilities 

To drive growth in assigned accounts and deliver customer business outcomes, you will lead internal and external stakeholders and consistently execute end-to-end account leadership—from building and running account plans, to executive relationship development, to demand generation through closing. 

  

Account Management 

  • Develop and execute the account plan for assigned accounts, leading delivery against revenue and Consumption targets as well as customer business outcomes. 

  • Prioritize across multiple accounts based on customer needs, revenue impact, growth opportunities, and account risks, adjusting plans and resource allocation as conditions change. 

  • Create mid- to long-term business plans based on industry and business scenarios, and drive strategic account growth by engaging internal and external decision-makers, partners, and senior leaders. 

  • Expand networks with key partners and, in collaboration with partner sales, accelerate demand generation and deal closing. 

  

Customer Engagement 

  • Build trusted relationships with executives and business/IT decision-makers, including CxO, and make the value and ROI of Microsoft solutions visible based on customer challenges. 

  • Deeply understand the customer’s business strategy, technology challenges, and priorities, and design and present insight-driven proposals. 

  

Sales Excellence 

  • Lead virtual teams and establish proposal and execution governance aligned to customer requirements to drive opportunities forward. 

  • Against KPI and Success Measures agreed with the customer and internally, visualize daily/weekly/monthly progress and manage through issue identification and execution of actions. 

  • Continuously review the pipeline, set priorities and next actions, improve forecast accuracy, and drive execution through to closing. 

  

Industry Knowledge 

  • Continuously update knowledge of Microsoft technology (products, cloud services, solutions, and roadmaps) and apply it to deliver the best proposals for customer challenges. 

  • Understand the manufacturing industry—especially assembly manufacturing—including industry structure, value chains, key trends/regulatory developments, and typical management and frontline challenges, and lead definition, proposal, and execution of mid- to long-term transformation themes.

Preferred Qualifications

This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of law, technology and some of the Middle East’s most ambitious digital transformation programmes. We have an immediate opening for a highly motivated and experienced lawyer to join the Middle East Legal Affairs team within Corporate, External and Legal Affairs (CELA). The position is based in Riyadh and will report to the Head of Legal Affairs for the Middle East.

This individual will serve as the lead Legal Affairs lawyer for Saudi Arabia and potentially other countries in the Middle East, contributing to the development and execution of Microsoft’s legal strategy across these markets. This role supports some of Microsoft’s most important Middle East markets and helps shape and execute strategic business priorities. The lawyer will advise on complex commercial and regulatory matters, review new business models, support strategic public sector transactions, and remove legal blockers to the responsible adoption and consumption of Microsoft’s Cloud and AI services.

The role requires close collaboration with Microsoft executives, sales and technical teams, legal peers, external partners, customers, regulators, and regional and global CELA teams. The Windows + Devices Fundamentals team improves the reliability, performance, responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and overall health of Windows devices. We build and operate the services, telemetry systems, and data pipelines that transform signals from labs and the installed base into trustworthy metrics, actionable diagnostics, and measurable engineering improvements.

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineering Manager to define strategy and lead an engineering organization responsible for critical Windows Fundamentals data and service capabilities. You will shape architecture and investment across backend services, telemetry platforms, data pipelines, metrics, and diagnostic workflows; grow senior technical and management talent; and drive coordinated execution that improves Windows health at scale.

This role is ideal for an experienced engineering leader who combines deep service and data-platform expertise with solid product judgment, organizational leadership, and a track record of aligning teams to solve complex technical and business problems.

The team combines fraud risk decisioning, operational controls, data-driven insights, and customer remediation to manage emerging payment risks while maintaining a secure and trusted customer experience. 

We are looking for a  Risk Manager, Payment Fraud Operations, based in Redmond, to lead fraud risk management and operational strategy across complex payment and customer scenarios. This role is responsible for identifying and analyzing fraudulent transaction and usage patterns, making risk-based accept/reject decisions, improving fraud prevention controls, and providing robust feedback loops to payment risk models, policies, and detection strategies. 

The role requires strong risk management expertise, sound judgment, analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across Operations, Engineering, Data Science, Customer Support, and other business teams.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We foster a culture of growth, innovation, collaboration, respect, integrity, and accountability where everyone can thrive.

Fraud Risk Decisioning

  • Identify emerging fraud patterns and root causes using transaction and usage data, translating insights into improved automated treatment strategies.  

Customer Remediation: 

  • Partner with Customer Support to resolve complex escalations and improve customer remediation strategies. 

  • Support incident management, root-cause analysis, and remediation for payment-fraud issues. 

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence: 

  • Identify and lead opportunities to streamline operations, reduce manual effort and rework, improve workflows and tooling, and increase efficiency without compromising fraud risk controls or decision quality.  

Risk Model & Control Feedback: 

  • Provide high-quality decisioning, fraud labels and investigation insights to support risk model refinement, policy improvements, and preventative controls.  

  • Deep dive into quality gaps, identify root causes, and implement improvement strategies and preventative controls to reduce recurrence and strengthen risk outcomes. 

Operations OKR Performance Management:  

  • Monitor and improve key metrics including accuracy, false positive/negative outcomes, decision time, productivity, and customer impact.  

Operations Strategy & Process Improvement:  

  • Develop preventative measures, process enhancements, and scalable solutions to address emerging risks and operational gaps.  

Stakeholder Collaboration & Communication:  

  • Partner with Engineering, Data Science, Customer Support, and Operations to drive root-cause analysis and implement risk solutions.  

  • Act as the primary Redmond payment-fraud point of contact for Engineering and Customer Support teams. 

Risk Governance & Communication:  

  • Communicate fraud trends, quality insights, process changes, and risk concerns to stakeholders and senior leaders.  

Capability Development:  

  • Develop guidelines, documentation, and training and support adoption of new tools, processes, investigation guidelines and controls.

The Copilot Security Engineering team sits at the core of Microsoft’s mission to deliver secure, trusted, and human-centered AI experiences across Microsoft’s Copilot offerings. We build the systems that detect, evaluate, and defend against emerging AI threats, including prompt injection, memory poisoning, data exfiltration, adversarial inputs, and abuse of agentic workflows. Our goal is to establish industry-leading security protections that enable customers to confidently adopt AI at scale.

 

Our team combines security engineering, AI systems expertise, and threat research to identify emerging risks, develop novel defenses, and continuously measure their effectiveness in production. You will turn ambiguous, evolving threats into an actionable engineering strategy and reusable platform protections, aligning partners on priorities, interfaces, and measurable security outcomes.

 

This is a hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of security, AI, and large-scale distributed systems. You will design and write production code, lead complex work from threat discovery through deployment and operation, and remain accountable for the effectiveness and reliability of the defenses you deliver. Your impact will extend through cross-team architectural decisions, partner influence, and mentorship, rather than people management.

We are seeking a Principal Optical Engineer to drive the architectural design, production roadmap, engineering efforts for next-generation optical interconnects in hyperscale AI infrastructure. 

This role will serve as an architect/engineer responsible for Cloud/AI optical interconnects, and rack-scale fiber management. The candidate will work across silicon, systems, networking, platform architecture, datacenter engineering, and external ecosystem partners to bring innovative optical technologies from concept through large-scale production deployment. 

The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in optical systems with architecture, ecosystem, and execution skills, and can influence platform-level decisions across multiple generations of AI infrastructure.

Responsibilities

This individual will serve as a technical leader for near-package optics (NPO), co-packaged optics (CPO), silicon photonics, and advanced packaging. The role will define multi-generation architectures and guide technologies from early feasibility through qualification, manufacturing ramp, and deployment in hyperscale AI systems. 

  • Own the end-to-end architecture and multi-generation roadmap for NPO and CPO optical interconnects used in AI scale-up networks. 

  • Translate system and network requirements into specifications for bandwidth density, reach, latency, energy per bit, optical-link budget, signal integrity, thermal limits, reliability, serviceability, manufacturability, and cost. 

  • Define silicon-photonic subsystem architectures, including optical engines, modulators, photodetectors, laser-source strategies, coupling interfaces, fiber attach, electronic-photonic integration, and control and monitoring functions. 

  • Build system models and budgets that connect photonic-device performance, SerDes and electrical channels, package parasitics, thermal behavior, controls, and network-level performance. 

  • Provide hands-on technical leadership in laboratory characterization and debug, including optical and electrical measurements, link bring-up, design-of-experiments, margin analysis, failure analysis, and correlation of simulation with measured data. 

  • Define verification, qualification, reliability, and manufacturing-test strategies at wafer, die, package, module, board, rack, and system levels 

  • Guide proof-of-concept designs through product definition, design reviews, qualification, manufacturing readiness, supply-chain ramp, and fleet deployment; lead root-cause and corrective-action efforts when issues arise. 

  • Drive technical alignment across silicon, packaging, signal integrity, thermal, mechanical, firmware, networking, manufacturing, and reliability teams. 

  • Set technical direction with foundries, OSATs, component suppliers, equipment vendors, and strategic partners; assess technology readiness, supply continuity, cost, yield, and roadmap alignment.

This role sits within Global EHS Engineering, Strategy & Standards (ESS) organization and partners closely with EHS program owners, regional EHS teams, and Datacenter Engineering and Operations to enable a safe and healthy working environment across Microsoft’s global datacenter portfolio. The successful candidate will identify hazards, analyze consequences and risks, and recommend practical, engineering‑based controls to mitigate risk in alignment with Microsoft standards and regulatory requirements, supporting the safe delivery of Microsoft infrastructure technologies worldwide. This is an individual contributor (IC4) role requiring strong technical judgment, cross‑functional collaboration, and program execution skills.

This role is available to candidates anywhere within the US. Successful candidates who live within 50 miles of a Microsoft hub will be required to work from the office a minimum of 3 days per week.  Hub locations - Redmond, WA, Atlanta, GA, San Antonio, TX, Phoenix, AZ, or Washington DC.

  • Analyze EHS performance metrics and indicators to identify trends, prioritize risk‑reduction opportunities, and inform program improvements.
  • Conduct inspections, assessments, and design reviews to verify compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and Microsoft policies.
  • Perform workplace risk and exposure assessments across electrical, mechanical, and operational hazard categories.

  • Embody our culture and values.

Principal Product Manager for Memory in Copilot Chat, owning customer scenarios, end-to-end product experiences, platform requirements, and AI quality/evaluation across a high-impact, cross-company area. 

Microsoft Copilot is transforming how people work by helping them reason across information, stay in context, and accomplish more. Copilot Memory is a foundational part of that experience: it enables Copilot Chat to understand durable user context and deliver more personal, proactive, and trustworthy assistance while preserving enterprise-grade controls. 

The Copilot Work Memory team is evolving memory from user's work context & history continuity into a governed, evaluable, multi-source capability grounded in user's real communications, documents, meetings and work content. The team is solving hard product and technical problems across memory generation, freshness, retrieval, serving, evaluation, transparency, safety, privacy, latency, and cost. 

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager, to lead a large, complex product area for Memory in Copilot Chat. This role requires exceptional technical fluency, end-to-end product judgment, and a proven ability to build and ship AI-powered experiences from the ground up. You will set direction across customer scenarios, product experiences, platform capabilities, and AI quality; translate ambiguous customer and technical problems into a durable strategy and execution plan; and align engineering, applied science, design, research, security, privacy, and partner teams across Microsoft to deliver measurable customer impact. You will also establish and sustain senior cross-organization relationships with teams driving critical parts of Copilot Memory, including Chat Memory. 

The ideal candidate combines customer obsession with systems thinking and organizational leadership: someone who can move comfortably from long-term product strategy and user scenarios to quality metrics, experiment design, platform tradeoffs, and executive-level decisions. You will operate with high autonomy, lead through ambiguity across a broad scope, create clarity across organizational boundaries, and establish the product practices and cross-company operating model that allow Copilot Memory to improve safely and rapidly at scale.

Key responsibilities include: 

  • Design, develop, and validate software solutions that support silicon bring-up, platform enablement, and feature readiness across emerging hardware platforms.
