Overview
Azure is a $100B business growing at more than 40% year over year at Microsoft — and application modernization is one of the largest driver of that growth. Customers are no longer asking whether to move to the cloud; they are asking which Azure destination is right for each application, and how fast they can get there. That decision is where you come in.
Are you curious, passionate about infrastructure and applications, and ready to solve complex modernization challenges in the AI era? Join us as a Digital Solution Engineer – Azure Platform, supporting mid-market customers across the Azure application and data platform.
In this technical sales role, you will help customers move beyond lift-and-shift and re-platform their application estate onto the best-fit Azure destination — Azure App Service, Azure Container Apps, or Azure Kubernetes Service — backed by the right data platform, whether that is Azure SQL or an open-source engine such as PostgreSQL or MySQL. You will translate architectural choices into business outcomes: lower run cost, faster release cadence, stronger security posture, and an application estate that is ready for AI.
About SME&C
At Small, Medium Enterprises and Channel (SME&C), we are leading a high-growth, AI-powered global sales team — one that is deeply connected to our partners and driven by customer success. By uniting our Small Medium Business, Corporate, Strategy, and Partner teams, we are unlocking the largest customer opportunity, backed by the industry’s most significant investments. Leveraging the power of AI and our extensive partner ecosystem, we are redefining how businesses of all sizes adopt technology to drive growth and innovation.
SME&C is more than a sales organization — it’s a culture of innovation, opportunity, and inclusivity. Here, you’ll be part of a diverse, high-performing, and customer-obsessed team where collaboration, connection, and continuous learning fuel everything we do. If you thrive in a fast-paced, digital-first environment and are eager to make a meaningful impact, explore how SME&C can be the next step in your career.
The Core of the Role: Driving Application Modernization
The defining capability of this role is your ability to take a customer’s existing application portfolio and drive it to the most appropriate Azure destination — on both the application and the data tier. This is a judgment-led discipline, not a template. You are expected to assess each workload on its operational model, scale profile, cost envelope, compliance constraints, and the customer’s developer velocity, then recommend and defend the right landing zone.
Application platform destinations
You are fluent across the full Azure application platform and can articulate — with credibility, in front of architects — when to choose each:
  • Azure App Service — for web apps and APIs that benefit from a fully managed PaaS runtime with minimal operational overhead; the fastest path off Windows/IIS and Java/Tomcat estates.
  • Azure Container Apps — for containerized microservices, event-driven workloads, and scale-to-zero scenarios where teams want containers without owning a cluster.
  • Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) — for complex, large-scale, or portability-driven estates that require full orchestration control, custom networking, and platform-engineering maturity.
  • Azure Functions, Azure Arc, and Azure VMs — as complementary destinations for event-driven code, hybrid and edge estates, and workloads that are expected to remain IaaS in the near term.
Critically, you can explain the trade-offs between these destinations rather than defaulting to one — including the cost, operational, and skills implications of each choice, and the containerization and refactoring path required to get there.
Data platform destinations
Modernizing the application without modernizing the data tier leaves most of the value on the table. You bring equal depth across the Azure database estate:
  • Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance — for modernizing SQL Server estates to PaaS, including compatibility assessment, Hyperscale, and Business Critical tiering.
  • SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines — where full instance control or third-party dependencies require IaaS, with a defined path to PaaS over time.
  • Azure Database for PostgreSQL (Flexible Server) — including Oracle-to-PostgreSQL modernization and PostgreSQL as the default open-source landing zone for new and refactored applications.
  • Azure Database for MySQL (Flexible Server) — for LAMP-stack and ISV application estates moving off self-managed MySQL or MariaDB.
  • Azure Cosmos DB — including the MongoDB (vCore) and PostgreSQL APIs, for globally distributed, high-throughput, and NoSQL workloads.
You are comfortable leading open-source database conversations on their own merits — licensing economics, extension compatibility, high availability, and migration tooling — and can run an Oracle, MongoDB, or self-managed PostgreSQL/MySQL modernization conversation end to end.
Modernization method
  • Lead portfolio-level assessment and apply the 6R framework (rehost, replatform, refactor, rearchitect, rebuild, replace) to segment an estate and sequence the work.
  • Apply containerization and refactoring leading practices, and use AI and intelligent agents to accelerate legacy code assessment, dependency mapping, and transformation.
  • Design the surrounding architecture — hybrid and cloud-native networking, virtual networks, private connectivity, secure routing, identity, and landing-zone design — so modernized applications meet enterprise performance and compliance requirements.
  • Complement Microsoft technology with trusted partner solutions such as NetApp, VMware, Red Hat, and SAP to deliver a secure, optimized, and scalable migration experience.
  • Ground every recommendation in Azure security services and compliance frameworks, so customers meet regulatory requirements and build a cloud estate that is ready for what comes next.
This Opportunity Will Allow You To
  • Accelerate your career growth by leading the modernization engagements that sit at the centre of a $100M, +40% YoY growth business.
  • Deepen your technical proficiency through hands-on architecture design, application and database migration planning, and implementation of hybrid and cloud-native environments.
  • Develop strategic influence by shaping the destination decisions — App Service, Container Apps, AKS, Azure SQL, or open-source databases — that determine a customer’s cost base and agility for years.
  • Strengthen your collaboration skills by working closely with engineering teams, partners, and customer stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.
  • Build future-ready capabilities through continuous learning, industry-recognized certifications, and exposure to Microsoft’s evolving application, data, security, and AI platform.
 


Responsibilities
  • Drive technical sales using architecture design sessions, technical demos, proofs of concept, and modernization accelerators to influence solution design and unblock deployment.
  • Own the destination recommendation — assess customer application portfolios and recommend the best-fit Azure application and data platform target, with a defensible rationale on cost, scale, operations, and developer velocity.
  • Lead application modernization workshops and migration assessments spanning App Service, Container Apps, AKS, Azure SQL, and open-source database options.
  • Build trusted relationships with platform leads, application owners, and data teams to co-design secure, scalable, and cost-efficient solutions.
  • Resolve technical blockers by collaborating with engineering, partners, and product teams, and channel customer insight back into the product.
  • Maintain deep expertise across cloud migration and modernization — Windows, Linux, .NET, Java, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and containerized workloads — alongside resiliency, security, and compliance.
  • Deepen knowledge of enterprise applications (SAP, Oracle) and Azure VMware Solution (AVS) as adjacent modernization paths.
  • Represent Microsoft in customer forums and technical communities through thought leadership on application and data modernization.


Qualifications
• Extensive technical pre-sales or technical consulting experience
• OR Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND demonstrated technical pre-sales or technical consulting experience
• OR Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND demonstrated technical pre-sales or technical consulting experience
• OR equivalent experience
• Proven experience driving application modernization to cloud platforms, including migration and replatforming of workloads such as Windows, Linux, .NET, Java, SQL Server, and PostgreSQL.
• Hands-on experience with managed application platforms and container services — Azure App Service, Azure Container Apps, and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) — and with containerization strategy.
• Demonstrated database modernization experience across both commercial and open-source engines (SQL Server / Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and NoSQL options).
• Experience designing or selling solutions involving hybrid networking, secure connectivity, or network performance optimization in enterprise environments.
• Advanced understanding of Azure services, including security, compliance, and hybrid cloud scenarios.
• Ability to engage both technical and business stakeholders to design and deploy scalable, secure cloud solutions.

The Azure Fiber team based in Romsey is globally recognised as the world leader in the development and manufacturing of HollowCore Fiber. The team continues to demonstrate new and innovative ways to disrupt the optical network while delivering world leading fiber performance. The ultimate purpose of the team is to reinvent the physical network so Azure can scale further, faster and more efficiently that ever before. We redefine the limits of fiber connectivity to power the next generation of Azure.

This role provides end-to-end technical and strategic leadership of the Azure Fiber technology portfolio, ensuring that fiber innovation is translated into scalable, deployable solutions that address Azure’s evolving network requirements. The role owns the integration of portfolio strategy, technology roadmaps, investment priorities, product requirements, engineering execution, industrialisation, supply readiness and deployment, creating a coherent path from emerging technology through to operation at Azure scale.

Working across Azure Fiber engineering, manufacturing, supply chain and network stakeholders, the role establishes portfolio priorities, resolves complex cross-functional trade-offs and drives decisions across multiple technologies, products and time horizons. The role uses deep engineering judgement and broad systems thinking to balance performance, cost, capacity, manufacturability, supply resilience, deployment readiness and long-term technology advantage.

As a technical leader, the role operates with significant autonomy and influence, shaping strategy beyond individual projects and creating the engineering frameworks, governance and decision mechanisms required to manage the Azure Fiber portfolio as an integrated system.
Ultimately, the role ensures Azure Fiber invests in and delivers the right fiber technologies, at the right maturity and scale, to remove physical network constraints and enable the future growth of Azure.

Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) is the organization that builds, operates, and continuously evolves the infrastructure behind the Microsoft Cloud, powering services used by more than 95% of Fortune 500 companies. CO+I is responsible for the full datacenter lifecycle from global planning and site acquisition through design, construction, deployment, operations, and eventual decommissioning, spanning 400+ datacenters across more than 70 Azure regions, connected by over 600,000 kilometers of fiber. As the engine that enables Microsoft’s cloud-first mission, CO+I delivers reliable, trusted, secure, and sustainable cloud and AI infrastructure, ensuring capacity is available on time, every time, to meet customer growth and support Microsoft’s broader mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more.
 
The Systems Engineering, Test, and Integration (SETI) team serves as Microsoft's technical proving ground for next-generation datacenter infrastructure. As a Datacenter Electrical Engineer in SETI, you will evaluate emerging power and electrical infrastructure technologies, determine whether they can meet Microsoft's requirements for reliability, scalability, and operational readiness, and help mature promising concepts into deployment-ready solutions. Projects may include medium-voltage architectures, HVDC distribution, power electronics, energy storage systems, advanced protection schemes, grid-interactive technologies, and other first-of-a-kind infrastructure innovations.
Success in this role requires more than technical analysis. You will be expected to define ambiguous problems, design and execute validation strategies, identify technical and operational risks, work directly with suppliers and internal engineering teams, and provide clear recommendations that influence Microsoft's long-term datacenter architecture. Our team is expected to develop evidence-based recommendations regarding technology readiness, deployment suitability, technical risks, and investment priorities. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on learning quickly, solving complex technical problems, and helping Microsoft make informed decisions about the future of datacenter infrastructure.
 
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Employees come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize shared goals. We build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive.

  • Evaluate, develop, and integrate next-generation electrical infrastructure technologies for Microsoft's datacenter portfolio.
  • Define system requirements, technical specifications, architectures, interfaces, and verification strategies for emerging power and infrastructure solutions.
  • Develop design documentation, engineering specifications, schematics, analysis, and technical recommendations that support technology maturation and deployment.
  • Create and execute test, validation, and verification plans to assess system performance, reliability, scalability, and operational readiness.
  • Perform technical due diligence on new technologies, supplier solutions, and industry developments to inform engineering and deployment decisions.
  • Analyze complex technical issues using modeling, testing, data analysis, and root cause investigation to improve system performance and reliability.
  • Evaluate design alternatives and make engineering recommendations based on technical performance, risk, cost, schedule, reliability, and operational impact.
  • Collaborate with internal engineering teams, suppliers, partners, and research organizations to develop and mature new electrical infrastructure solutions.
  • Support prototype development, laboratory testing, and system integration activities for first-of-a-kind infrastructure technologies.
  • Embody our culture and values.

As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT), you will develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning equipment under the guidance of more experienced Data Center colleagues.  This opportunity will allow you to develop an understanding of our Data Center environment, familiarize yourself with security and data management procedures, and accelerate your career growth in the process.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Overview

The Windows + Devices Fundamentals team builds and operates data platforms and backend services that help teams improve Windows performance, power efficiency, and reliability. We connect signals from labs and the installed base to trustworthy metrics, actionable diagnostics, and measurable improvements in responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and device health.

We are looking for a Product Manager II to own a data and services product area, from understanding the problem through delivery, adoption, and improvement. You will work closely with engineering, data science, and partner PMs to make data trustworthy, services useful, and insights actionable. This role combines hands-on analysis with product ownership: asking the right questions, defining clear requirements, and following through until the work makes a measurable difference.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Own a feature area: Understand the needs of teams using our data and services. Define problem statements, requirements, success measures, and acceptance criteria; prioritize the backlog within the team's broader roadmap.
  • Measurement and analysis: Define scoped metrics, queries, baselines, and cohorts. Use SQL/KQL to investigate product-health movements; work with data science and engineering to understand statistical uncertainty and separate customer regressions from data or population changes.
  • Improve data quality: Partner with engineering on instrumentation, schemas, and ingestion-to-consumption pipeline requirements. Define checks for completeness, correctness, freshness, and schema changes; incorporate privacy and security needs into the feature plan.
  • Build useful service experiences: Define requirements for service APIs, dashboards, alerts, and diagnostic workflows. Use partner feedback to improve onboarding, documentation, self-service, and automation that reduces manual analysis.
  • Ground decisions in fundamentals: Use measures such as responsiveness, memory usage, battery life, crashes, and hangs to prioritize customer problems. Help teams identify regressions across device and silicon cohorts and assess improvements.
  • Deliver with partners: Coordinate milestones, dependencies, and risks for your feature area. Work with engineering on safe rollout, release criteria, monitoring, and service-health guardrails; communicate blockers and resolve issues early.
  • Learn from operation: Track adoption, data quality, and service health after release. Use partner feedback and operational findings to prioritize improvements in usability, reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Communicate clearly: Explain findings, progress, and tradeoffs to partner teams. Document decisions and open questions, seek different perspectives, and contribute to an inclusive, collaborative team.


Qualifications

Required/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 2+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development.
    • OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in product management, program management, software engineering, data engineering, or a related technical role.
  • Experience defining and delivering a data, analytics, or service feature with engineering partners, including requirements and measures of success.
  • Experience using SQL, Kusto Query Language (KQL), or equivalent tools to analyze data and support product decisions.
  • Understanding of data pipelines, APIs, and basic service-health metrics, with the ability to turn technical findings and customer feedback into actionable requirements.
  • Foundational understanding of performance, power efficiency, or reliability, and how these affect customer experience.
  • Experience with telemetry, diagnostics, dashboards, or experiments used to identify problems and evaluate improvements.
  • Familiarity with Kusto, Azure or comparable cloud data platforms, monitoring, and service-level objectives.
  • Experience with Windows, operating systems, devices, or applications where responsiveness, battery life, and stability matter.
  • Experience collaborating with engineering and data science on data-quality, privacy, or security requirements.
  • Exposure to statistical analysis, anomaly detection, automation, or AI-assisted diagnostic workflows.

We connect signals from labs and the installed base to trustworthy metrics, actionable diagnostics, and measurable improvements in responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and device health.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a data and services product area that turns these signals into effective engineering workflows. You will define product and measurement strategy, set priorities across related capabilities, and partner with engineering and data science from customer discovery through delivery and adoption. This is a hands-on technical PM role: you should be comfortable querying data, reasoning about service behavior, and connecting platform investments to better customer experiences.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Responsibilities
  • Product direction: Own the strategy and roadmap for a data and services product area. Understand engineering teams' needs and prioritize reusable capabilities that address common problems, rather than one-off reports.
  • Data products: Define requirements across telemetry ingestion, transformation, orchestration, storage, and APIs. Partner on schema evolution, data quality, freshness, privacy, and access control so downstream consumers can trust and use the data.
  • Measurement and analysis: Establish metric definitions, baselines, and cohorts across devices, silicon, and customer segments. Use SQL/KQL and statistical reasoning to investigate metric movements, distinguish regressions from measurement changes, and guide investments.
  • Service fundamentals: Partner with engineering on service-level objectives, observability, scale, latency, availability, and cost. Define safe-release criteria and balance new capabilities with service health, security, compliance, and learning from live-site incidents.
  • Windows outcomes: Help define measurable targets and regression guardrails for responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and reliability. Connect insights to prioritized engineering action and track whether changes improve customer scenarios.
  • Cross-team delivery: Align engineering, data science, security, and partner PM teams on scope, dependencies, and tradeoffs. Drive delivery across related feature areas, resolve ambiguity, and raise risks early.
  • Automation and adoption: Prioritize self-service diagnostics, alerting, and validated AI-assisted analysis that help teams detect issues earlier and reduce manual investigation. Measure adoption, diagnostic effectiveness, time saved, and impact on Windows fundamentals.
  • Technical leadership: Communicate complex findings and tradeoffs clearly. Strengthen product thinking through knowledge sharing, mentorship, and inclusive collaboration.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 5+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development.
    • OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in product management, program management, software engineering, data engineering, or a related technical role.
  • Experience leading a data platform, analytics product, or cloud service initiative from problem definition through delivery and adoption in partnership with engineering.
  • Hands-on experience using SQL, Kusto Query Language (KQL), or equivalent tools to investigate large datasets, assess measurement quality, and guide product decisions.
  • Ability to reason about data pipelines, APIs, service dependencies, and operational tradeoffs, and translate customer needs into clear requirements and measurable outcomes.
  • Working knowledge of system performance, power efficiency, or reliability, and the ability to connect technical metrics to customer experience.
  • Experience with lab or deployed-device telemetry, cohort design, experimentation, anomaly detection, or data-quality systems.
  • Experience with Windows, operating systems, devices, or hardware-software interactions that affect performance, power, and reliability.
  • Familiarity with Kusto, Azure or comparable data platforms, and production service operations, including monitoring, incident learning, service-level objectives, and cost optimization.
  • Demonstrated ability to align multiple teams and turn ambiguous technical problems into a sequenced roadmap with measurable results.
  • Experience addressing privacy, security, access control, and retention requirements in data products.
  • Experience evaluating automation or AI-assisted analysis for engineering workflows, including accuracy, usefulness, and adoption.

The WSSI (Windows Silicon System Integration) team is looking for an experienced Silicon Design Verification Team Lead to lead verification for complex silicon subsystems that are part of advanced solutions delivered in Windows client products.

This is an opportunity for an excellent DV leader to combine people leadership with meaningful hands-on technical contribution. You will lead a silicon engineering team that includes design verification, silicon design, and physical design engineers, while serving as the technical anchor for the team's verification strategy, execution, and quality.

The team works on complex security-oriented silicon subsystems that require rigorous pre-silicon verification and close collaboration with architecture, design, firmware, system engineering, and physical design partners to deliver robust silicon quality.

We are looking for a leader who is passionate about building excellent teams, driving rigorous execution, contributing hands-on to complex verification challenges, and continuously improving verification methodologies - including applying modern AI-assisted techniques to improve productivity, debug efficiency, and verification quality.



Responsibilities
  • Lead, grow, and mentor a silicon engineering team that includes design verification, silicon design, and physical design engineers, while fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, collaboration, and continuous learning.
  • Own and drive the verification strategy for complex silicon subsystems from planning through execution, closure, and emulation readiness.
  • Provide substantial hands-on technical contribution and leadership in verification planning, testbench architecture, debug, coverage analysis, regression quality, and verification closure.
  • Build and promote modern verification workflows, including AI-assisted techniques that improve verification environment development, automation, debug efficiency, coverage analysis, and execution quality.
  • Define verification plans, quality metrics, regression strategy, coverage goals, and emulation readiness plans aligned with project milestones.
  • Collaborate closely with architecture, design, system engineering, firmware, and physical design partners to identify risks early, resolve complex issues, and deliver high-quality silicon subsystems.


Qualifications
 
  • B.Sc., M.Sc., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Proven experience and technical excellence in pre-silicon design verification for complex IPs, subsystems, or SoCs, including subsystem integration, and third-party IP integration.
  • Significant hands-on experience with modern DV methodologies, verification planning, testbench development, regressions, coverage analysis, debug, and verification closure.
  • Experience as a people manager or technical leader driving verification work across multiple engineers.

Preferred Qualifications - 

  • Proficiency in SystemVerilog-based verification environments and methodologies such as UVM, assertions, constrained-random verification, and coverage-driven verification, along with Python-based automation and modern verification infrastructure workflows.
  • Experience applying AI-assisted techniques to improve silicon design or verification productivity, debug, coverage, automation, or workflow efficiency.
  • Hands-on experience with Python, Linux, Git-based development workflows, and automation infrastructure.
  • Experience with formal verification, low-power verification, performance verification, or subsystem-level verification.
  • Experience with security-oriented silicon subsystems, including crypto engines, memory protection, secure boot, trusted execution, or related hardware security domains.
  • Experience with emulation platforms such as Palladium.
  • Experience leading or working in teams that include both design and verification engineers.
  • Familiarity with physical design considerations, synthesis, constraints, timing closure, or design handoff flows.
  • Proven problem-solving, communication, ownership, and cross-team collaboration skills.

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DIAT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.  Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Overview

Microsoft's Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) organisation powers the infrastructure supporting Microsoft's cloud services. Datacenter Physical Security is responsible for protecting people, facilities, assets and critical infrastructure.

The Datacenter Security Operations Manager (DSOM) leads day-to-day physical security operations across assigned Microsoft datacenters, campuses and metro locations. The role provides operational leadership, security subject-matter expertise and oversight of contracted security services, ensuring physical security measures remain effective, resilient and aligned with Microsoft policies, standards and operational requirements.

The ideal candidate will work closely with Datacenter Operations, Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety, Compliance, Investigations, Security Design and Delivery, lease providers, construction partners and contracted security service providers.



Responsibilities

Security Operations Leadership

  • Lead and oversee physical security operations across assigned datacenters, campuses and metro locations.
  • Ensure security programmes, procedures, post orders and site-specific instructions are implemented consistently.
  • Assess the effectiveness of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, alarms, physical barriers, screening checkpoints and other security measures.
  • Conduct regular site visits, security reviews and operational assessments to verify compliance with established security baselines.
  • Monitor operational performance, identify gaps and drive corrective and preventive actions.
  • Maintain accurate security documentation, operational records and leadership reporting.

Incident Management and Investigations

  • Lead on-site response to security incidents, threats and significant operational events.
  • Coordinate response activities with Datacenter Operations, security service providers, lease providers, internal security teams and local authorities, as appropriate.
  • Support security investigations, fact-finding, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis and after-action reviews.
  • Ensure incident and investigation records are prepared accurately and actions are tracked to closure.
  • Apply lessons learned from incidents to strengthen operational controls and procedures.
  • Support security bridge calls and provide timely situation updates to security leadership and stakeholders.

Risk, Compliance and Audit Readiness

  • Conduct or support physical security risk assessments and develop practical mitigation plans.
  • Maintain audit readiness across assigned locations.
  • Coordinate audit evidence and support internal, external, customer and regulatory audit activities.
  • Present site physical security posture during audits and operational reviews.
  • Track audit observations, risk actions and remediation commitments to closure.
  • Monitor changes in the local threat and operating environment and recommend appropriate adjustments to security posture.

Vendor Governance and Performance

  • Provide operational oversight of contracted security service providers and ensure services are delivered in line with contractual and programme expectations.
  • Establish a structured governance cadence with vendor security management, including operational reviews, performance discussions and action tracking.
  • Review security incidents, staffing readiness, training, procedure compliance, technology issues and service-delivery risks.
  • Hold service providers accountable for timely remediation of operational gaps while maintaining professional working relationships.
  • Support security staffing readiness for new sites, checkpoints, operational expansions and changes in site requirements.

Datacenter Delivery and Change Management

  • Support physical security readiness for new datacenters, site expansions, beneficial-use activities, early access, checkpoint deployments and security lockdowns.
  • Participate in security integration, end-to-end readiness and transition discussions.
  • Review security readiness requirements, implementation plans, site start-up activities and unresolved security issues.
  • Coordinate with Security Design and Delivery, project teams, Datacenter Operations and security service providers to transition new facilities into steady-state operations.
  • Participate in security-related projects, technology deployments and changes to physical security infrastructure or procedures.

Stakeholder Management

  • Build effective relationships with Datacenter Operations, Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety, Compliance, Security Design and Delivery, Investigations, lease providers and other internal stakeholders.
  • Provide physical security expertise and risk-based guidance to business partners.
  • Communicate security risks, operational constraints and mitigations clearly to management and stakeholders.
  • Influence cross-functional teams to achieve security outcomes without direct organisational authority.
  • Represent physical security in operational governance, readiness and business-review forums.

Crisis Management and Operational Resilience

  • Participate actively in the local crisis management structure.
  • Support emergency preparedness, crisis-response exercises and business-continuity activities.
  • Provide on-site security leadership during significant incidents or periods of elevated risk.
  • Ensure contracted security teams understand and execute their responsibilities under emergency and crisis-management plans.
  • Identify resilience gaps and support practical contingency and recovery measures.

Security Culture and Continuous Improvement

  • Promote security awareness, vigilance and responsible reporting across the datacenter community.
  • Support initiatives addressing insider risk, access control, protection of data-bearing devices and other physical security risks.
  • Analyse incidents, trends, security metrics and operational feedback to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Contribute to regional security programmes, standardisation and the adoption of effective security practices.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 14+ years of professional experience in physical security, security operations, critical-infrastructure protection, military service, law enforcement, investigations, intelligence, risk management or a closely related field.
  • A minimum of 3 years of corporate security experience within a private-sector organisation operating established security governance, compliance, reporting and stakeholder-management processes.
  • Demonstrated experience managing physical security operations in a complex, high-availability or critical-infrastructure environment.
  • Experience overseeing contracted security services, guarding operations or third-party service providers.
  • Experience managing security incidents, investigations, operational risks and corrective actions.
  • Working knowledge of physical security systems, including access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, alarms and screening technologies.
  • Experience supporting security audits, compliance reviews, risk assessments and remediation programmes.
  • Strong stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to work across operations, engineering, compliance, facilities, project and vendor teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of incident reports, risk summaries and leadership updates.
  • Ability to make sound, risk-based decisions in time-sensitive and operationally demanding situations.
  • Ability to travel between supported datacentre locations as business needs require and provide on-site support during significant incidents or critical operational activities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in security management, risk management, business administration, engineering, criminal justice, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience supporting datacenters, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, utilities, manufacturing, energy or another critical-infrastructure sector.
  • Experience working within a multinational corporation or similarly complex organisation.
  • Experience in new-site delivery, security commissioning, operational readiness, checkpoint deployment or site lockdown activities.
  • Experience in crisis management, emergency response, business continuity or operational resilience.
  • Experience managing multi-site security operations or security programmes across a metro or regional footprint.
  • Professional certification such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP), Physical Security Professional (PSP), Professional Certified Investigator (PCI), Project Management Professional (PMP), or an equivalent recognised credential.
  • Working knowledge of relevant Indian regulatory, statutory and operational requirements applicable to private security and critical infrastructure.
  • We encourage candidates to apply even if they do not meet every qualification listed. If your experience is closely aligned with this role and you are passionate about protecting critical infrastructure, we welcome your application.

At Microsoft 365 Core, we are reimagining how hyperscale platforms operate in a world of constrained resources. Our vision is a future where intelligent systems continuously optimize infrastructure, dynamically allocate capacity, and help services scale up, scale down, and adapt in real time without requiring customers to become infrastructure experts. 

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead the future of compute efficiency, workload elasticity, and intelligent capacity management for COSMIC, Microsoft's cloud-native platform powering some of the largest Microsoft 365 services and next-generation AI workloads. 

This role is not about incremental improvements to existing infrastructure. It is about defining how millions of cores of compute are managed in an age of AI. You will shape the strategy for evictable compute, workload mobility, intelligent scaling, and agent-driven capacity optimization. You will partner across Microsoft 365 and Azure to build systems that maximize efficiency while ensuring critical services remain reliable, performant, and cost-effective. 

If you are excited about solving some of the hardest infrastructure challenges in the industry and defining how intelligent platforms operate at hyperscale, we'd love to talk to you. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day. 



Responsibilities

The work in this role is wide-ranging and will involve: 

  • Define the strategy for evictable compute and intelligent workload placement across one of the largest cloud platforms in the world. 

  • Reimagine capacity management for the AI era, moving from human-driven decisions to agent-assisted and autonomous optimization systems. 

  • Build platform capabilities that automatically scale, rebalance, migrate, and reclaim compute resources while minimizing customer effort. 

  • Develop new operating models that maximize utilization of constrained infrastructure and unlock greater efficiency across Microsoft 365 workloads. 

  • Partner with Azure, Microsoft 365, and others to turn capacity from a fixed constraint into a dynamic, software-defined resource. 

  • Drive the long-term vision for autonomous platform operations where intelligent agents continuously optimize fleet and workload efficiency, cost, and scalability. 

  • Influence senior leaders across Microsoft on the future of hyperscale infrastructure, capacity allocation, elasticity, and cloud efficiency. 

  • Create experiences that allow customers to focus on their business outcomes while the platform intelligently manages the complexity of scaling. 

  • Embody our Culture and Values

    • OR equivalent experience.

Overview

Most people experience Microsoft through products like Windows, Office, Xbox, Azure, and Copilot. Behind each of those experiences are the platforms, systems, and operations that help Microsoft bring ideas to market, serve customers, and run at global scale. That's where Microsoft Business Operations (MBO) comes in.

As a Software Engineer in MBO, you'll build the technology that powers Microsoft's business. From the creation of new commercial offers and consumption meters to the systems that track usage, generate insights, enable billing, and measure business outcomes, you'll help shape the end-to-end lifecycle that connects innovation to customer value.

Our engineers operate at the intersection of software, data, AI, and commerce, building intelligent platforms that power some of Microsoft's most critical business processes. You'll work across disciplines to create trusted, scalable systems that provide governance, visibility, and automation from product launch through customer adoption and consumption. The services you build won't just support the business, they'll help define how Microsoft launches, sells, measures, and grows its products around the world.

This is an opportunity to solve complex engineering challenges, influence company-wide platforms, and see your work create impact at a scale few organizations can match.

Position Description

As a Software Engineer II, you will apply computer science principles to design, develop, and optimize software solutions for a set of product features and services. Working with minimal supervision, you will partner with product managers, technical leads, and fellow engineers to understand customer and business requirements and translate them into secure, reliable, scalable, and maintainable solutions.

You will use artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner, taking responsibility for the content of your AI-generated changes to artifacts and applying appropriate tooling and processes. You will apply coding patterns and recommended practices to build extensible, maintainable code; use logging and telemetry to investigate issues and improve reliability, availability, and performance; and uphold Microsoft standards of security, privacy, safety, and accessibility while collaborating with and learning from more experienced engineers.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

As a Software Engineer II, you will contribute across the engineering lifecycle for a set of product features and services - designing, coding, testing, deploying, and operating solutions that are secure, reliable, accessible, and maintainable. You will work with minimal supervision within your feature area, begin to own design decisions under technical leadership, and use AI tools across the development lifecycle in a disciplined manner.

  • AI-native development: Use AI tools across the full software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner. Take responsibility for the content of your AI-generated changes to artifacts, reviewing all changes and applying appropriate tooling and processes with minimal guidance, and apply Responsible AI practices.
  • Coding: Create and implement extensible, maintainable code for a product, service, or feature with minimal supervision, reusing code where applicable. Apply coding patterns and recommended practices, including GenAI-assisted development. Escalate blockers and unknowns and communicate how they impact timelines.
  • Code reviews: Review product features and test code to ensure it meets team standards, has correct test coverage, and is appropriate for the feature. Bring insight to code reviews to improve code quality and help develop other engineers’ skills, reviewing for coding patterns, security risks, compliance issues, and recommended practices.
  • Design and architecture: Provide feedback on architecture proposals under technical leadership, test and explore design options while outlining strengths and weaknesses and begin to own or collaborate on the architecture of solutions. Help ensure designs meet performance, scalability, resiliency, cost (COGS), security, and privacy requirements, and contribute to design documents that support user stories.
  • Testing and quality: Create a clear test strategy that ensures solution quality and prevents regression with minimal supervision. Add tests to cover gaps, fix or remove broken tests, build testable code, and leverage AI tools for test automation, including security testing to validate security invariants.
  • Customer requirements: Work with internal stakeholders (e.g., product managers, security/privacy subject matter experts, technical leads) to understand customer and user requirements for a set of features. Incorporate customer insights and continuous feedback loops and advocate for the security and privacy needs of customers.
  • Dependencies and coordination: Identify dependencies and incorporate them into design documents, understand downstream interactions between systems, and collaborate with other teams to reach common goals where dependencies and validation concerns overlap.
  • Planning and implementation: Execute project plans, release plans, and work items; contribute to breaking larger work items into smaller ones with estimation; escalate issues that might cause delays; and ensure security, privacy, and compliance requirements are accounted for in planning with minimal guidance.
  • Deployment and velocity: Support safe deployment to customers by following safe-change practices, contribute to deployment automation targeting zero-touch deployment, monitor dependency status to ensure only the latest secure versions ship, and help identify when rollback plans should be enacted.
  • Experimentation: Conduct experiments using feature flags and flighting to determine the impact of changes, collaborating with internal partners (e.g., Data Science, product managers) to incorporate success and guard rail metrics.
  • Engineering excellence: Apply secure design principles and “security as code,” build and share tools that improve engineering efficiency, reuse open-source or internal code responsibly, and stay current with developments that improve availability, reliability, efficiency, observability, and performance.
  • Live site and reliability: Participate in an on-call rotation as a designated responsible individual (DRI), mitigating live-site issues using least-privilege access and escalating appropriately. Improve troubleshooting guides, telemetry, and tests to make on-call better, respond within SLA, and contribute to logging and instrumentation for monitoring system health, performance, and security.
  • Security, privacy, and compliance: Apply security guidelines, contribute to deployment gates, scanners, and security monitoring, and follow the correct processes for privacy, safety, and accessibility. Maintain an up-to-date understanding of global and local regulations for the technologies you work on.
  • Collaboration and communication: Communicate clearly and respectfully - verbally and in writing - to drive collaborative, mutually beneficial outcomes; work effectively across teams; and contribute to an inclusive culture and a growth mindset.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience using artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner, taking responsibility for the content of AI-generated changes to artifacts and reviewing all changes.
  • Experience applying computer science principles to design, develop, and optimize scalable algorithms, distributed systems, and business applications, including reference architecture and patterns for resilient system design.
  • Experience in one or more technology domains (e.g., analytics, applications, web, mobile, big data, compute, containers, databases, developer tools, Internet of Things, microservices, or storage).
  • Experience across the engineering and product lifecycle, including task estimation, design and code review, specification review, bug triage, code check-in, sign-off, test targeting, and performance standards.
  • Experience with quality assurance processes, measurements, and standards, including test automation and security testing to validate security invariants.
  • Experience validating solutions and driving improvement by identifying opportunities, and delivering informed, ready designs ahead of production with time for feedback and iteration.
  • Experience building secure software and meeting regulatory and compliance requirements, including secure coding practices, threat modeling, and privacy considerations.
  • Experience with logging, telemetry, monitoring, and live-site operations, including on-call/DRI rotations to maintain reliability and availability.
  • Problem-solving and data analysis skills, applying systems thinking and a data-driven approach to extract actionable insights and make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience contributing to code reviews and coaching engineers, reviewing for coding patterns, security risks, and recommended practices to improve code quality and help develop others’ skills.
  • Experience collaborating across teams on novel solutions, resolving conflict, and communicating clearly and respectfully - verbally and in writing - to achieve mutually beneficial outcomes.

This role will own the product development lifecycle from early concept and technology selection through qualification, manufacturing readiness, and large-scale production deployment.

You will define technical requirements and roadmaps, drive design tradeoffs, lead cross-functional execution, and ensure that optical links, modules, cabling, connectors, and rack-level fiber architectures meet performance, power, reliability, serviceability, cost, and deployment goals. 

You may bring deep knowledge of optical systems along with experience in areas such as product architecture, technology development, ecosystem collaboration, or engineering execution. They can influence platform-level decisions across multiple generations of AI infrastructure, align diverse engineering teams and suppliers, manage technical risk, and deliver innovative optical technologies from concept to production at cloud scale. High-Speed Interconnect & Emerging Technologies

Accelerate Growth

Identifies, qualifies, leads, manages, and closes strategic industry cloud opportunities on prioritized accounts aligned to documented customer business value and outcomes. Accelerates Microsoft Cloud differentiation (e.g., security, AI) against competitors and win more market share. Leverages customer connections and the account team's insights to confirm budget, authority, need and timeline (BANT) information to determine progression or lack thereof of a lead to become a Services Sales opportunity. Contributes to creating and managing connections and driving agreement between necessary stakeholders within Microsoft and customers.

Overview

We are seeking a Web Compliance Manager to help lead and operationalize Microsoft’s enterprise Web Compliance program, with a primary focus on Accessibility compliance, program management, stakeholder engagement, reporting, and operational excellence.

The Web Compliance program helps protect Microsoft’s legal, regulatory, brand, and reputational interests across approximately 1,300 externally facing Microsoft websites. The program brings together Accessibility, Privacy, Cookies, Security, governance, compliance scanning, automation, and reporting to provide a consolidated view of compliance health across Microsoft’s external web estate.

Each quarter, the team consolidates compliance results across major Microsoft businesses, including Windows, Azure, Microsoft 365, Copilot, Gaming/Xbox, Security, Microsoft AI, and Marketing, providing executive leadership with enterprise-level visibility into compliance health, material risks, and remediation progress.

This role will serve as the primary Accessibility compliance lead for Marketing, partnering with CELA, Accessibility teams, website owners, engineering teams, and business stakeholders. Accessibility will be the primary area of ownership, with an expectation that the candidate is familiar with, or open to learning, adjacent Web Compliance areas including Privacy, Cookies, Security, reporting, governance, and audit readiness.

This is a highly matrixed role requiring someone who is diplomatic, collaborative, pragmatic, and a strong communicator. The ideal candidate can navigate organizational friction, competing priorities, and ambiguity while influencing without direct authority and maintaining strong partnerships.

An interest in AI and automation is strongly preferred. Experience with Copilot, agentic workflows, and low-code/no-code solutions is a plus, not a requirement. We are looking for someone who can identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and partner with engineering or vendor resources to bring those solutions to life.



Responsibilities

 

Accessibility Compliance Leadership

  • Serve as the primary Accessibility compliance lead for Marketing, including reporting, consultations, assessments, and remediation coordination.
  • Partner with CELA (Legal), website owners, engineering teams, and business stakeholders to drive compliance outcomes.
  • Coordinates letter-grade tracking, dashboard, and leadership reporting.
  • Drives follow-through with accountable teams.
  • Monitor emerging Accessibility requirements and determine potential impacts to processes, reporting, guidance, and technology.

Web Compliance Program Management & Reporting

  • Help operate Microsoft’s enterprise Web Compliance program across Accessibility, Privacy, Cookies, Security, governance, reporting, and audit readiness.

The Travel and Card Operations Program Manager will support the delivery, operational governance, optimization, and continuous improvement of Microsoft’s global corporate Travel and Card programs, helping ensure consistent, scalable, and effective program operations across a complex global environment.  

This role will focus on building scalable operational solutions across corporate travel and payments, including the development and optimization of corporate card and commercial payment solutions   that improve efficiency, financial controls, reconciliation, and employee experience. 

The successful candidate will bring hands-on corporate travel and payments experience, strong operational program management capabilities, and an AI-first mindset. The role will identify opportunities to simplify processes, automate manual activities, improve service delivery, and build solutions that can scale across a complex global organization. 

This role will partner closely with Procurement, Finance, Controllership, Human Resources, and business stakeholders, including Finance Controllers, HR Business Partners, Budget Managers, and Business Managers, to understand business requirements and translate them into practical, scalable Travel and Card solutions. 

The ideal candidate combines strong knowledge of corporate travel operations and commercial payment programs with a builder mentality, using data, AI, automation, and process improvement to solve operational challenges and continuously improve the employee experience. 



Responsibilities

Scalable, AI-First Operations 

  • Apply an AI-first mentality to Travel and Card operations by identifying opportunities to automate repetitive work, improve decision-making, and simplify employee and operational experiences. 

  • Identify practical applications of AI, automation, analytics, and workflow capabilities across travel servicing, payment operations, employee support, reconciliation, compliance, and reporting. 

  • Design processes and solutions with scalability in mind, reducing reliance on manual activities and one-off operational support. 

  • Use experimentation, data, operational insights, and customer feedback to continuously improve Travel and Card processes. 

  • Support the adoption and operationalization of new tools and capabilities that improve program efficiency and employee experience. 

Business Stakeholder Engagement 

  • Build effective partnerships across Procurement, Finance, Controllership, Human Resources, and other corporate functions. 

  • Engage with Finance Controllers, HR Business Partners, Budget Managers, Business Managers, and other business stakeholders to understand business needs, identify operational challenges, and develop appropriate solutions. 

  • Translate complex Travel and Card requirements into clear operational recommendations. 

  • Facilitate working sessions and operational reviews to drive decisions, accountability, and follow-through. 

  • Balance business requirements with global program standards, financial controls, operational scalability, policy requirements, and employee experience. 

Travel Operations & Governance 

  • Support the effective delivery and governance of Microsoft’s global corporate travel program, driving consistency, scalability, and operational excellence across markets. 

  • Monitor operational performance, service trends, employee feedback, and recurring issues to identify opportunities for program improvement. 

  • Support global and regional program changes, ensuring operational requirements, stakeholder needs, and employee experience are considered throughout implementation. 

 Global Card Program & Payment Solutions 

  • Support the operational management, optimization and continuous improvement of Microsoft’s global corporate Card Program. 

  • Support the design, implementation and ongoing management of corporate card and commercial payment solutions that improve employee experience, operational efficiency, financial controls and scalability. 

  • Partner with Finance, Controllership, Procurement, card issuers, payment providers, and suppliers to implement and improve payment capabilities. 

  • Identify opportunities to expand centralized, digital, and automated payment solutions that reduce manual processes and improve financial controls. 

  • Monitor payment operations and supplier performance and drive resolution of recurring issues. 

  • Support the development of scalable payment operating models, processes, controls, and governance.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in corporate travel, commercial payments, corporate card programs, Travel & Expense operations, or closely related disciplines.
  • Experience partnering with business stakeholders including Finance, Controllership, Procurement, Human Resources, Budget Managers, or Business Managers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting corporate travel, Travel & Expense, payment/card, or commercial payment operations in a complex business environment.
  • Experience with commercial card or B2B payment solutions, such as corporate cards, purchasing cards, virtual cards, lodge/central accounts, centralized travel payment solutions, or related providers/suppliers.
  • Experience managing cross-functional operational programs, partnering with multiple stakeholder groups, and translating business requirements into scalable solutions.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills, with experience using data, analytics, Power BI, AI, automation, or workflow technologies to improve operations.
  • Experience with global service delivery, supplier performance management, operational governance, continuous improvement, and managing priorities in a global, matrixed environment.

Microsoft’s Audit, Risk, and Compliance group identifies emerging risks and assesses the effectiveness of management’s response. As a Risk Manager, you will support the Chief Risk Officer for MIPSL by helping shape risk governance, risk reporting, oversight, and regulatory engagement for a new regulated entity. You will work in a hybrid model in Dublin and partner closely with ARC, MIPSL leadership, Operations, Technology, and FinCrime stakeholders.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Responsibilities

• Enterprise Risk Framework Execution: Support the MIPSL CRO in implementing and maintaining the MIPSL enterprise risk management (ERM) framework, aligned with CBI expectations and proportional to a regulated payments institution.

• Risk Register & Governance: Maintain the MIPSL enterprise risk register, ensuring risks, controls, and mitigation actions are current, and support structured risk governance through committees and reporting forums.

• Incident & Issue Oversight: Oversee MIPSL risk events, incidents, and near misses, ensuring root cause analysis is performed and lessons learned are embedded into the control environment.
• Third-Party & Outsourcing Risk Coordination: Work closely with MIPSL Operations and Technology oversight roles to ensure third-party risks are captured within the MIPSL enterprise risk view and aligned to outsourcing requirements.
• Stress Testing & Scenario Analysis: Support MIPSL risk scenario analysis and stress testing activities, particularly relating to operational disruption, financial crime exposure, or third-party failure.
• Regulatory Engagement Support: Prepare MIPSL risk materials for CBI engagement, including inspections, risk assessments, and ongoing supervisory dialogue.

  • Relevant experience in risk management, privacy, security, compliance, government intelligence, operations, auditing, and/or finance; OR equivalent experience.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree in Risk Management, Engineering, Government Intelligence, Security, Information Technology, or a related field, with solid experience in risk management across operations, engineering, information technology, business analysis, consulting, auditing, privacy, security, compliance, government intelligence, and/or finance; OR Bachelor’s Degree in a related field, including Cybersecurity, with significant relevant experience; OR equivalent experience.

  • Experience supporting audits, regulatory reviews, inspections, or risk governance in a regulated environment.
  • Experience with AI, AI-based analytical tools, AI governance, or AI governance frameworks.

Overview

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to help redefine how engineering gets done across Windows Silicon and System Integration (WSSI) and demonstrate what agentic engineering can make possible for Windows at scale. 

The Windows Silicon and System Integration (WSSI) organization delivers a leading integrated silicon + OS platform for the new era of computing. Our work spans new and in-market devices, multiple form factors and silicon partners, and some of the hardest systems challenges in Windows, including performance, power, reliability, compatibility, and overall product quality. We believe agentic AI can fundamentally change how engineers build, validate, debug, and improve complex systems. 

As a Principal Software Engineer, you will set technical direction for agentic engineering across WSSI while remaining deeply engaged with the technology. You will identify the engineering problems where agents can have the greatest impact, architect and build solutions alongside teams, and take promising ideas from prototype to trusted production workflows.  

In this role, you will help turn WSSI's most successful agentic capabilities into a compelling technical story: demonstrating what is possible, sharing lessons and reusable approaches, building excitement and credibility with engineering leaders, and establishing WSSI as a source of innovation in agentic engineering across Windows + Devices and Microsoft. As those capabilities mature, you will identify opportunities to extend them to new engineering scenarios and partner organizations, creating new areas where WSSI technology and capabilities can have broader impact. 

This role therefore sits at the intersection of deep engineering, technical strategy, and organizational influence. You will bring together AI, engineering systems, telemetry, diagnostics, and developer workflows to create closed-loop experiences that help engineers find problems faster, understand root causes, develop solutions, and validate outcomes. At the same time, you will articulate the vision behind that work, engage technical leaders and partner teams, and create momentum around opportunities that can grow from successful WSSI solutions into broader engineering capabilities. 

This is not a role solely focused on introducing new AI tools. You will instead define how engineering itself evolves as agentic capabilities mature, while also shaping the role WSSI plays in that evolution. You will establish reusable technical patterns, raise the engineering bar for AI-enabled systems, influence teams across organizational boundaries, and build the mechanisms that allow successful approaches to scale while expanding the impact and reach of WSSI's agentic engineering capabilities.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Set the technical vision and multi-year strategy for agentic engineering across WSSI, defining how agents can transform design, implementation, code review, testing, validation, debugging, diagnostics, and release workflows. 

  • Lead from architecture through production. Identify the most impactful engineering problems, establish the technical approach, build critical components where needed, and lead focused cross-functional AI squads from experimentation through evaluation, deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement. 

  • Pioneer closed-loop agentic engineering systems that combine telemetry, engineering data, tools, and reasoning to detect issues, investigate likely causes, automate diagnostic and debugging workflows, propose and implement solutions, and verify outcomes with appropriate human oversight. 

  • Establish the technical architecture for agentic workflows at scale, including reusable approaches for orchestration, context engineering, tool integration, evaluation, observability, reliability, and safe operation in complex engineering environments. 

  • Turn technical breakthroughs into organizational momentum. Build compelling demonstrations and technical narratives around WSSI's agentic capabilities, communicate their impact to engineering and technical leadership, and represent WSSI's work across Windows + Devices and Microsoft. 

  • Create the engineering bar for production AI systems. Define rigorous evaluation methods, quality standards, failure-mode analysis, safeguards, and operational practices that enable teams to move from compelling demos to dependable engineering workflows. 

  • Measure real engineering impact. Establish outcome measures and feedback loops across engineering productivity, product quality, workflow reliability, developer experience, and sustained adoption, using evidence to guide technical investment and continuously improve deployed systems. 

  • Drive technical alignment across organizational boundaries. Build consensus around architecture and engineering standards, influence technical leaders without direct authority, and create durable approaches that teams across WSSI can adopt and extend. 

  • Establish rigorous standards for responsible AI, security, privacy, compliance, and human oversight, ensuring agentic systems earn engineers' trust and can be safely integrated into critical engineering workflows. 

  • Multiply technical capability across WSSI. Mentor engineers and technical leaders, develop communities of practice, share reusable patterns and lessons, and help teams build the technical proficiency to create and operate agentic workflows independently. 

  • Stay ahead of a rapidly evolving field. Maintain deep awareness of relevant industry and research advances, determine which developments matter for WSSI, and translate them into concrete technical recommendations, experiments, and durable engineering improvements. 

  • Identify opportunities to expand WSSI's impact. Recognize where technology, architectures, and workflows developed within WSSI can address broader engineering problems, cultivate partnerships around those opportunities, and help shape new areas of technical investment and ownership.

  • Experience architecting production agentic systems, including orchestration, tool use, prompt and context engineering, retrieval, evaluation, observability, reliability, cost, latency, and integration into existing engineering environments.

Search Platform is the retrieval and grounding foundation for Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents. Our shared services turn Microsoft 365 knowledge into trusted, permission-aware evidence through indexing, retrieval and ranking, and grounding. Product teams across Microsoft consume them through Microsoft Graph and Work IQ, and relevance teams ship quality on top of them. Every Copilot answer, search result, and agent action is only as good as the evidence behind it, so our job is to make every quality gain land faster, cheaper, and everywhere, and to prove it with data everyone trusts. 

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager on the Enterprise Search and Grounding Platform team to drive strategy and execution to deliver Copilot and Agents quality gains.  

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Responsibilities

The strategy 

  • Define the vision, multi-year roadmap, and success metrics for the Developer Experience pillar, anchored on the Search Platform north star: one trusted platform, tuned by scenario, with recall-forward, low-latency retrieval for agents. 

  • Own product definition for the developer-facing API surface, including the next major version of our core retrieval API and the Work IQ and Retrieval API integration patterns, with a bias toward stable, scenario-agnostic contracts that outlive any single experience. 

  • Decide what the platform should offer as a shared capability and what stays with individual agent teams, and drive the consolidation of bespoke integrations onto supported patterns.

Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide, and we are looking for Senior Lease Delivery Program Manager, Datacenter Portfolio Management to help achieve our mission.
