Overview
CADET (Customer and Analytics Driven Evals Team) is building a customer-grounded quality system for Copilot. Our mission is to rapidly identify the customer scenarios that matter most, represent them faithfully in evaluation and learning assets, run quality gates continuously, and turn every important failure into reusable product and model improvements.
 
We bring together DSAT and other product signals, deep customer engagements to create representative eval sets. Operating in a fast-paced environment, we connect customer grounded quality issues with quality teams to advance Copilot quality and product innovation. 
 
We are looking for a Principal Applied Scientist to work directly with enterprise customers and Copilot teams, translating high-value workflows, expected outcomes, and recurring pain points into trusted evaluation and learning signals. You will set the scientific direction for customer-grounded quality: define what “good” means, assess whether eval portfolios represent real needs, diagnose model and agent failures, and convert evidence into reusable evals, RLEs, reward signals, and post-training priorities. The ideal candidate combines scientific depth with product judgment and can turn ambiguous customer problems into rigorous, scalable methods in partnership with applied researchers and ML engineers.
 
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
 


Responsibilities
  • Set the scientific strategy for customer-grounded quality across priority Copilot intents, defining what good means and the tradeoffs across various quality and safety attributes
  • Translate user research, enterprise customer feedback, DSAT, and production incidents into evaluation and post-training priorities, then lead cross-team creation of reusable evaluation, regression, RLE, and post-training assets for the highest-value workflows and failure patterns.
  • Develop methods to assess evaluation-set representativeness, coverage, freshness, discrimination, grader reliability, and alignment with production outcomes, identifying material gaps, drift, and emerging loss patterns.
  • Design behavior and task evaluations, rubrics, graders, and calibration methods that translate qualitative customer expectations into measurable release-over-release quality.
  • Establish methods to attribute quality losses across grounding, retrieval, tools, orchestration, model reasoning, response generation, and evaluation, linking offline movement with online signals such as DSAT, task completion, retries, abandonment, and escalation.
  • Set a high bar for scientific rigor, reproducibility, documentation, and interpretation of results while mentoring scientists and engineers and influencing evaluation and post-training strategy across organizational boundaries.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
    • OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 4+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
    • OR Doctorate in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 3+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
    • OR equivalent experience. 

Preferred: Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in computer science, machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Significant experience applying machine learning, natural language processing, information retrieval, reinforcement learning, experimentation, or evaluation methods to complex production systems.
  • Experience designing evaluations, metrics, experiments, datasets, graders, or reward functions for AI or agentic systems.
  • Hands-on ability to inspect model outputs, identify behavioral patterns, and translate qualitative judgments into testable hypotheses and measurable evaluation criteria.
  • Solid understanding of statistical inference, sampling, measurement validity, bias, uncertainty, and experimental design.
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to drive results across organizational boundaries by aligning science, engineering, product, and platform teams around shared quality goals, explicit ownership boundaries, and measurable outcomes.
  • Experience with large language models, copilots, agents, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, or enterprise grounding.
  • Experience running or partnering on RLHF, direct preference optimization, instruction tuning, fine-tuning, or human-preference data programs.
  • Experience connecting offline metrics with online product behavior and customer outcomes.
  • Experience working directly with enterprise customers or translating qualitative research and customer signals into scientific assets.
  • Publication record, patents, or demonstrated industry impact in relevant applied research areas.

Overview

The Cloud & AI organization accelerates Microsoft's mission to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers' heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world.

Are you passionate about emulating the world's most determined adversaries – and about teaching machines to do it alongside you? Join the Microsoft Red Team (MRT) organization, where we emulate real-world advanced persistent threats to ensure Microsoft, and the customers who depend on us, are prepared to face and respond to any adversary.

CyberShield is the MRT program that extends our red team capability beyond Microsoft's own estate to select external customers. Our mandate is to shift red teaming from point-in-time, human-led engagements to a software-driven, continuous model powered by agentic, AI-driven red teaming. CyberShield operators work across Microsoft's own environment and customer environments spanning cloud, identity, network, endpoint, hardware, and operational security domains, and partner closely with Microsoft's adversary hunting organization to present a unified front to the customers we defend together.

We are looking for a Principal Security Engineer to serve as a principal-level operator on CyberShield engagements. You will plan and execute full-scope adversary emulation operations end-to-end, and – critically – you will drive agentic, AI-driven red team operations: designing, directing, and supervising autonomous and semi-autonomous agents that discover, chain, and exploit weaknesses at a scale and cadence no human-only team can match. You will be a forward-deployed technical authority in front of customer security leaders, a trusted peer to senior engineers across MRT, and a force multiplier who raises the technical bar for every operator and agent on the team.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.



Responsibilities
  • Execute CyberShield red team operations end-to-end – initial access, privilege escalation, lateral movement and pivoting, persistence, objective completion, and reporting – against Microsoft's own environment and select external customer environments, using real-world adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures to validate detection, investigation, and response.
  • Develop custom tooling, implants, and tradecraft to evade modern defenses and emulate the capabilities of advanced adversaries.
  • Lead agentic red team operations: design and direct AI agents that autonomously perform reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and post-exploitation; define guardrails, oversight, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints; and drive the shift from human-led execution to continuous, software-driven, agentic analysis.
  • Discover and exploit vulnerabilities end-to-end across application, cloud, identity, network, hardware, and operational security layers, chaining findings into realistic attack paths that demonstrate business impact.
  • Serve as the forward-deployed technical lead with customers: brief CISOs and security leaders, translate findings into actionable narratives, and deliver lightweight defensive engineering guidance alongside offensive results.
  • Prototype and productionize tools, agents, and techniques that scale offensive emulation and vulnerability discovery, and feed requirements back to our offensive AI platform engineering team based on what works in real environments.
  • Collaborate with Blue Teams, GHOST (Microsoft's adversary hunting organization, which proactively hunts for and responds to real-world intrusions in Microsoft and customer environments), MSTIC (the Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center, which tracks nation-state and criminal threat actors and their tradecraft), and internal Microsoft service teams to convert findings into product hardening and improved defender readiness.
  • Set operational standards and playbooks for CyberShield engagements; mentor senior operators and virtual-team specialists drawn from across MRT.
  • Advocate for security change across Microsoft and its customers by building partnerships and clearly communicating the impact of risk.
  • Embody our Culture and Values.


Qualifications

Required/minimum qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 4+ years experience in security or related field OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 6+ years experience in security or related field OR equivalent experience.

Other requirements

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
    •    Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
    •    Customer environment screening: Operators working in customer environments may be required to complete additional customer- or government-directed vetting.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 8+ years experience in security or related field OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 12+ years experience in security or related field OR equivalent experience.
  • 6+ years of experience planning and leading red team or adversary emulation operations against enterprise or cloud environments.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience building, directing, or operating AI-driven or agentic offensive security tooling in real operations. Active U.S. Government TS//SCI clearance with full-scope polygraph is a strong plus, enabling immediate work with our most sensitive customers.
  • 8+ years of experience identifying and exploiting security vulnerabilities across cloud (Azure, AWS, GCP), identity (Entra ID / Active Directory), Windows and Linux endpoints, network, and hardware.
  • Experience designing multi-agent or autonomous systems using large language models – orchestration frameworks, tool use, agent evaluation, and safety guardrails – applied to offensive security.
  • 6+ years of experience with coding or scripting in languages such as Python, C#, C++, Go, PowerShell, .NET, Rust, or other comparable programming languages, including building and maintaining offensive tooling.
  • Experience in customer-facing or consulting roles delivering red team results to executive audiences; ability to move fluently between deep technical detail and business impact.
  • Blue team, detection engineering, or incident response experience – you understand how defenders think and can help them get better.
  • Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK, threat-informed defense, and regulated red team frameworks (e.g., TIBER-EU, CBEST, DORA).
  • Recognized contributions to the security community: research, open-source tooling, conference talks, or CVEs.

As a Software Engineer II, you will build and improve features for commercial seller experiences. You will implement and test code, participate in feature design, collaborate with engineers and product partners, and use customer feedback and service data to improve the software. You will work with AI-powered experiences, Dynamics 365 integrations, web applications, and Azure services while growing your skills in secure, reliable systems. 

This is an opportunity to contribute to meaningful product features, learn from experienced engineers, and see the impact of your work in sellers’ daily workflows.

The Commercial Sales Experiences Engineering team builds the platforms, applications, and AI-powered experiences that enable Microsoft's commercial sellers to operate more effectively, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to customers. Through modern engineering practices and intelligent technology solutions, the team drives digital transformation across Microsoft Sales. 

 



Responsibilities

  • Implement, test, and maintain code for product features and services, reusing existing components and patterns where appropriate. 

  • Explore design options for assigned features, identify strengths and trade-offs, and provide feedback on proposed technical approaches. 

  • Work with engineers, architects, and product partners to build or modify features; contribute to design documents, user stories, and product requirements with guidance. 

  • Develop and improve seller-facing experiences, APIs, and integrations across AI-powered workflows, Dynamics 365, and Azure services as needed for the team’s priorities. 

  • Write automated tests, investigate defects, and use code reviews and service data to improve quality, accessibility, security, and performance. 

  • Contribute to live-site support by monitoring features, helping investigate incidents, and implementing fixes or follow-up improvements with the team. 

  • Engage with product partners and, where appropriate, customers to understand scenarios and feedback; share findings that help refine features and priorities. 

  • Contribute reusable components and development practices that make the team’s work more consistent and efficient. 



Qualifications

Required Qualifications 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related technical field and 5+ years of technical engineering experience coding in languages such as C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python; or equivalent experience. 

  • Experience designing, developing, testing, and shipping software features or services in a team environment. 

  • Proficiency in at least one programming language and the ability to learn and work across a modern application stack. 

  • Experience building web applications, backend services, or distributed systems. 

  • Experience working with APIs, data stores, and cloud services. 

  • Working knowledge of software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, debugging, automated testing, source control, performance, and secure coding. 

  • Ability to collaborate across disciplines, communicate design choices, and deliver work iteratively. 

 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience taking ownership of a feature area, from technical design through production rollout and follow-up improvements. 

  • Experience building AI-powered applications, Copilot experiences, intelligent agents, or conversational workflows. 

  • Familiarity with Dynamics 365, Dataverse, Power Platform, or similar business application platforms. 

  • Experience developing services with C#, .NET, ASP.NET Core, or a comparable backend stack. 

  • Experience building modern user interfaces with React and TypeScript. 

  • Experience with Azure application hosting, serverless or messaging services, containers, or other cloud services. 

  • Experience working with relational or NoSQL data stores and data integration patterns. 

  • Understanding of identity, authentication, authorization, privacy, and secure software development. 

  • Experience improving developer workflows through reusable components, automation, or platform tooling. 

  • Ability to compare design options, explain trade-offs, and work through cross-team dependencies. 

  • Clear communication and effective collaboration with engineers, product partners, and business stakeholders. 

  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools responsibly and validating their output.

Overview

Azure Fiber is looking for a Senior Optical Measurement Systems Engineer to join our Metrology team. You will apply fundamental science to develop advanced measurement capabilities for optical fibre products, with particular relevance to hollow-core fibre and, where applicable, fibre-cable characterisation.


In this role, you will own significant measurement-system challenges from first principles through deployment. You will use fundamental physics and measurement science to explain the underlying optical behaviour, define what must be measured and establish methods that are both scientifically rigorous and practically useful. You will connect theoretical modelling with bench-top characterisation, then translate successful methods into robust, automated and fully productionised test systems. You will create clarity in technically ambiguous areas, make data-driven engineering decisions, and influence partners across research, product engineering, manufacturing and quality.

This is a hands-on laboratory role requiring regular on-site work in our state-of-the-art Romsey facilities. You will build, align, automate, troubleshoot and validate optical systems while helping others adopt rigorous measurement practices.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Lead the architecture, development and validation of optical measurement systems for fibre and related products, with emphasis on hollow-core fibre and occasionally cable-level measurements.
  • Apply fundamental science—including optics, materials science and measurement physics—to identify observable signatures, derive measurement principles and develop new characterisation methods for complex fibre systems.
  • Translate physical models and measurement theory into test requirements, measurement methods, uncertainty budgets, calibration strategies, traceability plans and acceptance criteria.
  • Bridge early theoretical and bench-top characterisation work to repeatable production test solutions, including optical and electronic hardware, instrument control, automation software, data pipelines, fixtures, safety controls and maintainability.
  • Design experiments and interpret observations relevant to fibre characterisation, including attenuation, mode coupling and modal content, polarisation effects, interference and other light–matter interactions.
  • Establish and maintain measurement-system-analysis practices, including gauge repeatability and reproducibility studies, correlation studies, reference artefacts, calibration controls, statistical process control and capability assessment.
  • Apply control-systems fundamentals to sensing, actuation, feedback, stabilisation and automation, improving the performance and robustness of laboratory and production equipment.
  • Drive technical investigations and root-cause analysis across relevant areas; communicate decisions and risks clearly, influence cross-functional partners, mentor engineers and improve shared engineering standards. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Degree in Optical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND technical engineering experience OR equivalent experience.
  • Understanding of optical-fibre characterisation, light-scattering and related optical phenomena, together with control-systems fundamentals and the ability to lead complex technical work across teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop hands-on optical measurement or characterisation systems, including laboratory instrumentation, experiment design, automation and data analysis.

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role.
  • These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: 
    • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in characterising optical fibres (hollow-core fibres would be a plus), fibre components or optical cable, using techniques such as cutback, OTDR or backscatter, modal, polarisation, interferometric or imaging measurements.
  • Experience in converting research or prototype test methods into production equipment with appropriate throughput, reliability, serviceability, safety, data integrity and operational controls.
  • Programming and test-automation experience using tools such as Python, C# or equivalent, including instrument communications, data pipelines, analysis and visualisation.
  • Evidence of technical leadership at senior individual-contributor level: creating clarity in ambiguous problems, setting technical direction, influencing stakeholders, reviewing designs and mentoring other engineers.

It requires executive presence, consultative selling discipline, technical depth, and the ability to connect customer outcomes with Microsoft solutions and services.

We anticipate and provide capacity for continuous scale. The CO+I Engineering team (CO+IE) delivers services, applications, and automation supporting datacenter planning, construction, and operation. CO+I Engineering is a competitive advantage for Microsoft, and an important pillar in its cloud success.

  • Collaborate with and demonstrate features developed to stakeholders in an Agile environment

Overview

We are looking for a Principal Customer Success Account Manager (CSAM) to join our team in Stavanger. The role is intended to work with one of our largest customers in the energy sector and be an integral part of the account team. Our focus as a Customer Success organization is straightforward: helping our customers succeed with the investments they have made in Microsoft technologies and services.As CSAM you are responsible for what happens after the customer has decided to invest. That means understanding their business priorities, agreeing on a plan for how cloud, data and AI should support them, and following through so the plan is actually delivered and the customer sees the value they expected. The Account Executive owns the commercial relationship; you own the delivery and value side of the same account.In practice, much of the job is coordination. You bring together Microsoft Unified services, consulting and partner resources, keep the overall picture across several parallel workstreams, and make sure risks and dependencies are raised early rather than late. You will spend time with both senior decision makers and the people doing the day-to-day work at the customer, and you need to be comfortable in both settings.This is a senior individual contributor role. We are looking for someone with solid experience from large, multi-year transformation programs, preferably from oil and gas or a similar industry, who lives in the Stavanger area and wants to work close to the customer.Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

The Principal CSAM's mission is simple to state and demanding to deliver: ensure the customer realizes the full value of what they have invested in with Microsoft. You do this as an integral part of the account team, complementing the Account Executive's commercial leadership with delivery and adoption leadership. Your responsibilities span three themes: owning the customer success engagement end to end, leading the planning and governance of large transformation programs, and orchestrating people across roles through a collaborative, composed leadership style.

Own customer success and value realization end to end

  • Own the end-to-end customer engagement lifecycle for one or more strategic enterprise accounts — from listening and consulting through design, delivery, value realization and ongoing optimization — ensuring clean handovers and evidenced business outcomes at every stage.
  • Ensure the customer is getting the most value out of their Microsoft investments, driving adoption and optimization of the cloud, data and AI services they have already committed to and connecting each engagement to measurable business results.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior customer stakeholders across business and technical functions, developing long-term relationships grounded in a deep understanding of each customer's business context, operating model and technology landscape.

Lead complex, multi-year transformation programs

  • Lead the planning, orchestration and review of multi-year, multi-workstream cloud and data transformation programs with significant technical complexity and executive visibility on both the customer and Microsoft side.
  • Develop and maintain customer success plans and strategic delivery roadmaps — in partnership with the Account Executive and account team — that align engagements to the customer's priorities, prioritize investments and set clear executive expectations on outcomes, risks and dependencies.
  • Proactively anticipate, identify, mitigate and escalate delivery risks, blockers and customer concerns, applying disciplined program governance and structured communication.

Orchestrate and lead across the account team

  • Partner with the Account Executive and the wider account team so that commercial strategy and customer success planning move as one, and orchestrate internal and partner delivery resources across sales, engineering and consulting functions with a natural reflex to share ownership across roles rather than defend role boundaries.
  • Set the tone for cross-team collaboration through a calm, consensus-building communication style that absorbs pressure, de-escalates friction and maintains executive composure across a sustained, multi-year program horizon.
  • Continuously improve delivery management methodology, processes and tools to strengthen operational health and the predictability of customer outcomes.


Qualifications

Required qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Business, Sociology, Psychology, Computer Science, or related field AND several years customer success, solution delivery, practice management, customer-facing consulting, or portfolio management experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Sociology, Psychology, Computer Science or related field AND severa years customer success, solution delivery, practice management, customer-facing consulting, or portfolio management experience OR equivalent experience.
  • Fluent in Norwegian and English, both spoken and written.

Architecture Design and Deployment

Collaborates with the Project Manager to jointly drive project/technical governance of the design, build, and deployment into use of proof of concepts (POCs) and pilots, using enterprise architecture processes and ensuring quality control through peer review. Collaborates with the Account Team and/or Bid Team to understand the business solution/problem. The Defender for Office 365 product group owns the protection experience for email and collaboration across Microsoft 365. The product management team drives end-to-end ownership across the product lifecycle, partnering with groups and stakeholders across the organization and directly with customers and partners. As part of Microsoft XDR, the product spans real-time detection, post-delivery response and recovery, investigation and hunting, and pre-breach capabilities. The team owns one of the largest security solutions in the XDR portfolio and helps shape how communication and productivity security will work in an era of AI-powered social engineering, using AI to strengthen detection and making MDO the trusted entry point into the broader Defender suite. The group works at the intersection of protection efficacy, explainability and everyday usability, serving SOC analysts, email administrators and end users alike.

Are you a product leader who wants to own a product line that protects organizations every single day, and to build the team that delivers it Come work with us at the largest security company in the world, on one of its most broadly deployed security products.

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 protects email and collaboration across Microsoft 365. Attackers are shifting from recognizable malicious artifacts toward adaptive, multi-step social engineering, and generative AI is lowering the cost of personalizing those attacks at scale. Staying ahead of that shift — while keeping protection fast, explainable and operable at enterprise scale, is the challenge this role leads.

You will oversee a portfolio of complex engagements while developing high-performing teams and shaping a sustainable security product. You will own the overall health, quality and success of a product line and its features within the MDO portfolio.

Overview

As a Senior Critical Environment Technician (CET) based in Western Sydney and within Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from co-ordinating with supplier/vendors, working closely with Management to address operational, risk and safety situations, mentoring other Critical Environment (CE) Technicians, having a hands-on understanding on how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while co-ordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.  This role is based 100% onsite within one of our Data Centers. 

 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.  Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.  Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities
  • Serve as an operations specialist in one major area of CE operations (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators) and work on advanced tasks independently.
  • Inspect and supervise critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), mechanical systems), building, and grounds regularly for unsafe or abnormal conditions and escalate per applicable policies and standards.  
  • Utilize internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work.
  • Safely and quickly respond to and leads onsite incident response teams for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs without supervision.
  • Enhance, develop new or follow pre-existing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), and standard operating procedures (SOPs) in relation to CE operations and incidents.
  • Perform various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for CE equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) and escalate when appropriate.
  • Have a hands-on understanding of how equipment works and how to troubleshoot equipment, systems, subsystems, and components independently within your trained discipline(s).
  • Provide consultation to lower-level colleagues in troubleshooting systems and problems.  
  • Understand, follow, and ensure safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], environmental health and safety (EH&S), toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance with applicable federal, state, local, and Microsoft requirements.
  • Embody our culture and values

    • OR equivalent industry work experience.

Overview

As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT), you will stage, set up and perform hardware deployments. In addition, you will also perform troubleshooting and diagnostics on equipment, as well as perform hardware decommissions for simple changes and refreshes following Standard Operating Procedures. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your understanding of Data Center standard processes and procedures, develop mentoring skills while providing guidance to peers, familiarizing yourself with security and data management procedures, and accelerate your career growth in the process.  This role is based 100% onsite in one of of Data Centers based in Melbourne.

 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.  Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.  Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities
  • Perform diagnostics and troubleshooting following standard procedures, quickly identifies the cause(s) of issues, and replaces faulty components with minimal customer and business disruption.
  • Perform post-execution quality checks and verifies that grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling are set up properly according to safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Tasks (NDTs).
  • Decommission hardware for simple changes and refreshes (e.g., memory upgrades, rebuilds) following standard procedures with minimal guidance.
  • Follow procedures to communicate, report, and escalate incidents to appropriate Microsoft data center operations management units, Technician Leads, and engineering specialists.
  • Assist and provide guidance to other technicians to complete challenging or complex tasks.
  • Complete required training aligned to the role and workload; observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training.
  • Contribute to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with others, contributing to regular team meetings, asking questions, and staying apprised of the status of others' work.
  • Take pride and a sense of accountability for the service quality, completeness, and resulting user experience; displays accountability and ownership of the data center facilities.
  • Embody our culture and values.

 



Qualifications

 Required Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma, TAFE, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components AND 1+ year(s) industry work experience supporting IT hardware equipment or related technology (specifically server management, routers, switches, cabling, racking & stacking etc).

 

Background Check Requirements: 

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: 

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
  • Citizenship Verification: This position requires verification of Australian Citizenship (including an Australian Passport) to meet federal government security requirements.
  • NV1/2, PV Clearance Assessment: This position may require an enhanced background check conducted through the Australian Government Security Vetting Agency.

 

Whilst not required, we also look for the following Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years' industry worik experience supporting IT equipment or related technology.
  • Applicable certifications: CompTIA (A+, Server+, Network+), Basic Structure Cabling (BSC).

Senior Director, Workforce Intelligence 

Lead the development of workforce intelligence products that help leaders make more informed decisions about talent, capability, capacity and investment. This role combines product leadership, workforce analytics and strategic foresight to turn complex information into practical choices with measurable business value. 

You will take products from concept through adoption, connecting business needs with rigorous analysis and thoughtful user experience. Working across People, Finance, Engineering, Research and business teams, you will build trusted solutions that help the organization understand its workforce, anticipate changing needs and evaluate investment trade-offs. This is a product-building leadership role, not solely a reporting or analytics function. 



Responsibilities

What you will lead 

Product direction and delivery 

Own product direction, priorities and delivery plans, starting with the decisions leaders need to make. Translate ambiguous needs into clear requirements, testable hypotheses and useful products. Make disciplined choices about what to build, reuse, partner on or stop, balancing business value, feasibility, cost and risk. 

Lead discovery, prototyping, testing and scaling in close partnership with users and technical teams. Establish evidence-based success measures, use feedback to improve the experience and drive adoption beyond initial delivery. Favor reusable capabilities over disconnected one-off solutions, while maintaining clear accountability for product quality and ongoing performance. 

Workforce insight and business impact 

Develop forward-looking insight into workforce supply, demand, skills and capability needs. Bring together internal workforce information and external labor-market trends to support planning, identify capability gaps and inform talent investment and internal mobility decisions. Use forecasting and scenario analysis to help leaders understand uncertainty, options and likely implications. 

Partner with Finance and business leaders to connect workforce choices to capacity, cost and business performance. Build clear measures of value and translate analysis into recommendations and trade-offs, not simply dashboards. Assess whether products improve decisions and deliver meaningful returns on workforce and capability investments. 

Trusted data and responsible use 

Set clear standards for workforce data quality, consistent definitions and skills information in partnership with data and technology teams. Strengthen ownership, governance and ongoing stewardship so products are reliable and maintainable. Embed privacy, security, fairness and appropriate access into product decisions, communicate analytical limitations and preserve human judgment in the use of sensitive employee information. 

Partnership and executive influence 

Align cross-functional partners around shared outcomes, clear ownership and delivery commitments. Resolve dependencies and competing priorities through sound judgment and influence, including where you do not have direct authority. Communicate complex findings and product choices simply and credibly to executives, making assumptions, trade-offs and recommendations explicit. Build the team capabilities and partnerships needed to sustain delivery. 

What you will bring 

A track record of building and scaling data or intelligence products, including taking an ambiguous problem from concept to a working solution. You can demonstrate how you set priorities, translate user needs into requirements and use evidence to guide product decisions and measure adoption and value. 

Substantial experience in workforce strategy, people analytics, talent intelligence or related transformation work, with an understanding of workforce planning and skills or capability insight. Strong analytical judgment and strategic financial acumen, including the ability to evaluate investment, capacity, capability and cost together. 

Technical fluency to work effectively with engineering and data specialists, challenge assumptions and understand data dependencies without relying on a particular platform. Practical experience with data governance, quality and privacy, and sound judgment about the responsible use of employee information. 

A systems perspective, strong executive communication and the ability to build productive relationships across disciplines. You bring clarity to complex problems, influence decisions without relying on formal authority and combine long-term thinking with disciplined delivery. Experience developing teams and partnerships that sustain product adoption and improvement is valuable. 

What success looks like 

Success means leaders use trusted workforce intelligence to make better-informed choices, products move from concept into sustained use, and their value is demonstrated through clear measures. Priorities and accountability are shared across partners; workforce and skills information is more consistent and reliable; and the organization can anticipate capability needs and assess investment options with greater confidence. 

Success Profile  

Successful Workforce Intelligence leaders typically demonstrate:  

  • Product Leadership: Translate ambiguous decision needs into useful products, testing with users and prioritizing adoption and value.  

  • Business Acumen: Balance workforce capacity, capability, cost and performance through disciplined financial trade-offs and measurable business value.  

  • Systems Thinking: Connect business, workforce, skills, data and product dependencies to anticipate capability needs and assess future options.  

  • Analytical Judgment: Use evidence, forecasts and scenarios for credible recommendations, making assumptions, uncertainty and limitations explicit.  

  • Data Stewardship: Ensure reliable data, clear ownership and consistent definitions while protecting privacy, security, fairness and human judgment.  

  • Executive Influence: Communicate findings and product choices clearly, aligning partners and resolving competing priorities without formal authority.  

  • Adaptable Execution: Navigate ambiguity, learn from evidence and feedback, and sustain disciplined delivery, team capability, improvement and adoption.

Business Understanding & Impact 

This role enables Microsoft's Marketing organization to transform raw data into trusted, scalable, AI-ready data products that fuel campaign performance measurement, customer intelligence, audience engagement, revenue growth, and executive decision-making through the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.

  • Review, validate, and govern AI-generated code, infrastructure definitions, documentation, tests, and data transformations to ensure production readiness, performance, security, and maintainability.

Overview

Join the Quality, Reliability, and Telemetry (QRT) team and help reinvent how Windows is tested, validated, and proven across the broader hardware ecosystem. Our charter is to ensure Windows builds and updates land safely, predictably, and at scale across a growing set of third-party OEM, silicon, firmware, driver, and software configurations. 

We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer to lead automation and deep Windows platform quality in the Customer Experience Review (CER) Lab. You will define a productized validation capability for Microsoft labs and third-party partners, including OEM self-assessment, shared automation, repeatable test collateral, and decision-ready reporting. 

You will turn ambiguous ecosystem quality problems into durable architectures, standards, and roadmaps. You will guide engineers through difficult Windows debugging, system internals, driver, reliability, and orchestration challenges while keeping the platform secure, extensible, observable, and practical to operate. 

You will partner with data engineering, data science, and analytics teams to define telemetry and evidence that turns failures into actionable issues. You will establish responsible use of generative AI, agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based workflows while preserving deterministic test execution. 

You will set the technical direction for end-to-end Windows validation across the third-party ecosystem, including: 

• A productized validation platform and OEM self-assessment package that can be deployed, versioned, supported, and measured across Microsoft and partner environments. 

• A common architecture for station control, harnesses, runners, scheduling, device orchestration, and result aggregation. 

• Diagnostics for Windows kernel, driver, firmware, deployment, power, performance, reliability, and cross-layer failures. 

• Evidence pipelines that make results comparable and support release, remediation, prioritization, and investment decisions. 

• AI-assisted capabilities that expand coverage and accelerate analysis without replacing deterministic scenarios or accountable judgment. 

This role is less about owning a single feature and more about creating the technical foundation, operating model, and engineering culture for a validation capability used across the Windows ecosystem. 

• We optimize for early signal, measurable customer outcomes, and clear ownership. 

• We build tools and test products that reduce partner friction rather than add process. 

• We expect principal engineers to lead through influence, make sound decisions under ambiguity, and raise the technical capability of the organization. 

• We are AI-forward, with clear boundaries between deterministic validation and AI-assisted authoring, diagnosis, and operations. 

• We value pragmatic engineering: simple where possible, robust where required, and measurable in production. 

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities

• Lead adoption and extension of the platform, creating reference patterns that work across diverse OEM hardware, silicon, firmware, drivers, and Windows configurations. 

• Drive architecture and design reviews for station control, distributed orchestration, packaging, versioning, security, telemetry, result services, and partner integration. 

• Resolve systemic and high-severity technical problems through deep Windows debugging, kernel and system internals analysis, driver diagnostics, and cross-layer root-cause investigation. 

• Establish engineering standards for reliability, security, privacy, observability, supportability, test determinism, and operational excellence. 

• Partner with data engineering, data science, and analytics leaders to define trustworthy schemas, signals, quality bars, and decision-ready reporting. 

• Set the strategy and guardrails for AI-assisted test authoring, anomaly detection, failure classification, log analysis, bug filing, and developer workflows. 

• Influence and align WSSI, WSD, WECE, Surface, Windows engineering, Selfhost, Fundamentals, AppCompat, and OEM partners on requirements, interfaces, and success measures. 

• Mentor senior and early-in-career engineers, create technical growth opportunities, and raise the bar for design quality, code quality, debugging depth, and end-to-end ownership. 

• Use architecture, technical judgment, and measurable outcomes to guide quarterly planning, investment tradeoffs, and prioritization across multiple workstreams.

    • OR equivalent experience.

• Experience productizing and operating packaged test collateral, lab automation, or self-service validation capabilities at scale. 

• Experience defining architecture and operational standards for device orchestration, telemetry, logging, tracing, result aggregation, security, and reliability.

MCAPS-Core accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. We differentiate through value creation - delivering world-class, AI-powered customer experiences that accelerate adoption, strengthen loyalty, and create sustainable competitive advantage, driving growth that outpaces the market.

Within MCAPS - Core, the Customer Service & Support (CSS) organization builds trust and confidence for every person and organization through delivering a seamless support experience. In CSS, we are powered by Microsoft’s AI technology to help consumers, businesses, partners, and more, resolve their issues quickly and securely, helping prevent future problems from occurring and achieving more from their Microsoft investment.

Microsoft’s SCIM organization is seeking a Principal Software AI Engineer to lead the architecture, development, and production deployment of agentic AI solutions that transform support experiences. This is a hands-on technical leadership role for an engineer who can solve ambiguous, high-impact problems; set engineering direction; and translate support experience intent and readiness requirements into secure, reliable, and scalable AI systems.
You will combine deep software engineering expertise with applied AI judgment to build diagnostics, workflows, evaluation frameworks, and tooling that improve how support teams and customers resolve complex issues. You will work across engineering, product, program management, data, security, Responsible AI, and frontline support teams, influencing technical strategy while remaining close to implementation.

This role is suited to a principal-level engineer who combines strategic influence with deep hands-on execution. The ideal candidate is energized by ambiguous problems, makes sound architectural tradeoffs, learns rapidly as AI technologies evolve, and maintains a high bar for customer impact and operational excellence.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

  • Validate quality and readiness. Evaluate groundedness, accuracy, task completion, robustness, latency, cost, safety, and failure modes at each deployment milestone in partnership with TPMs and support-domain experts.

  • Hands-on experience building applied AI systems, including generative AI, large language models, or autonomous agents.

  • Strong proficiency in one or more modern programming languages, with the ability to contribute directly to production code; experience with Python is highly relevant.

Overview
As a Data Center Technician (DCT), you will demonstrate expertise in standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning equipment, as well as a holistic understanding of the functions of, and interactions between, network and server equipment. You will provide input for suggested modifications to these processes and procedures as needed to improve service quality and efficiency while providing guidance to other technicians.
 
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
 
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
 
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
 
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays. 
 
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties 
 


Responsibilities
Datacenter Operations
  • Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.
  • Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type with guidance from experienced technicians. Seeks guidance from more experienced technicians on challenging or complex tickets.
  • Receives guidance and supervision to develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Develops and acquires a fundamental understanding of the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment.
  • Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.
Datacenter Work Environment
  • Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
  • Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work. Encourages providing and responding to feedback received on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams
  • Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or established reporting methods.
  • Participates in daily safety briefings. Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, complies with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), completes required Task Hazard Analysis (THAs), and uses appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, taking proactive action to alert others of safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in regular cadence proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.
  • Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
  • Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Managing Service
  • Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
  • Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
  • Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
Service Delivery
  • Develops an understanding of effective execution order strategy(ies) for assigned tasks with assistance from experienced technicians or direct-line management. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.
  • Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.
  • Directly performs decommissions, simple changes (e.g., memory upgrades, OS rebuilds) and refreshes of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, and server equipment, following standard procedures whilst seeking clarification and guidance from more experienced technicians as needed. Processes data-bearing devices (DBDs) for destruction or confirms any-and-all such devices (e.g. hard-drives, solid-state drives, flash cards, etc.) contained within network, storage, or server equipment has been identified for eradication or destruction with guidance.
  • Performs basic diagnostics and troubleshooting with guidance from experienced technicians and/or via standard procedures to identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Develops awareness of conditions, circumstances, and scenarios which may reflect significant customer or business impact within the Data Center environment.
  • Learns about post-execution verification of grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling to align with all safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Templates (NDTs). Learns about errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and escalates to relevant technicians or specialists to coordinate corrections as needed.
Working Conditions
  • Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Other
  • Embody our culture and values 


Qualifications
Required Qualifications
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
  • This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components AND 3+ years experience supporting IT equipment or related technology OR equivalent experience.

Overview

Microsoft is seeking a Program Manager to serve as the on-site representative of Microsoft engineering to a strategic government partner. The role exists because what matters most in this partnership cannot be learned at a distance: what the partner needs and what it will need next surface in hallways, in after-action reviews, and in the ordinary course of a workday spent alongside its people.

You will therefore work from the partner's site five days a week, and you will own the rhythm of business that keeps our Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) healthy — coordinating across internal and external stakeholders to schedule, plan, and execute the meetings and decision forums the partnership depends on. 

While approximately 95% of the role follows a predictable schedule, there are occasional periods when the organization shifts into crisis-response mode and requires extended support. During these infrequent events, flexibility and a willingness to support mission-critical activities outside of standard working hours are important. 
 


Responsibilities
The work follows a straightforward mission: identify partner needs, translate those needs into actionable requirements, and help deliver capabilities that make a real impact.  At any given time, you will guide multiple efforts through that lifecycle, helping each move forward while building trusted relationships across Microsoft and our partner organization.
 
A significant part of the role focuses on customer requirements discovery. Using a user-centered and human-centered design framework, you will work closely with users to understand their environment, challenges, and goals. Through interviews, structured observation, and day-to-day engagement, you will identify who the users are, how they operate, what capabilities they need, and why those needs matter. You will then translate those insights into clear technical requirements that engineering teams can build against. As you develop a deep understanding of partner priorities, you will maintain a living body of knowledge that helps shape future innovation and informs strategic decision-making.

Where a documented requirement meets a partner need, addresses a gap in the market, and draws on a Microsoft core competency, it becomes a candidate for an Individual Work Plan (IWP) — the vehicle through which this partnership turns a requirement into committed, funded work. Beyond requirements discovery, you will help drive a portfolio of IWPs from concept through delivery.  The CRADA governs the broader relationship between Microsoft and the partner; IWPs nest beneath it and define the specific work and its scope. You will run a portfolio of IWPs at once — translating qualified requirements into IWP form, shepherding each through Microsoft's internal approval process, and, once approved, project managing it from creation through completion: standing up execution, sequencing dependencies, tracking progress and risk, and seeing the resulting capability through to delivery and adoption. 

 
Success in this role comes from collaboration. You will work across Microsoft business units, including engineering, legal, trade compliance, finance, and security, to align priorities, remove obstacles, and ensure successful outcomes. You will also play a key role in sustaining the long-term health of the partnership, including leading the CRADA renewal process during its five-year lifecycle. 
 
Communication is woven throughout every aspect of the role. You will synthesize partner feedback, emerging requirements, market opportunities, sources of friction, and urgent needs into clear, actionable insights for executive leaders. Whether communicating through written reports, presentations, or in-person discussions, you will help ensure leaders have the context they need to make informed decisions and respond quickly when priorities evolve.  Done well, this role places you at the center of a unique strategic partnership, where your ability to connect customer needs with Microsoft's expertise directly influences the capabilities we build, the value we deliver, and the strength of a relationship that drives innovation forward.

At Microsoft, our mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. The next decade of cloud computing and artificial intelligence will require breakthroughs not only in compute and software, but also in the physical infrastructure that connects datacenters, regions and customers worldwide. Azure Fiber is developing transformative hollow-core fiber technology that is already being deployed and operationalized across the Azure Network. This is groundbreaking technology that is redefining the performance, efficiency and scale of future Azure infrastructure.

Azure Fiber’s Hollow-core fiber has demonstrated compelling performance advantages in networks across all the early field deployments and currently carries production traffic across Azure regions. The remaining challenge is deploying this technology at scale into the production infrastructure. High density cables for Metro, Long Haul and Submarine requirements will come with new challenges to the cable design that have never been seen before. As the Senior Cloud Network Engineer for HCF Cable Development, you will be part of a team owning significant technical problems, define engineering approaches and deliver cable technologies that improve the performance, reliability, scalability and cost effectiveness of Microsoft’s global network.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Drive cable product development of new fiber-optic cable products for Metro, Long Haul and Submarine applications, translating network and fiber requirements into practical, manufacturable cable designs.
  • Develop and evaluate cable architectures, materials and designs against optical, mechanical, environmental, reliability, deployment, manufacturability, supply-chain and cost requirements. Identify technical trade-offs, quantify risks and recommend solutions that meet end-to-end Azure network needs.
  • Lead prototype builds, engineering trials and qualification activities. Define test plans and acceptance criteria, analyze results and drive design improvements through to qualification. Work closely with cable manufacturers and suppliers to transition new designs from engineering development into repeatable, production-ready products.
  • Independently investigate and resolve complex cable design, manufacturing, qualification and deployment issues using engineering analysis, testing and structured root-cause analysis.
  • Ensure cable products are suitable for real-world Azure deployments, considering installation methods, duct infrastructure, handling, jointing, environmental conditions and operational requirements.
  • Set technical direction with cable manufacturers and technology partners, evaluate supplier designs and manufacturing capabilities, make evidence-based technical recommendations, and influence partner roadmaps and investment decisions to resolve issues and meet Azure requirements.
  • Develop and maintain engineering specifications, product requirements, qualification plans, design documentation and technical reports, working across fiber development, optical engineering, network architecture, deployment, operations and supply chain teams to ensure cable solutions meet end-to-end network requirements.

Required Qualifications:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND technical experience in network design and development OR equivalent experience
  • Experience developing and qualifying fibre-optic cables, telecommunications infrastructure or comparable physical network products, including ownership of complex technical work across design, manufacturing, product lifecycle management and deployment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience delivering network designs into production and experience with live site accountability for a network.
  • Experience of managing manufacturing partners,
  • Experience working with vendors or optical suppliers on multi-year roadmaps.
  • Evidence of technical leadership at senior individual-contributor level: creating clarity in ambiguous problems, setting technical direction, influencing stakeholders, reviewing designs and mentoring other engineers. 

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role.

Substrate services operate at global scale and are designed to deliver high availability, reliability, and security for some of the world’s most demanding workloads. 

As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer, you will lead reliability improvements across multiple services or components, solving complex, cross-cutting operational problems. You are recognized as a subject matter expert in your area and lead by example through strong technical judgment, ownership, and accountability. 

You will influence service architecture, define reliability strategies, mentor other SREs, and drive meaningful reductions in incidents, toil, and operational risk—particularly for services operating in regulated, sovereign, or compliance-sensitive environments.

  • Drive high-quality post-incident reviews that identify systemic issues and result in durable engineering improvements. 

  • Drive automation, monitoring, and observability strategies to reduce incident volume and mean time to recovery.

If you are excited by the opportunity to shape how Microsoft plans for hundreds of billions of dollars in commercial business, this role offers a unique seat at the center of that process.

 

The Microsoft Customer and Partner Solutions (MCAPS) Finance team is looking for a Senior Finance Manager to lead Reporting & Analytics for the Central Revenue Planning team. Working across Microsoft’s commercial portfolio, our team translates growth ambitions into the targets and budgets that guide business and sales organizations around the world.

 

Our highly visible team is on a mission to transform revenue planning, making it simpler, more efficient, more insightful, and increasingly enabled by technology, automation, and AI.

 

As our Reporting & Analytics lead, you will shape the data, analytics, and reporting foundation behind revenue planning and budget setting. You will lead the evolution of our reporting ecosystem, including Power BI solutions, Excel analytics, and executive presentations that enable hundreds of Finance and business stakeholders to make better, faster decisions.

 

Beyond reporting, you will be a key analytical thought partner, helping uncover budget drivers and identify pockets of risk and opportunity across the business. This is a unique opportunity to reimagine historically complex and manual processes through data, technology, automation, and AI, creating solutions that can unlock impact for hundreds of people across the company.

 

What We Value

We are looking for someone who combines strong financial and analytical capabilities with the curiosity and leadership to challenge how things have traditionally been done.

You will thrive in this role if you bring:

•             Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with complex datasets and translate them into meaningful business insights.

•             Strong data and reporting capabilities, with an understanding of how to design effective analytical experiences and decision-support solutions.

•             AI, automation, or technology fluency, along with excitement about using emerging capabilities to transform Finance processes.

•             Strong cross-team partnership, with the ability to influence and bring together stakeholders across Finance, Engineering, Sales, and business organizations.

•             Excellent communication and executive presence, with the ability to turn complexity into clear, compelling narratives for senior leaders.

•             A growth mindset and change orientation, with a desire to continuously improve processes, challenge the status quo, and deliver meaningful impact at scale.

 Lead Reporting & Analytics for Central Revenue Planning, shaping the reporting strategy, data foundation, analytics, and executive views supporting Microsoft's commercial revenue planning process.

•  Translate complex planning data into clear executive insights and narratives that help corporate, field sales, and Finance leaders understand our growth ambitions and make informed decisions.
