Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for passionate engineers to help achieve that mission. 

  

As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and hardware infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the Cloud Hardware Systems Engineering (CHSE) team is instrumental in defining and delivering operational measures of success for hardware manufacturing, improving the planning process, quality, delivery, scale and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware. We are looking for engineers with a dedicated passion for customer focused solutions, insight and industry knowledge to envision and implement future technical solutions that will manage and optimize the Cloud infrastructure.  

We are looking for a Principal Hardware Engineer - Networking to serve as a technical leader for complex network switch platforms for Microsoft Azure AI infrastructure. This role will define multi-generation platform strategy and drive execution from requirements and architecture through board design, system integration, validation, manufacturing, and deployment. The ideal candidate will combine deep electrical engineering expertise with architectural judgment, cross-organization influence, supplier leadership, and the ability to turn ambiguous infrastructure needs into scalable platform solutions. 

 

#SCHIE #azurehwjobs #CHSE 



Responsibilities

  • Define and drive the multi-generation electrical and system architecture roadmap for custom network switch platforms supporting Azure AI infrastructure, including technology insertion, platform reuse, risk retirement, and lifecycle strategy. 

  • Own platform-level requirements decomposition and architectural tradeoffs spanning network, rack, performance, reliability, availability, serviceability, security, telemetry, manufacturing, cost, and schedule. 

  • Provide technical authority for switch ASIC, control-plane CPU, BMC, CPLD/FPGA, clocking, reset, power delivery, high-speed Ethernet, retimers, optical modules, cable backplanes, telemetry, and platform-management interfaces. 

  • Lead architecture and design reviews across schematic, PCB stack-up, signal integrity, power integrity, layout, BOM, component derating, DFT, DFM, DFR, and system integration; establish decision criteria and drive closure of cross-disciplinary issues. 

  • Establish platform bring-up, electrical validation, margining, interoperability, stress, reliability, and production-test strategies; ensure evidence-based exit criteria and scalable test coverage across development phases. 

  • Lead resolution of the most complex board-, system-, rack-, manufacturing-, and field-level issues by organizing cross-team debug, forming hypotheses from data, and driving verified corrective actions and prevention mechanisms. 

  • Provide technical direction to ODM/OEM and technology partners; define deliverables, design-review criteria, quality expectations, and escalation paths while influencing supplier roadmaps and execution. 

  • Mentor senior engineers, raise engineering standards, and build reusable specifications, design guides, validation methods, reference architectures, and lessons learned across network-switch programs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field and 10+ years of technical engineering experience, or equivalent experience. 

  • 10+ years of experience designing and delivering board- or system-level hardware for networking, compute, storage, accelerator, or datacenter products across the hardware development lifecycle. 

  • Experience leading architecture, requirements, design reviews, bring-up, validation, root-cause debug, and production readiness for complex hardware platforms. 

  • Experience developing high-speed serial and high-current power-delivery hardware and leading execution across electrical, firmware, mechanical, thermal, SI/PI, validation, manufacturing, and system-integration disciplines. 

  • Experience providing technical leadership across internal organizations and external ODM/OEM, silicon, component, or manufacturing partners. 

  • Proven ability to identify architectural and execution risks, frame system tradeoffs, and drive decisions across performance, reliability, cost, schedule, and long-term platform value. 

  • Experience architecting merchant-silicon Ethernet switch platforms for AI, cloud, hyperscale, or datacenter infrastructure. 

  • Deep experience with switch ASIC, CPU, BMC, CPLD/FPGA, clocking, reset, power-delivery, telemetry, and hardware-management architectures. 

  • Experience with 112G/224G PAM4, high-speed connectors, cable backplanes, retimers, pluggable optical modules, and end-to-end channel-budget tradeoffs. 

  • Experience with SONiC hardware enablement, platform APIs, firmware interfaces, and switch-platform management. 

  • Demonstrated ability to assess SI/PI analyses, PCB and package constraints, PDN behavior, power transients, thermal interactions, and laboratory correlation data. 

  • Experience delivering hardware through architecture, EVT, DVT, PVT, production qualification, and high-volume manufacturing. 

  • Experience defining supplier strategy, influencing technology roadmaps, and leading ODM/OEM execution across multiple concurrent programs. 

  • Proven technical communication, specification writing, executive-level decision framing, mentoring, and cross-organization influence.

As a Data Center Technician (DCT), you will demonstrate expertise in standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning equipment, as well as a holistic understanding of the functions of, and interactions between, network and server equipment. You will provide input for suggested modifications to these processes and procedures as needed to improve service quality and efficiency while providing guidance to other technicians.
 
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
 
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
 
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
 
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.

  • Demonstrates an applied understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment.   • Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites.   • Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
  • Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work.   • Participates in daily safety briefings.   • Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
  • Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
  • Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
Service Delivery
  • Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.
  • Develops and employs an effective execution order strategy for assigned tasks. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.
  • Performs diagnostics and troubleshooting and/or leverages standard procedures to quickly and efficiently identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Our shared services turn Microsoft 365 knowledge into trusted, permission-aware evidence through indexing, retrieval and ranking, and grounding. Product teams across Microsoft consume them through Microsoft Graph and Work IQ, and relevance teams ship quality on top of them. Every Copilot answer, search result, and agent action is only as good as the evidence behind it, so our job is to make every quality gain land faster, cheaper, and everywhere, and to prove it with data everyone trusts. 

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager on the Enterprise Search and Grounding Platform team to drive strategy and execution to deliver Copilot and Agents quality gains.  

This position is based in Redmond, Washington and requires the employee be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week.

The strategy 

  • Define the vision, multi-year roadmap, and success metrics for the Developer Experience pillar, anchored on the Search Platform north star: one trusted platform, tuned by scenario, with recall-forward, low-latency retrieval for agents. 

  • Own product definition for the developer-facing API surface, including the next major version of our core retrieval API and the Work IQ and Retrieval API integration patterns, with a bias toward stable, scenario-agnostic contracts that outlive any single experience. 

  • Decide what the platform should offer as a shared capability and what stays with individual agent teams, and drive the consolidation of bespoke integrations onto supported patterns. 

Make the platform easy to build on 

  • Design the onboarding path for a new agent team, from first call to production: reference integrations, documentation, samples, and self-serve tooling that remove the need for a bespoke engagement. 

  • Treat debuggability as a product requirement. Specify the observability, tracing, and diagnostics developers need to understand why a query returned what it did and to fix issues without escalating to the platform team. 

  • Translate agent needs into platform requirements for recall, latency budgets, and evidence formats, working with the Quality Improvements and Frontier Platform Innovation pillars so that recall-forward retrieval tuned for agents ships as part of the core platform. 

Lead across the organization 

  • Author crisp specs, requirements documents, and program plans; drive execution across multiple engineering teams and owners; and communicate status, risks, and trade-offs clearly to leadership. 

  • Represent Search Platform developer experience with senior stakeholders across Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Graph, Work IQ, and partner organizations, landing decisions and aligning roadmaps.

  • Serve as final decision authority for investigative disposition in assigned cases

  • Ensure consistent application of:

    • Cross-team operational discipline

D365 Contact Center is a robust application that extends the power of CRM’s like Dynamics 365 Customer Service to enable organizations to instantly connect and engage with their customers via channels like Live Chat, Voice, and SMS.  

As a Principal Software Engineer in the Microsoft Dynamics Customer Experience Applications team, you will provide technical leadership for the architecture, design, implementation, and operation of intelligent capabilities within Dynamics 365 Contact Center. You will solve ambiguous, high-impact engineering problems spanning distributed cloud services, applied AI, data, security, and reliability. You will set technical direction, align partner teams, and lead delivery of secure, scalable, production-ready systems that create measurable customer and business impact.

 
We innovate quickly and collaborate closely with our partners and customers in a very agile environment. If the opportunity to collaborate with a diverse engineering team, on enabling end-to-end business scenarios using cutting-edge AI first technologies and to solve problems for large scale 24x7 business SaaS applications excite you, we would love to talk to you!

As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

 

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft is on a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Our culture is centred on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world. You can help us achieve our mission. 
Do you want to work in a company that is transforming the world? How about working on cutting-edge issues, with world class clients and the support of a global community of professionals? If you are ready to work directly with business leaders and their teams to solve problems and drive change, then a career with the Microsoft National Security Team is for you.
 
The UK National Security Team (NST) is a small, high-impact group of security experts working at the intersection of compliance, technology, policy and business strategy. NST partners closely with sales, engineering, legal and business leaders to enable Microsoft’s most strategic customer opportunities while managing regulatory and reputational risk.
We have an immediate opening for a highly motivated and experienced Information Security Manager to join the NST, which sits within the UK & Ireland Legal Affairs team and National Security Team, and supports compliance with government personnel, project, information and facility-security requirements.  The position is based at our offices in Reading and will report to a Principal Corporate Counsel in Legal Affairs. 
Role Purpose:
 
The Information Security Manager is responsible for information security governance, assurance and operational security support across Microsoft UK Public Safety and National Security activities. The role helps ensure compliance with UK Government security policy, contractual obligations and customer security requirements.
The post holder acts as a trusted information security adviser to programme teams, engineering, sales, legal, security stakeholders and leadership. They translate complex regulatory and contractual security requirements into practical controls that enable secure, compliant delivery throughout the programme lifecycle.
A key priority is identifying security requirements early and reducing avoidable delivery friction without weakening compliance. This work supports customer confidence, programme delivery and revenue realisation by reducing the risk of contractual breaches, accreditation delays, security incidents and unplanned remediation.


Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities - Information Security Governance & Policy
 
  • Define, maintain and implement information and operational security policies, standards and procedures aligned with UK Government policy, Microsoft requirements and contractual obligations.
  • Act as a subject matter expert on information security governance for UK national security programmes.
  • Translate government and customer security requirements into scalable, operationally workable controls.
  • Provide independent advice and constructive challenge where security, contractual or compliance obligations may be at risk.
  • Support audits, inspections, assurance reviews and customer accreditation activity.
  • Maintain awareness of evolving UK Government security policy, regulation and the national security threat landscape.

 

Programme Security Governance & Assurance
  • Provide information security leadership across the programme lifecycle, from early engagement and tenders through delivery and operation.
  • Work with programme management and engineering teams to embed security in programme design and delivery.
  • Review and interpret Security Aspects Letters, Security Grading Guides, contractual security schedules and security flow-down requirements.
  • Support the development and maintenance of Security Management Plans, procedures and assurance documentation.
  • Help establish or participate in customer and programme Security Working Groups.
  • Ensure information security risks are identified, documented, reviewed and escalated through appropriate governance.

 

Contract Security:
  • Engage with sales, account and bid teams to identify security requirements early.
  • Review relevant DEFCON, Defence Standard and customer-specific security requirements.
  • Advise on security obligations within Statements of Work and related contractual documents.
  • Identify delivery and compliance risks associated with proposed commitments or solutions.
  • Support customer discussions where security requirements require clarification or negotiation.
  • Ensure agreed security requirements transition effectively into programme delivery.

 

Information Security Risk Management:
  • Support security risk assessments across UK national security programmes.
  • Review programme risk registers and evaluate the effectiveness of proposed mitigations.
  • Ensure significant security risks are escalated to the appropriate risk owner or governance body.
  • Provide information security assurance to programme leadership and senior stakeholders.
  • Support remediation, assurance assessments, accreditation reviews and security testing.
  • Monitor recurring issues and identify opportunities to improve controls, processes and programme security maturity.
  • Promote consistent, evidence-based security risk management across programmes.

 

Information Protection & Secure Collaboration:
  • Provide guidance on the handling, storage, sharing, transfer, retention and disposal of sensitive information.
  • Advise on the suitability of Microsoft tooling and collaboration environments for sensitive programme activity.
  • Support secure document management and customer-specific information handling requirements.
  • Advise on restricted collaboration environments, ethical firewalls and information-separation controls.
  • Help ensure sensitive information is handled in line with contractual and government requirements and need-to-know principles

 

Security Incident Management:
  • Provide information security advice and support during security incidents affecting relevant programmes.
  • Ensure potential incidents are identified, recorded and escalated appropriately.
  • Support proportionate, independent incident investigations where required.
  • Assess security, customer and contractual implications.
  • Recommend containment, remediation and risk-reduction actions.
  • Produce or support incident reports and after-action reviews.
  • Ensure lessons learned are reflected in programme controls, guidance and training.

 

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement:
  • Act as an information security point of contact for UK national security programmes.
  • Build trusted relationships with programme teams, Engineering, Sales, Legal and Microsoft security stakeholders.
  • Engage with UK Government, defence and national security customers on security assurance and compliance matters.
  • Represent Microsoft at Security Working Groups, assurance meetings and security governance forums.
  • Develop security briefings for programme leadership, senior executives and customers.
  • Communicate complex security risks and requirements clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Promote security as a practical business enabler.
Other areas: 
  • Develop positive relationships with legal colleagues within the UK & Ireland Legal Affairs team, with UK government affairs colleagues and with colleagues in the wider EMEA region to coach and advise on compliance issues.
  • Engage with legal and business colleagues to identify and share best practices.
  • Support programme-specific security briefings, training and awareness material.
  • Support and collaborate with NST Personnel Security Controller and Facility Manager.
  • Develop positive relationships with customers, and partners to protect and advocate for Microsoft’s interests.
  • Collaborate with service providers to develop strategies and innovative solutions to address business issues and achieve business objectives.
  • Some knowledge of Defence exports compliance issues would be an advantage but not essential. The role includes support to project teams and liaison with Microsoft’s international trade specialists on matters involving US and other applicable export-control regimes.
  • Identify gaps and inefficiencies in security processes and lead proportionate improvements
  • Use AI solutions to scale work and drive continuous improvement.
  • Monitor emerging risks, policy developments and operational security trends.

 

Attendance at our Reading offices as required.
International travel will be required from time to time.


Qualifications
Required qualifications:
 
  • Demonstrable experience in information security, operational security, programme security or a government security role. 
  • The successful candidate is a sole UK National and hold, or be able to obtain and maintain, the UK Government security clearance required for the role (DV). 
  • Knowledge of UK Government security policy, security controls and government information handling requirements. 
  • Demonstrable experience supporting large, complex programmes for UK Government, defence or national security customers.

 

Preferred qualifications:
 
  • Experience interpreting contractual security requirements and translating them into practical operational controls.
  • Experience managing information security risk, assurance or accreditation activities.
  • Stakeholder-management skills, including engagement with leaders, customers and multidisciplinary delivery teams and ability to  establish a “trusted advisor” relationship.
  • An ability to work independently while also being a collaborator with the ability to work with colleagues based in different locations.
  • A high tolerance for ambiguity and change.
  • Passion for technology, the potential of digital transformation and Microsoft’s diverse range of products and services

Overview

The CSAM (IC1) is an early-in-career Customer Success Account Manager who supports the delivery of standardised customer success activities across Customer Health, Cloud Adoption, AI Transformation and Unified Success.  

Working alongside more experienced CSAMs who lead executive customer relationships and overall account strategy, the CSAM IC1 contributes to the successful execution and orchestration of agreed customer success priorities and activities.  

Reporting to an M1 Manager, the CSAM IC1 operates as part of a defined pod or industry team supporting a shared portfolio of customers. The role provides an opportunity to build customer success capability and experience while contributing to measurable customer outcomes across Customer Health, accelerating Cloud Adoption, AI Transformation, and the health and growth of customers’ Unified Success engagements. 

 



Responsibilities
 
 

Success Plan Execution 

  • Customer Success Planning: Support customers across three core Customer Success Plan priorities: Customer Health, Cloud Acceleration and AI Transformation. The scope and depth of each plan will vary according to the customer’s needs, priorities and maturity. 

  • Plan Execution and Co-ordination: Support the execution, co-ordination and ongoing management of activities within Customer Success Plans, working under the guidance of experienced CSAMs and management. 

  • Delivery Excellence: Complete assigned activities accurately and within agreed timescales, proactively raising risks, blockers or exceptions and seeking appropriate guidance where required. 

  • Milestone and Delivery Tracking: Support experienced CSAMs in tracking delivery progress, milestones, insights and actions across engagements involving ISD, partners, CSAs and other members of the customer virtual team. 

  • Virtual Team Orchestration: Help co-ordinate and bring together relevant virtual teams to maintain alignment, address customer health concerns and support remediation or acceleration activities. 

  • Progressive Unified Ownership: As capability and experience develop, the CSAM will take increasing ownership of Unified activities, including bookings, scoping conversations and value capture. The expectation is that, by approximately three months in role, the CSAM will begin to take a more leading role in these activities with appropriate support and guidance 

Portfolio-level intelligence and preparation 

  • AI-Powered Account Insights: Leverage AI and available account signals to identify and summarise actionable insights to experienced CSAMs. 

  • Delivery and Milestone Visibility: Maintain visibility of upcoming customer deliveries, including resourcing, bookings, scoping activities and key milestones. Ensure relevant account information and progress updates are accurately captured and maintained. 

  • Develop Account Understanding: Build knowledge and context across the assigned customer portfolio over time, enabling increasingly valuable insights and recommendations to support customer success priorities. 

  • Customer Meeting Planning: Apply a strong, structured planning approach to support experienced CSAMs in preparing for customer meetings. 

  • Identify Trends and Themes: Analyse information across the portfolio to highlight recurring themes, risks, blockers or opportunities that may require remediation, escalation or acceleration. 

  • Progressive Customer Engagement: Support the preparation of customer meetings through relevant insights and materials. As capability and experience develop, and under the guidance of an experienced CSAM, take increasing ownership of defined customer-facing activities, such as standard scoping calls and delivery of standard customer presentations. 

  • Customer Success Insights: Consolidate relevant data and insights to support customer conversations across the core Customer Success Plan priorities:  

  • Customer Health: product retirements, service alerts and relevant reactive insights. 

  • Cloud Acceleration: delivery progress, milestones, identify risks and acceleration opportunities. 

  • AI Transformation: programme updates, adoption and usage insights, and progress against agreed AI priorities. 

 

Operating model 

  • The CSAM will work across a defined portfolio of customer accounts, aligned where possible by industry and team, providing the opportunity to progressively build industry expertise and a strong understanding of customer priorities. 

  • Reporting to an M1 Manager, the CSAM will receive ongoing guidance, coaching and support as they build their customer success capabilities and take on increasing responsibility. 

  • The role will work in partnership with experienced CSAMs who retain ownership of customer strategy and key customer relationships. Depending on the portfolio, the CSAM may partner with several experienced CSAMs, providing exposure to different customers, scenarios and approaches while developing towards greater ownership over time. 

Example Activities 

Activities below are illustrative, not exhaustive.  

Strengthen Customer Health 

  • Maintain a clear view of high-priority customer health recommendations across the aligned portfolio, identifying key offerings that can support agreed follow-up actions. 

  • Consolidate insights and prepare materials to support customer health conversations and meetings  

  • Maintain awareness of priority product retirements, end-of-support considerations and associated risks across the portfolio, together with the relevant customer follow-up actions and available offerings. 

  • Synthesise incident and service information to identify recurring patterns, themes and potential systemic drivers 

  • Support preparation for internal and customer-facing Customer Health plan reviews, ensuring plans, insights, recommendations and actions are accurate and up to date. 

Accelerate Cloud Adoption 

  • Support the tracking of Unified deliveries and associated customer value, maintaining visibility of progress, actions and outcomes. 

  • Track customer milestones, maintain accurate milestone notes and work with experienced CSAMs to ensure appropriate MSX data quality and hygiene. 

  • Where agreed with the experienced CSAM, proactively gather insights and progress updates from delivery partners, CSAs and other virtual team members relating to deliveries, milestones and Customer Success Plan activities. 

  • Consolidate delivery and milestone insights to support internal and customer-facing Cloud Acceleration plan reviews, highlighting progress, risks, blockers and areas requiring action. 

Advance AI Transformation 

  • Support the tracking of AI Transformation milestones and agreed activities, maintaining accurate and timely updates and working with experienced CSAMs to ensure appropriate MSX data quality and hygiene. 

  • Gather relevant insights and progress updates from delivery partners, CSAs and other virtual team members to provide visibility of progress against agreed AI Transformation priorities. 

  • Consolidate programme, adoption and milestone insights to support AI Transformation plan reviews and customer conversations. 

  • Support preparation for internal and customer-facing meetings, ensuring relevant progress, insights, risks and agreed next actions are clearly represented. 

Unified Growth and Health 

  • Develop the capability to independently manage standard Unified operational activities, including submitting resource booking requests, dispatching Success Programmes and supporting scoping activities. 

  • Within approximately three months, and subject to appropriate experience and readiness, take increasing ownership of standard scoping calls, clearly capturing customer objectives, intended outcomes and value. 

  • Support the proactive management of Unified consumption and contract health, working with experienced CSAMs and relevant teams to address areas such as over-consumption, package utilisation and SKU changes to maximise customer value and support RBI attainment. 

  • Capture and maintain evidence of the value delivered through Unified, ensuring outcomes and supporting evidence are accurately recorded. 

  • Consolidate Unified value and outcome insights into clear materials that support executive-level customer value conversations, working alongside experienced CSAMs. 



Qualifications

Required 

  • Bachelor’s degree in any discipline, or equivalent relevant experience gained through employment, apprenticeships, internships or other early-career pathways. 

  • Legally authorised to work in the United Kingdom to be eligible for this role (Legally authorised = has citizenship or has been granted a valid visa or work permit)

  • Typically, 2 years of professional experience, which may include customer-facing roles, programme or project management, technology delivery, or other relevant experience. 

  • Demonstrated confidence in using AI tools and AI-first ways of working to support productivity, insight generation, communication and day-to-day activities. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to communicate clearly and confidently with a range of stakeholders. 

  • Effective presentation and collaboration skills, with a willingness to learn, seek feedback and build confidence in customer-facing environments. 

Preferred 

  • Coursework, qualifications or practical experience in programme or project management, business operations, customer success or sales.  

  • Exposure to enterprise technology or software solutions, cloud platforms, customer success, or large-scale technology and transformation programmes. 

  • Experience working collaboratively across cross-functional or matrixed teams, bringing together different stakeholders to support shared priorities and outcomes. 

What Success Looks Like in Year One 

  • Develop towards customer-facing responsibility within the first three months, initially leading defined activities such as standard scoping calls, and progressively taking ownership of standardised customer presentations and conversations. 

  • Within the first year, build strong customer and portfolio knowledge and demonstrate readiness to independently own a broader range of internal and customer-facing activities. 

  • Consistently deliver accurate, timely and high-quality contributions across Customer Success Plans, milestone and activity management, insights and customer meeting preparation. 

  • Demonstrates measurable contribution to customer success by helping accelerate key KPIs and drive progress against the priority success metrics for the assigned customer portfolio

Role Purpose

The Sr Construction Project Engineer – MEP provides site-based project engineering support while contributing to the APAC CE&I regional support network. The role is grounded in electrical engineering and extends across mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems, including interfaces with controls, life safety systems, construction delivery and commissioning.

The role supports project teams in resolving multidisciplinary engineering and commissioning issues, assessing compliance with approved design requirements and Microsoft standards and translating project experience into practical improvements through root cause analysis, lessons learnt and technical guidance.

Operating Context

The Sr Construction Project Engineer – MEP focused on assigned project and site delivery responsibilities while supporting regional activities when specialist input or coordinated MEP review is required. The role works collaboratively with project delivery teams, design and engineering stakeholders, commissioning teams, contractors, consultants and the APAC CE&I network. Matters requiring final design authority are escalated through the appropriate engineering governance pathway.



Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

1. Project Delivery and Site Engineering

  • Provide practical engineering support throughout construction, testing, commissioning and project close-out.
  • Review MEP installation issues, technical queries, RFIs, submittals, design changes and field conditions.
  • Assess whether proposed solutions align with approved design documentation, specifications, safety requirements and project objectives.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary interfaces to identify gaps, clashes, sequencing constraints and system integration risks.
  • Support resolution of site issues without displacing the accountability of the responsible designer, contractor or project delivery team.
  • Monitor closure of assigned technical actions and verify that agreed outcomes are reflected in field execution and project records.

2. MEP Technical Assurance

  • Apply strong electrical engineering judgement while reviewing the wider MEP system and its interfaces.
  • Support technical reviews and project assessments across electrical, mechanical, plumbing, controls, fire and life safety systems as applicable.
  • Identify non-compliance, deviations, design gaps, scope gaps, constructability concerns and risks to operability or maintainability.
  • Provide clear, evidence-based recommendations and escalate issues requiring specialist or final engineering authority.
  • Promote consistent interpretation and implementation of approved requirements across APAC projects while recognising local regulatory obligations.

3. Commissioning Support

  • Support commissioning readiness reviews, system turnover, pre-functional checks, functional testing and integrated systems testing activities.
  • Investigate commissioning failures, repeated test issues, equipment performance concerns and MEP system interface problems.
  • Work with construction, commissioning, design, vendor and operations stakeholders to establish safe and technically sound recovery actions.
  • Confirm that commissioning issues are documented, assigned and tracked to an evidence-based closure.
  • Identify recurring commissioning constraints and recommend improvements to procedures, sequencing, temporary arrangements and future project planning.

4. Root Cause Analysis and Lessons Learnt

  • Support and review root cause analyses for material construction, quality, engineering and commissioning events.
  • Challenge incomplete problem statements, unsupported causal conclusions and corrective actions that do not address the identified cause.
  • Help distinguish immediate causes, contributing factors, systemic causes and required corrective or preventive actions.
  • Capture lessons learnt from mistakes, misunderstandings, misinterpretations, design gaps, scope gaps, specification gaps and commissioning issues.
  • Translate validated lessons into actionable recommendations, project controls, technical guidance or proposed controlled document changes.
  • Support verification that approved corrective actions and lessons are implemented and closed.

5. Regional CE&I Contribution

  • Provide targeted regional support to other APAC projects when requested and when compatible with primary site responsibilities.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary reviews with mechanical, electrical and project delivery specialists.
  • Contribute to programme reviews, technical assessments, technical papers, guidance documents and improvement initiatives.
  • Share proven solutions and emerging risks across the regional network to improve consistency and prevent recurrence.
  • Support feedback to the appropriate document owners where evidence indicates a need to clarify or update specifications, drawings, contracts or technical requirements.

Overview

Security represents the most critical priorities for our customers in a world awash in digital threats, regulatory scrutiny, and estate complexity. Microsoft Security aspires to make the world a safer place for all. We want to reshape security and empower every user, customer, and developer with a security cloud that protects them with end-to-end, simplified solutions. The Microsoft Security organization accelerates Microsoft's mission and bold ambitions to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers' environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world.  

Our team turns real vulnerabilities and adversary behavior into reproducible tasks that models and agents can learn from and be evaluated against. Reliable grading and reward signals are central to this work: success must reflect a verified security outcome, not simply a convincing response. 

We are looking for several Principal and Senior Security Research Engineers to build realistic, safely contained attack scenarios across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments. You will combine hands-on security research with software engineering to reproduce vulnerable conditions, construct representative multi-step attack chains, and implement checks that establish what actually happened. Your scenarios will support reinforcement learning for Microsoft’s MAI family of models and evaluation of security Perception agents and the software harnesses that run them. Working with threat researchers, AI engineers, and environment engineers, you will test whether systems can distinguish threats from benign activity, connect evidence across an attack chain, and identify effective responses. You will own scenarios from research through implementation and grading, adapting them as attacker techniques evolve. Your work will give teams trustworthy training signals and concrete evidence of whether model, agent, or harness changes improve security capabilities that matter to customers. 

Candidates residing within commuting distance of the Redmond or Reston hub are required to work on-site under a hybrid work arrangement, in accordance with Microsoft’s and the team’s in-office requirements for these designated locations.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.  



Responsibilities

  • Turn threat research into working scenarios, reproducing real vulnerabilities and emerging adversary techniques in cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments.  

  • Build realistic attack chains.

  • Connect vulnerable applications, identity weaknesses, and misconfigurations into multi-step scenarios with verified prerequisites and observable security impact.  

  • Make outcomes verifiable.

  • Build automated graders and reward signals grounded in system state and telemetry, distinguishing agent success, effective defenses, and environment failures.  

  • Evaluate beyond familiar patterns. 

  • Create attack variants, benign lookalikes, and patched controls that expose missed threats, false positives, and memorization.  

  • Deliver safe, reusable research.

  • Own scenario code, isolation, evidence capture and reset; partner with AI and environment engineers to turn findings into better training and evaluation.

SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for engineers to help achieve that mission. 


We seek a knowledgeable and experienced Principal Hardware System Engineer - Memory & Storage Validation to collaborate with Cloud Hardware Infrastructure Engineering, Azure Engineering, and Exchange Engineering groups to qualify memory and storage components for Microsoft Data Center. 

We are looking for a candidate who can understand components architecture, software applications, and OS environment to create components qualification test plan for both device and system levels. This role will also include writing test software in some cases and debug. At the cutting edge of high-performance computing, provides an opportunity to benefit millions of users daily. The successful candidate must be able to synthesize complex and sometimes conflicting requirements from hardware, software and business teams. 

 

#SCHIE 



Responsibilities
  • Define and drive Microsoft's memory and storage qualification strategy across current and future Azure server platforms.
  • Lead the architecture of scalable qualification frameworks, validation methodologies, automation infrastructure, and deployment readiness processes for cloud-scale environments.
  • Influence component and platform architecture decisions by partnering with engineering, silicon, firmware, operating system, and service teams across Microsoft.
  • Establish qualification coverage, reliability requirements, usage models, telemetry strategy, and health monitoring frameworks to ensure production readiness at hyperscale.
  • Drive resolution of the most complex memory and storage issues impacting Azure platform availability, performance, and reliability.
  • Lead cross-functional investigations involving hardware, firmware, operating systems, drivers, and cloud services to identify root causes and define corrective actions.
  • Influence supplier roadmaps and engineering investments through strategic engagement with OEMs, ODMs, silicon providers, and storage and memory ecosystem partners.
  • Champion engineering excellence through data-driven decision making, technical reviews, risk management, and continuous improvement of qualification processes.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship across engineering teams, helping establish best practices and raising organizational capability. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications: 

  • Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience OR equivalent experience.

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer, and/or government security screening requirements is required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to, the following specialized security screening: 
    • Microsoft Cloud Background Check. This position is required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire or transfer and every two years thereafter. 
       

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • 5+ years of experience in hardware validation and qualification (planning, documentation, development, execution, and debug) 

  • Knowledge of server system, system memory, and storage architecture 

  • Familiar with networking, power, rack management and remote access environments 

  • Experience integrating and validating hardware components and/or system levels

  • Familiar with and able to develop scripts (PowerShell, Python, Perl) and routines to enable debug and accelerate data collection and data reduction via automation 

  • Self-motivated individuals must be able to work collaboratively in team environment and across internal divisions and industry (OEM, ODM), demonstrate technical leadership in driving successful product development

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage leadership audiences

  • Expertise with storage architecture including NVMe 

  • 10+ years Experience in server systems validation and qualification 

  • Experience defining test strategy for new products

Customer Solution Lifecycle Management

  • Conduct in-depth root cause analysis, identify improvement opportunities, and drive resulting repair and prevention actions to closure. 

Relationship/Experience Management 

  • Represent the voice of strategic customers to Product Groups, identify recurring usage and product patterns, and drive durable resolutions and product improvements. 

  • Partner with product teams, support, and other stakeholders to prioritize, unblock, and resolve critical customer issues.

Overview

Join the Windows Cloud Experiences team to build core Windows client technologies that power secure, high-performance remote desktop experiences at global scale. As part of the Windows + Devices organization, you will design and ship foundational Windows client components that integrate with the
operating system, devices, and hardware while connecting to cloud-powered services.

This role is suited for engineers with experience building native C++ software close to the operating system, particularly in performance-sensitive and reliability-critical environments. You will solve systems-level problems, contribute to technical design decisions, and own well-scoped features and components
through the engineering lifecycle.


Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to
create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

Build Core Windows Client and Device Experiences

  • Implement native Windows components in modern C++, integrating with Win32, COM, Windows services, and system APIs.
  • Build capabilities involving device redirection, input, display, audio/video, USB, and HID integration for remote desktop and virtualization scenarios.
  • Develop and maintain cross-process, cross-thread, performance-critical code paths where correctness, latency, reliability, and stability are important.
  • Contribute to technical design decisions and evaluate tradeoffs across the Windows client components and devices you work on.

 

Systems-Level Engineering

  • Investigate and resolve systems-level issues spanning kernel and user-mode boundaries, operating system integration, drivers, services, and client applications.
  • Optimize memory usage, threading models, IPC, and I/O within complex, long-running Windows client processes.
  • Diagnose performance, reliability, memory, and concurrency issues using telemetry, traces, dumps, debuggers, and other diagnostic tools.
  • Partner with Windows platform, security, device, and other engineering teams to design robust and secure implementations.
  • Work through technically ambiguous problems with the team, identify appropriate engineering tradeoffs, and carry solutions across component boundaries.

Technical Ownership

  • Own well-scoped features across the engineering lifecycle, including design, implementation, testing, deployment, telemetry, and live-site debugging.
  • Contribute to design and code reviews, and apply engineering practices for testability, performance, reliability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Contribute to iterative improvements to Windows client technologies in an agile engineering environment with frequent releases.
  • Investigate customer and production issues, determine root causes, and implement engineering improvements that reduce recurrence.
  • Share systems-level knowledge through design discussions and code reviews, and contribute to raising engineering quality across the team.


Technologies

You may work across technologies including:

  • C++ for native Windows and systems-level development.
  • C#, .NET, and WinUI.
  • Win32, WinRT, COM, RPC, Windows services, and system APIs.
  • Windows input, graphics, audio/video, networking, and device stacks.
  • Windows diagnostics and debugging technologies, including ETW, traces, dumps, and debuggers.


Qualifications

Required/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to,  C++, C#
    • OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience developing native Windows applications or system components.
  • Experience with Win32, COM, Windows services, or Windows system APIs.
  • Experience debugging performance, memory, threading, or concurrency issues in native code.
  • Experience with device integration, USB, HID, audio/video, or driver-adjacent development.
  • Familiarity with remote desktop or virtualization technologies such as RDP or ICA.
  • Experience using ETW, traces, dumps, or debuggers for Windows diagnostics.
  • Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools responsibly to improve development, testing, or
    debugging workflows.

As a Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays. Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.



Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
  • Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members.  Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
  • Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
  • Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. The Regional Managing Director, Data Center Community is an externally facing leadership role responsible for earning and sustaining trust in a major Microsoft data center community or regional cluster of communities. The role serves as Microsoft’s local community leader, local stakeholder point of contact, and chief spokesperson for the assigned region, representing the company with civic leaders, elected officials, business organizations, education and workforce partners, nonprofits, media, and community stakeholders.  

 

This position is designed for a high-visibility data center environment where local trust, transparent communications, public engagement, and community benefit are central to Microsoft’s long-term license to operate. The Managing Director leads a regional team that includes a Community Manager and a Communications Manager and works in close partnership with the local data center operations, as well as Microsoft legal, government affairs, philanthropic and communications teams to deliver a coordinated, locally empowered, and campaign-ready approach.  

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

 

Role Scope and Leadership Model  

  • Lead Microsoft’s regional data center community strategy, including local stakeholder engagement, public narrative, community investment,  and trust-building priorities.  

  • Serve as the chief local spokesperson for the region, shaping Microsoft’s voice in community forums, public events, local media engagements, business and civic convenings, and high-stakes community conversations.  

  • Manage and guide a regional team and budget consisting of a Community Manager and a Communications Manager, setting priorities, aligning execution, and ensuring the team operates as one integrated local function.  

  • Partner closely with the local data center operations leader to align community engagement, communications, and operational priorities, ensuring Microsoft shows up as a coordinated and accountable neighbor.  

  • Coordinate with regional and national surge teams when new market entry, permitting, zoning, local controversy, media attention, or urgent community concerns require additional support.  

  • Manage a locally focused budget to enable local partnerships and support community priorities in relation to the data center and its operations.



Responsibilities

Regional Leadership and Community Strategy  

  • Own and accountable for the integrated community engagement strategy for the assigned data center region, translating Microsoft’s public  Community-First AI Infrastructure commitments into locally relevant plans, partnerships, communications, and measurable outcomes. 
  • Build and sustain trusted relationships with local elected officials, civic leaders, business organizations, education and workforce institutions, nonprofits, labor partners, community advocates, and other priority stakeholders. 
  • Represent Microsoft as a trusted local leader in public forums, community meetings, advisory boards, chambers of commerce, business councils, nonprofit coalitions, and other high-impact venues. 
  • Anticipate community risks and opportunities, maintain a clear stakeholder map, identify emerging sentiment, and escalate issues quickly with recommendations for action. 
  • Ensure community engagement begins early, remains transparent, and continues through the full data center lifecycle, including planning, construction, operations, expansion, and moments of heightened scrutiny.  

 

Chief Spokesperson and Public Narrative  

  • Serve as Microsoft’s chief local spokesperson for the assigned data center community, delivering clear, credible, plain-language messages about Microsoft’s investments, operations, community commitments and impact, and long-term presence. 
  • Guide the local narrative across community engagement, media, social sentiment, public meetings, and stakeholder communications, ensuring consistency with Microsoft’s regional and national messaging while remaining responsive to local needs. 
  • Prepare for and lead public-facing engagements such as town halls, hearings, office hours, tours, groundbreaking events, listening sessions, briefings, and community benefit discussions. 
  • Work with the Communications Manager to develop talking points, FAQs, briefings, local proof points, media materials, rapid-response guidance, and storytelling that demonstrates Microsoft’s accountability and community impact. 
  • Act as the trusted local voice during sensitive moments, helping Microsoft respond with transparency, empathy, speed, and operational accuracy.  

 

Communications and Community Engagement Oversight  

  • Lead the regional team’s budget communications and community engagement operating rhythm, ensuring the Community Manager and Communications Manager have clear priorities, coordinated plans, and defined accountability. 
  • Oversee local communications strategy, including proactive storytelling, local media engagement, social sentiment monitoring, stakeholder updates, community event messaging, and crisis-response readiness. 
  • Guide community programming and philanthropic investments, ensuring local grants, sponsorships, employee engagement, AI skilling, workforce initiatives, nonprofit partnerships, and education programs align with community priorities and Microsoft commitments. 
  • Connect communications, media, and community efforts so local programs generate credible proof points and community voices that strengthen trust and demonstrate tangible benefit. 
  • Ensure the regional team maintains accurate data, metrics, outcomes, and qualitative feedback to support internal reporting, public transparency, and continuous improvement.  

 

Cross-Functional Coordination and Escalation  

  • Serve as the central coordinator for community-facing work across various cross-functional internal Microsoft teams 
  • Leverage clear escalation paths for operational, reputational, policy, permitting, media, and community issues, ensuring news travels fast and decision-makers receive concise, action-oriented guidance. 
  • Support local government relations by aligning stakeholder engagement, meeting preparation, follow-up, and messaging with appropriate internal teams. 
  • Bring local insight into regional and national planning, including feedback on community sentiment, stakeholder expectations, program gaps, policy concerns, and communications needs. 
  • Help Microsoft move with local empowerment while operating within company guardrails for accuracy, legal review, brand alignment, and responsible engagement.

    • OR Bachelor's Degree AND 8+ years work experience in corporate social responsibility (CSR), philanthropies, corporate affairs, government affairs, business and international development, or related area
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years of experience serving as a public spokesperson or external representative, including comfort with public speaking, media-adjacent environments, stakeholder briefings, and sensitive community conversations.  
  • 4+ years of experience leading high-visibility community engagement in complex environments involving elected officials, media, business leaders, nonprofits, education and workforce partners, and community advocates.  
  • Ability to travel frequently within the assigned region and participate in evening or weekend community events as needed.  

 

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Master's Degree AND 8+ years work experience in corporate social responsibility (CSR), philanthropies, corporate affairs, government affairs, business and international development, or related area
    • OR Bachelor's Degree AND 12+ years work experience in corporate social responsibility (CSR), philanthropies, corporate affairs, government affairs, business and international development, or related area
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years experience managing a corporate social responsibility (CSR) or related program.
  • 3+ years people or team management experience.

  • Experience navigating local permitting, zoning, public meetings, community benefits discussions, coalition-building, or issue advocacy.  
  • Knowledge of AI infrastructure, cloud technology, workforce development, digital skilling, sustainability, electricity, water, construction, or local economic development issues relevant to data center communities.  
  • Experience designing community investment strategies, advisory boards, nonprofit partnerships, workforce pathways, AI skilling programs, grants, sponsorships, employee volunteer engagement, or local impact campaigns.  
  • Experience working effectively across large, matrixed organizations with legal, policy, communications, operations, engineering, and executive stakeholders.  
  • Proven ability to manage or guide cross-functional teams, consultants, or pods that include communications, community engagement, public affairs, program delivery, and issue-management responsibilities. Experience managing budgets and resource allocation for community engagement programs.

Overview

Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.

 

The Security Research Group at Microsoft Research Redmond works on a variety of areas to ensure computer systems are secure and trustworthy. Its current work investigates systems that leverage general software/systems security, confidential computing, formal verification, zero-knowledge proofs, data-driven security, and agentic security. The internship will explore new ideas and approaches to building secure and trustworthy software and cloud services. 



Responsibilities

Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer.



Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, STEM, or a related field.

Overview

Microsoft is seeking a Chief Technology Officer for the US Federal Civilian business, including US Tribal Nations. The Chief Technology Officer serves as the senior technology executive for the business, translating emerging technologies, customer priorities, market dynamics, and Microsoft capabilities into actionable strategy for the business and its most strategic accounts.

 

Working across Microsoft leadership, account teams, product and engineering groups, partners, and senior government executives, the Chief Technology Officer shapes Microsoft's most strategic Civilian engagements, guides use of the product portfolio, develops the Federal partner ecosystem, leads complex escalations and creates a framework of technical adoption that can be scaled by account aligned technical resources.

 

The successful candidate will be a technologist, strategist, customer advocate, partner leader, and business executive, equally at ease discussing enterprise architecture with engineers, mission priorities with a government CIO, account strategy with sales leadership, partner solutions with a systems integrator, and product requirements with Microsoft engineering. Above all, the Chief Technology Officer will connect what Federal Civilian customers need, what Microsoft and its partners can deliver today, what Microsoft should build next, and how technical differentiation becomes customer outcomes, platform adoption, and sustainable growth.



Responsibilities

Business, Market, and Technology Strategy

  • Provide strategic technology leadership for the Civilian and Tribal Nations business, ensuring customer mission priorities, competitive dynamics, and emerging technologies inform business, investment, and go-to-market decisions.
  • Represent the Civilian business in Federal and USPSI strategy development, and translate broader Microsoft priorities into actionable Civilian strategies
  • Partner with account teams and customer executives to shape account-level technology and business strategy for Microsoft's most strategic Civilian customers and pursuits measured by growth and wins across the business.
  • Provide Civilian leadership with a clear point of view on technology shifts on new and emerging technology, customer adoption signals, competitive developments, product risks, and areas where Microsoft should invest or change direction.

 

Customer and Executive Engagement

  • Serve as a trusted technology advisor to senior Federal leaders, including CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, CDOs, CAIOs, acquisition executives, and mission leaders.
  • Guide customers in translating mission and modernization objectives into practical technology strategies, architectures, and transformation initiatives, particularly where the challenge spans multiple Microsoft technologies, engineering organizations, or partners.
  • Serve as Technology Lead for major pursuits, enterprise transformations, strategic renewals, and significant escalations, balancing mission requirements, engineering realities, compliance obligations, and business considerations while preserving long-term customer trust.
  • Represent Microsoft as an external technology voice at customer forums, government technology events, industry conferences, and executive briefings.

 

Technology Portfolio and Government Cloud Leadership

  • Maintain an integrated view of the Microsoft portfolio as it applies to Federal Civilian missions, spanning cloud and hybrid infrastructure, cybersecurity and identity, AI, data, application modernization, contact center, business applications, and collaboration.
  • Guide customers and account teams through architectural tradeoffs, product dependencies, service limitations, and emerging capabilities across commercial and government cloud environments.
  • Apply Federal cybersecurity, compliance, and authorization requirements, including NIST SP 800-53 and 800-171, CUI protection, Authority to Operate, and data sovereignty, to strategy, architecture, and product adoption, engaging specialized expertise where required.
  • Identify repeatable technology patterns, solutions, and engagement models for application across Civilian accounts.

 

Product and Engineering Influence

  • Serve as the principal connection between the Federal Civilian market and Microsoft product and engineering organizations.
  • Aggregate customer, partner, and field feedback into systemic product gaps, roadmap priorities, and adoption barriers, prioritized by mission impact, growth potential, and competitive significance.
  • Ensure clear, credible, and consistent communication regarding product capabilities, roadmap direction, limitations, and dependencies.

 

Federal Partner and Ecosystem Strategy

  • Develop and execute an end-to-end Civilian  partner engagement strategy aligned to the business's technology priorities and growth objectives.
  • Build executive and technical relationships with Federal systems integrators, solution providers, independent software vendors, and small businesses that influence customer technology decisions and mission outcomes.
  • Ensure priority partners incorporate Microsoft's latest cloud, AI, security, data, and application capabilities into their solutions, reference architectures, managed services, and go-to-market strategies.
  • Bring partner requirements, technical barriers, and competitive intelligence back to the business and to product and engineering, and evaluate partner engagement by technical capability, platform adoption, and contribution to growth.

 

Technical Community Leadership

  • Provide strategic direction, mentorship, and practical frameworks and messaging to architects, technology strategists, specialists, and customer success teams, developing leaders who operate effectively with senior government executives, partners, and Microsoft engineering.
  • Share customer insights, reusable architectures, competitive intelligence, and lessons learned across teams, and align account, technical, partner, and business teams around the Civilian technology agenda.
  • Foster a culture of customer advocacy, technical excellence, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning, leading through influence across a large and highly matrixed organization.
