Overview

As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT) Manager, you will lead a team of technicians, providing expert guidance on performing hardware deployments, diagnostics on equipment, and hardware decommissions. You will support technician performance, prioritizing technician tasks while monitoring Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).  This opportunity will allow you to model leadership principles, provide training to technicians, and accelerate your career growth in the process.

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 data centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays. 

Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties. 



Responsibilities

Datacenter Operations

Encourages the sharing of expertise in and provides guidance on standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Encourages the sharing of expertise and provides guidance on the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment. Develops awareness of Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation components: Incident Management and Change Management.
 
Provides guidance on, and holds a team of technicians accountable for compliance with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines. Proactively reviews and provides feedback regarding Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines. Resolves issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities directly, or with assistance from compliance colleagues and/or business partners. Provides input on improvement plan components for service delivery gaps or challenges.
 
Ensures a team of technicians can complete assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type. Supports escalation of challenging or complex tickets to internal business partners and appropriately summarizes relevant issues for communication to direct-line management. Coordinates and assigns tasks to technicians, and/or provides input or coordination with appropriate program managers and direct-line management for ticket assignment automation to provide direction as needed, to ensure work is appropriately allocated to meet Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type. Monitors progress of tickets assigned to teams of technicians and adjusts where necessary, to meet established Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type. Analyzes data related to technicians' performance on tickets and shares with direct-line management.
 
Advises on and reviews suggested modifications to process and procedures to manage changes and drive improvement in service quality and/or efficiency. Proactively investigates, evaluates, and analyzes changes. Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) to evaluate impact on service execution and shares relevant information about change with stakeholders across functions and disciplines to mitigate the impact they may have on others. Encourages technicians to ask questions when they do not have required information, resolves others' questions in a timely manner, and may provide feedback on changes to processes to direct-line management, standards management teams, and/or project, program, or special initiative managers.

Datacenter Work Environment

Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
 
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
 
Promotes a positive and effective team environment by modeling best practices, leading regular team meetings, cross-discipline collaborations, and monitoring the status of work across their team to understanding the impact on other shifts/technician teams, engineering groups or internal business partner needs and the overall business. Provides, responds to, and encourages providing feedback regarding on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams.
 
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
 
Conducts daily safety briefings, ensuring their team members attend, and/or participates in onsite safety committees. Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, ensures technicians comply with EHS training completion requirements and are compliant with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), Task Hazard Analysis (THAs) completion, and use of appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, empowering technician teams to report and/or take proactive action regarding safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in regular cadence proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems, and follows up with their team members as needed regarding actionable safety observations reported.

Overview
 

Do you love working on paid advertising?  Thrive on seeing your work out in the world?  Believe that finding creative solutions to complex problems is a superpower of yours? We are looking for a creative, collaborative, and highly accountable team player with expertise in paid advertising campaign management to join our WDS Creative & Integrated Marketing team. We believe great campaigns are built through partnership, clear ownership, candid feedback, inclusive decision-making, and disciplined execution.  

The Senior Advertising Campaign Manager will lead the operating rhythm and end-to-end delivery of complex, high-visibility consumer campaigns. This person will serve as the campaign’s connective tissue and “air traffic controller,” bringing together the people, decisions, inputs, assets, and timelines required to get excellent advertising into market on time and at quality. You will own campaign operations across key paid workstreams, including video, digital display, social, creator, custom media, audio, retail, localization, and asset handoff. This role would work closely with campaign managers, creative leads, product marketing, integrated marketing, media, research and insights, legal, engineering, regional teams, creative and production partners, and external agencies. The ideal candidate combines marketing judgment with exceptional program leadership, understands how paid creative gets made and trafficked, and is comfortable driving the details without losing sight of the customer ambition or the campaign goals. 

About the Team 

WDS Creative & Integrated Marketing team sets a high bar for the work while supporting one another, staying curious, and bringing positive energy to complex, fast-moving challenges. We value people who simplify ambiguity, anticipate what is needed, respectfully push for clarity, and create the conditions for teams and agencies to do their best work.  The team translates product and business priorities into integrated consumer experiences and high-impact marketing that builds the Microsoft brand, creates demand, and helps customers understand why Microsoft products matter. Global Advertising leads the development and delivery of consumer paid advertising campaigns.  



Responsibilities
 

· Lead end-to-end campaign operations from kickoff through launch and wrap-up, translating campaign strategy, media plans, and creative requirements into an integrated plan of record with clear owners, milestones, dependencies, and decision points. 

· Own cross-workstream orchestration across video, display, social, creator, custom media, audio, retail, localization, and market activation, ensuring work moves cohesively across creative development, production, post-production, approvals, versioning, trafficking, and launch. 

· Build and manage detailed workback schedules, campaign trackers, hot sheets, status dashboards, launch calendars, and risk logs. Maintain a reliable single source of truth and provide concise, audience-appropriate updates to working teams and leaders. 

· Establish and run effective campaign rhythms, including agency status, production, mission control, trafficking, creative review, and cross-functional V-team meetings. Create agendas, drive decisions, document actions, and follow through to closure. 

· Identify risks early, clarify dependencies, escalate tradeoffs with sound recommendations, and remove blockers so the campaign can meet quality, timing, budget, legal, and media requirements. 

· Serve as a primary day-to-day partner for creative, production, adaptation, localization, and media agencies. Define ways of working, roles, service-level expectations, review paths, and handoff requirements. 

· Coordinate creative asset readiness against the media plan, including specifications, versioning, retailer and partner requirements, URLs, tracking, end cards, offer language, disclosures, source files, and delivery packages. 

· Partner with CELA and business stakeholders to plan and route creative reviews, track feedback and substantiation needs, and ensure approved changes are reflected consistently across assets and markets. 

· Drive rigorous QA/QC across campaign materials and handoffs, partnering with experts to confirm product accuracy, brand consistency, accessibility, format specifications, naming conventions, and completeness before release. 

· Lead global and regional activation readiness, including localization, market reviews, asset sharing, usage-rights considerations, toolkit creation, and coordination of new edits or adaptations. 

· Manage campaign documentation and asset organization across approved Microsoft systems, including onboarding materials, campaign walking decks, creative wrap decks, toolkits, archives, and agency access. 

· Partner with media, research, analytics, and campaign leads to connect creative delivery with measurement, in-market optimization, and post-campaign learning. Capture process and partnership learnings and turn them into practical improvements. 

· Model Microsoft leadership principles by creating clarity, generating energy, and delivering success across teams without relying on direct authority 



Qualifications
 

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Advertising, Marketing, Communications, or related field AND 4+ years experience in media, marketing, or advertising on the client or agency side
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years campaign management experience, digital marketing experience, and/or product, project, or site management experience.
 

·

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Advertising, or related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience,
    • OR Master's Degree in a related field AND 5+ years of relevant experience, 
    • OR AND 3+ years of experience managing integrated or paid advertising campaigns across multiple channels and stakeholders, including responsibility for schedules, dependencies, approvals, asset delivery, and launch readiness
    • OR equivalent experience. 

  • Experience working directly with creative, production, media, and adaptation agencies and managing complex deliverables in a deadline-driven environment. 

  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional work, create clarity from ambiguity, identify and resolve risks, and influence decisions without direct authority. 

  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams with precision while maintaining a calm, collaborative, and solutions-oriented approach with written and verbal communication, meeting facilitation and stakeholder management. 

    Experience delivering large-scale global consumer advertising campaigns, with working knowledge of the full paid campaign lifecycle from brief through trafficking, launch, optimization, wrap-up and communicating campaign status, risks and decisions.

【マイクロソフトにおけるサポートエンジニアとは？】  
Microsoft の法人向け有償サポートでは、お客様の課題を技術力で解決する「最後の砦」としての役割を担います。メールと電話を通じて、お客様と直接コミュニケーションを取りながら、Microsoft を代表して対応します。  最高のサポートサービスを提供するために，社内外の技術エキスパートと連携し、Azure や M365 の最新機能を活用しながら、セキュリティポリシーの設計、情報保護、DLP（データ損失防止）などの領域で、実践的かつ戦略的なサポートを提供します。  
 
 
【サポートエンジニアの魅力】
常に最先端の技術に触れながら学び続けられる環境が整っており、純粋に技術を追求したい方にとって理想的な職場です。Azure や Microsoft 365 をはじめとする幅広いプロダクトに携わりながら、国内外の多様な環境・課題に対応することで、製品の第一人者として活躍できるチャンスがあります。大規模な製品や目的のために連携するチームの一員として、日々新しい技術に触れ、技術者としての成長を実感できる非常に魅力的なポジションです。   
 
 
【どんなサポートエンジニアが働いているの？】
私たちはセキュリティ製品を支えるクラウド技術支援の専門チームです。個人の専門性だけでなく、チームで協力しながら課題に取り組む文化が根付いています。セキュリティ製品やテクニカルサポート経験者が新しい製品に挑戦してキャリアを広げている一方、未経験からスタートし、仲間の支援を受けながら成長しているメンバーもいます。

Overview

As a Senior Recruiter and Metro Lead supporting Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I), you will lead talent acquisition strategy and execution for a priority datacenter metro. Serving as the primary recruiting partner for the market, you will help build the teams responsible for planning, constructing, commissioning, and operating the infrastructure that powers the Microsoft Cloud. 

You will partner closely with metro leadership, hiring managers, HR, and cross-functional stakeholders to translate local business priorities into integrated hiring plans. The role will focus on critical power, electrical, energy, utilities, construction, engineering, and datacenter operations talent, while coordinating searches across functions and creating a consistent, high-quality experience for leaders and candidates. 

This metro-lead role requires strategic judgment, operational rigor, and the ability to influence across a complex, fast-growing organization. You will use market intelligence and recruiting data to identify talent risks, build differentiated sourcing strategies, and advise leaders on workforce availability and location-specific dynamics. A candidate based in or near one of CO+I’s largest U.S. datacenter metros—such as Texas or Wisconsin—is preferred to enable strong local partnership and market presence. You will also support Microsoft’s Community First Infrastructure Plan by strengthening local partnerships and helping create inclusive pathways to employment in the communities where our datacenters operate. 

Do what you love. Create the future you want. Explore the career options that Microsoft Security has to offer. 

You may be a fit for this role if you: 

  • Thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments where agility and adaptability are key. 

  • Enjoy working in a mission-driven culture where protecting customers is at the heart of everything. 

  • Are passionate about cybersecurity and excited to help shape the teams building the future of digital defense. 

  • Demonstrate a bias for action, a passion for innovation, and the ability to navigate ambiguity. 

  • Have a proven track record of developing and executing creative hiring strategies that attract top-tier technical talent in highly competitive markets. 

  • Possess executive presence with the ability to engage and influence leadership stakeholders, including hiring leaders and executive staff. 

  • Balance long-term talent planning with immediate hiring needs, thinking strategically while executing tactically. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities

Stakeholder/Client Engagement 

  • Identifies current and future talent needs through proactive exploration and analysis of market supply. Proactively consults leaders to provide clarity of talent market insights. 

  • Applies deep knowledge and consultative skills relevant to the business and hiring managers' needs (e.g., time to hire, location, budget, inclusivity) and uses this knowledge to manage the execution of end-to-end hiring plans aligned to the needs of the business group, division, region, or subsidiary. Engages with senior-level stakeholders to develop hiring plans. 

  • Consult on critical talent needs and influence leaders to embrace differentiated and non-traditional talent pools for the metro.  

Data Analysis & Hiring Plans 

  • Performs deep analysis of external market data leveraging industry/market expertise, providing market and channel insights to the business to recommend and drive strategies and talent acquisition initiatives. 

  • Lead the implementation of hiring plans for complex organizations or talent pools that address both short- and long-term needs (12+ months). 

Candidate Attraction 

  • Use deep knowledge of competitor opportunities to differentiate Microsoft’s unique career possibilities and rewards. 

  • Share compelling stories that help others source, recruit, and close candidates. 

  • Track candidate activity and share insights with internal stakeholders. 

  • Coaches the client to represent Microsoft’s unique career possibilities, advantages, and rewards that are distinct from those of competitors.  

  • Helps develop learning and training resources for hiring managers, metro employees, and recruiting to help advance outcomes and capabilities. 

Candidate Experience 

  • Develop hiring plans that meet candidate needs throughout the lifecycle, especially for critical, complex, or high-level searches. 

  • Enhances the candidate experience at all stages of the process by proactively identifying factors that may impact the candidate and partnering with hiring managers/business leaders to develop appropriate acquisition or mitigation strategies.  

Operational Compliance & Excellence 

  • Lead optimization of policies, systems, and processes, and guide stakeholders on their impact. 

  • Maintain accurate documentation in compliance with guidelines (e.g., OFCCP, GDPR), and leverage data to inform insights. 

Other 

  • Embody our culture and values

Required/minimum qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years talent acquisition experience (e.g., recruiting, sourcing), HR experience, or industry experience related to role
    • OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 12+ years talent acquisition experience (e.g., recruiting, sourcing), HR experience, or industry experience related to role
    • OR Master's Degree AND 8+ years talent acquisition experience (e.g., recruiting, sourcing), HR experience, or industry experience related to role
    • OR equivalent experience.

Overview

The Windows + Devices Fundamentals team improves the reliability, performance, responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and overall health of Windows devices. We build and operate the services, telemetry systems, and data pipelines that transform signals from labs and the installed base into trustworthy metrics, actionable diagnostics, and measurable engineering improvements.

We are seeking a self-driven Software Engineer II to design and deliver data-driven systems that reveal how Windows devices behave at scale. You will independently own well-scoped backend services and data pipelines, investigate product-health signals, and deliver improvements that advance Windows Fundamentals across devices, silicon, and customer segments.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Define and implement well-scoped Windows Fundamentals metrics, queries, cohort strategies, and measurement workflows across reliability, performance, responsiveness, power, battery life, memory, and storage.
  • Design, build, deploy, and operate reliable backend services and data pipelines for telemetry ingestion, transformation, orchestration, storage, health monitoring, diagnostics, and engineering workflows.
  • Apply and improve engineering practices for service reliability, security, compliance, observability, data quality, schema evolution, deployment safety, incident response, and operational support.
  • Analyze large-scale telemetry, diagnostic signals, and traces to identify trends, anomalies, regressions, causal factors, and customer impact.
  • Independently investigate metric movements and service issues using statistical methods, experimentation, debugging, and performance-analysis tools; translate findings into well-scoped engineering actions.
  • Design and deliver automation, AI-assisted analysis, dashboards, alerts, and diagnostic workflows that detect issues earlier and reduce manual engineering effort.
  • Contribute to technical designs and code reviews, resolve dependencies with partner teams, share findings, and mentor less-experienced engineers on well-understood areas.


Qualifications

Required/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python.
    • OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Candidates need at least three years of software engineering experience. A bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience, is also required.
  • At least one year of experience in backend service development, data engineering, distributed systems, large-scale analytics, systems analysis, or related work.
  • Experience developing, testing, deploying, or operating reliable production software, services, data pipelines, telemetry systems, or analytics.
  • Solid programming, debugging, software-design, data-analysis, and problem-solving skills; ability to independently execute well-scoped work, navigate partial ambiguity, and use evidence to guide decisions.
  • Experience with distributed services, Azure or other cloud platforms, data pipelines, operating systems, performance engineering, or large-scale fleet analytics.
  • Experience defining metrics, establishing baselines and cohorts, investigating regressions, and communicating insights through dashboards or technical reports.
  • Experience with telemetry schemas, service APIs, orchestration, monitoring and alerting, data-quality controls, anomaly detection, or automated diagnostic workflows.
  • Experience with Kusto, Azure data platforms, privacy-conscious telemetry, statistical analysis, machine learning, AI-assisted engineering workflows, or Windows internals.
  • C, C++, C#, Python, PowerShell, and SQL/KQL; WinDbg, Windows Performance Analyzer, and ETW; Kusto, Azure services and data platforms, orchestration and monitoring systems, Power BI, statistics, experimentation, anomaly detection, machine learning, and AI-assisted analysis.

Overview

As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT), you will stage, set up and perform hardware deployments. In addition, you will also perform troubleshooting and diagnostics on equipment, as well as perform hardware decommissions for simple changes and refreshes following Standard Operating Procedures. This opportunity is an ideal role for an Early Careers professional with 1+ yrs' industry work experience and a keen interested in hardware.  The role will allow you to deepen your understanding of Data Center standard processes and procedures, develop mentoring skills while providing guidance to peers, familiarizing yourself with security and data management procedures, and accelerate your career growth in the process.  This role is based 100% onsite in one of our Data Centers in Macquarie Park, Sydney.

 

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.  Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

 

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.  Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities
  • Perform diagnostics and troubleshooting following standard procedures, quickly identify the cause(s) of issues, and replace faulty components with minimal customer and business disruption.
  • Perform post-execution quality checks and verifies that grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling are set up properly according to safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Tasks (NDTs).
  • Decommission hardware for simple changes and refreshes (e.g., memory upgrades, rebuilds) follow standard procedures with minimal guidance.
  • Follow procedures to communicate, report, and escalate incidents to appropriate Microsoft data center operations management units, Technician Leads, and engineering specialists.
  • Assist and provide guidance to other technicians to complete challenging or complex tasks.
  • Complete required training aligned to the role and workload; observe more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training.
  • Contribute to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with others, contribute to regular team meetings, ask questions, and staying apprised of the status of others' work.
  • Take pride and a sense of accountability for the service quality, completeness, and resulting user experience; display accountability and ownership of the data center facilities.
  • Embody our culture and values.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma, TAFE, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components AND 1+ year(s) industry work experience supporting IT equipment (hardware, routers, switches, cabling, server management, racking & stacking etc) or related technology.

 

Background Check Requirements: 

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: 

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
  • Citizenship Verification: This position requires verification of Australian Citizenship to meet federal government security requirements including verification of an Australian Passport or an AU Citizenship Certificate.
  • NV1/2, PV Clearance Assessment: This position may require an enhanced background check conducted through the Australian Government Security Vetting Agency.

 

Whilst not required, we also look for the following Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years' industry work experience supporting IT equipment or related technology.
  • Applicable certifications: CompTIA (A+, Server+, Network+), Basic Structure Cabling (BSC).

Overview

Come build community, explore your passions and do your best work. Microsoft's Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) team is the engine that powers our cloud services, operating a global portfolio of datacenters that serves more than a billion customers and 20 million businesses. Join us and help keep that infrastructure safe, available and efficient. 

As a Critical Environment Program Manager, you will be accountable for the availability, safety and operational performance of the mechanical and electrical infrastructure inside our leased datacenters, ensuring work is executed safely, on time, within scope and in alignment with Microsoft standards. You will own the relationship with the landlord partners who operate that infrastructure, govern every change that touches the live environment, and support at a regional level for critical environment risk and escalations. The role bridges datacenter operations, engineering, construction, IT and network teams, landlord partners and external vendors, translating business and technical objectives into executable maintenance and risk-mitigation plans. 

This opportunity will allow you to accelerate your career growth, develop deep critical environment expertise, hone your risk and change management skills, and become adept at partner and vendor management. This role is based at our leased datacenter sites, and you will be able to partner with your manager to define how you work when you are not on site. 

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more, and we're dedicated to this mission across every aspect of our company. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. Join us and help shape the future of the world. 



Responsibilities

  • Oversee the daily operations and maintenance of mechanical and electrical systems within a data center environment, ensuring the effective planning, coordination, and execution of preventative and corrective maintenance programs 

  • Ensure uptime and reliability of critical environment systems through proactive monitoring, maintenance oversight, and risk mitigation  

  • Lead operational excellence by executing and governing processes such as maintenance procedures, incident reviews (RCAs), and change management  

  • Drive safety and compliance, ensuring adherence to Microsoft standards and immediately addressing risks or incidents  

  • Partner cross-functionally with engineering teams, vendors, and landlord partners to optimize DataCenter performance and resolve issues across a country or the subregion, 

  • Identify and reduce risk, minimizing human-error and high-impact incidents year over year  

  • Support emergency response readiness, acting as an escalation point for facilities-related incidents  

  • Deliver efficiency outcomes by advancing cost optimization and energy efficiency initiatives and support data-driven operations through the accurate measurement and reporting of key metrics, including power, temperature, and service-level (SLA) performance 

  • Recognizes and communicates the customer impact of operational events such as lock-downs and maintenance windows, planning accordingly to minimize disruption to clients and the business. 

  • Act as a regional subject matter expert for Critical Environment operations, providing remote and on-site support to leased datacenter sites across the sub-region beyond the home site, 

  • Shares best practices; assists others in learning role, process, procedures and provides mentorship across data centers 

  • Support new site onboarding, landlord partner transitions, and hand-over of newly delivered capacity within the sub-region   

  • Provide coverage and backfill for peers at other sites during absences, vacancies, or periods of elevated activity   



Qualifications
    • High School Diploma or equivalent AND proven industry experience in a DataCenter or other critical environment facility.
    • Relevant experience in Critical Environment infrastructures (e.g., UPS, Generator, Chillers, AHU.
    • Experience applying formal change and maintenance controls (MOP/SOP/EOP) and participating in root cause analysis in a live production environment. 
    • Willingness and ability to travel across the sub-region on a regular basis to provide on-site support, with travel expected to represent a meaningful proportion of working time (typically up to 25–30%, varying with business need).

Overview

As a Senior Networking Project Manager you will engage with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Drives customer satisfaction by engaging with customers stakeholders in a positive manner, reviewing and analyzing customer feedback, and leveraging trusted relationships with key internal resources to act as the voice of the customer. Adheres to project compliance standards and requirements of the contract and accommodates customer compliance standards. Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program. Facilitates contracting process for partner resources by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports colleagues in projects of high complexity.
Provides review of defined metrics, proactively monitors and tracks risks, ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables, and manages stakeholder communications. Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks. Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor to colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

Account Delivery Management 

  • Drives and maintains obligations to customer across the delivery lifecycle including envisioning, solution development, delivery planning, cloud consumption and usage, delivery management while ensuring adherence to security best practices in partnership with Solution Area SMEs. Ensures that customer-required or market-required security certifications are active. Leads or participates in steering committee meetings with strategic customers to discuss progress toward delivery success. 
  • Contributes to consumption activities, through others (e.g., Customer Success resources), for customers by identifying blockers to consumption goals and enabling customers, through internal teams, to get the full value of their purchases. Holds accountability for project delivery forecast.
  • Supports relationships with key stakeholders in the customer portfolio to ensure service delivery is on track and issues are being anticipated, identified, and managed. Communicates current view of delivery to customer stakeholders, as appropriate.
  • Collaborates with Sales to support contract setup, signature, compliance, and execution from deal approvals to invoicing and closure. Manages areas of fiscal responsibility within project portfolio, staying within budget while driving engagement profitability and risk management. 

Business Growth 

  • Demonstrates accountability for the financial health of a project or program (e.g., revenue attainment, accurate forecasting, cost management, and utilization, skills, and capacity planning). Identifies opportunities to accelerate and drive consumption and delivery. Owns and drives backlog risk management. Drives incremental business on top of existing projects and programs through next step proposals, conducts customer discussions related to next stage proposal (NSP) and other opportunities. Engages in the pursuit cycle to ensure deals are structured appropriately. Supports and contributes to rhythm of business (ROB) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) forecasting. 
  • Looks for or creates opportunities to maximize timely cloud consumption through current deliveries. Identifies new opportunities with customers and facilitates follow up conversations with customers on Consumption both strategically and operational, and to accelerate delivery or prevent delivery delays. 

Closure 

  • Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas to execution and delivery, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor to less experienced colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects. 
  • Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks (e.g., system closeout updates, deletion of customer data, Deliverable Acceptance Form). Drives incremental process improvement by reflecting on and sharing lessons learned across teams, creating and suggesting improvements to intellectual property (IP), providing feedback to managers on team member performance, and conducting closeout interviews with team members. 

Contracting 

  • Facilitates contracting process for customer and partner resources (e.g., contractors, vendors) by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Supports negotiation and structuring of fixed-fee subcontractor contracts with oversight from senior colleagues. Monitors and initiates Amendments, Delivery Acceptance, Proof of Delivery, and Invoicing processes. Reviews contracts according to security and data governance standards. Provides session on SFI/SBD to the onboarding partner team 

Initiation 

  • Balances needs across projects in challenging situations (e.g., scarce technical resources), with support from colleagues as needed, and collaborates with other groups (e.g., resource managers, Global Delivery Center) on integrated planning and organization of onshore/offshore projects. 
  • Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity (e.g., multiple offerings, and/or supports projects of high complexity (e.g., tailored offerings, high visibility, high impact, market making) by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program, by driving commitment of delivery resources, assigning resources, assisting in sourcing and qualifying partner resources, and creating work breakdown structures (WBSs) with delivery team. Drives checklist and process finalization for Secure Future Initiative (SFI) with team and customers 

Intellectual Property (IP) 

  • Researches and proactively shares intellectual property (IP) and provides recommendations for improvement including submitting new IP. Holds others accountable for reusing appropriate IP and collective knowledge by enforcing use of processes and artifacts with team members. 

Monitoring and Controlling 

  • Orchestrates and oversees a broad range of project metrics on midsize to large projects with high visibility (e.g., Vice President-level). Proactively ensures adherence to key performance indicators (KPIs) and provides strategic direction to drive success throughout project lifecycle.
  • Discusses and confirms Microsoft change control processes at kickoff with customer. Anticipates changes and proactively addresses by probing to ensure change can happen smoothly early in the process. Tests process before initiating formal change.
  • Ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables (e.g., documents) and tracking of agreed upon metrics for projects of standard complexity by applying quality management techniques (e.g., benchmarking, interviews) for collecting data. Uses analyses to identify solutions to systemic issues.
  • Proactively manages risks (including security risks) and issues within projects of standard complexity, leveraging technical knowledge and previous experience to evaluate risks, perform qualitative analyses (e.g., probability, impact, urgency), create risk management plans, establish processes, and work with cross-functional groups and leaders to mitigate identified risks. Contributes to recovery efforts and ensures tools are updated. Manages issue closure as a high priority. Ensures that the mandatory Information Security Risk Assessment (ISRA) is completed during project initiation, is regularly reviewed, and is signed off by accredited InfoSec Delivery Compliance Leads during delivery. Reports Security and Data Compliance breaches in a timely manner (using ReportItNow and other pertinent customer reporting outlets as applicable), informing both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Manages stakeholder communications on project health, issues, and financial performance for mid-size to large deals throughout entire project lifecycle, tailoring communications to the audience. Tracks and maintains customer deliverables.
  • Manages finances for projects with mid-size to large scopes and budgets by balancing funding and resources across workstreams, performing analyses, and leveraging cost management experience and expertise. Aims to reduce cost and improve delivery margin without impact to quality or customer experience and understands impact of decisions on the broader business (e.g., profits and losses [P&L], accrual-based accounting). 

Planning 

  • Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports colleagues in projects of high complexity, leveraging existing materials and experience to drive scope, resources, and Microsoft project schedule in alignment and collaboration with customer plan. Ensures use of baselining, resource load balancing, and application of work effort, dependency management, contingency planning, and utilization of software (e.g., Timeline). 
  • Establishes clear expectations and accountabilities (e.g., reconfirm scope, Responsible-Accountable-Consulted-Informed matrix) with all project team members (e.g., consultants) and stakeholders for teams of medium complexity by leading internal and external kick-off meetings (e.g., sales to delivery handoff, formal kick-off meetings). Integrates security-first mindset into expectations for self and others. Proactively engages broad set of internal and external stakeholders, including those who are impacted by project scope/outcome, but not directly involved (e.g., Enterprise Operating Unit, India Global Delivery, customer stakeholders) and engages subject matter experts in holistic planning activities, including team validation. 

Presales 

  • Contributes to pre-sales for medium-impact projects by articulating the business value proposition associated with the project/change and considering associated complexities and risks to ensure feasibility of commercial offer. Participates in review of proposed scope and assists in developing Statement of Work (SOW), Work Breakdown Structures (WBSs), estimates, preliminary risk assessments, etc. Ensures that ISD consulting deal appropriately includes Delivery Compliance, Privacy & Security (DCPS) package to fund Secure by Default activities. 

Relationship Development 

  • Engage with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Manages escalations or ensures resolution of escalations with customer stakeholders through tailored corrective action (e.g., education) and overcomes ambiguous situations as needed. Learns to leverage project sponsors and internal networks to influence stakeholders and resolve situations. 
  • Drives customer satisfaction by engaging with customers stakeholders in a positive manner, reviewing and analyzing customer feedback, and leveraging trusted relationships with key internal resources to act as the voice of the customer. Manage expectations with political sensitivity by leading Success Expectation discussions with customers, and documenting, executing, and monitoring through customer and partner experience (CPE).
  • Adheres to project compliance standards (e.g., confidentiality, privacy, security) and requirements of the contract and accommodates customer compliance standards, including managing compliance-related complexities (e.g., high sensitivity to confidentiality). Champions compliance by contributing to knowledge sharing across teams to build compliance capability of others.

Preferred/Additional Qualifications

  •  Bachelor's Degree in related field AND 8+ years’ experience in project management OR equivalent experience.

  • 4+ years financial management experience.
  • Agile certification, Scrum Master, Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), or Professional Scrum Master One (PSM1) certification.
  • Minimum 6 years of experience as a network engineer or technical program manager for networks.

  • Experience with architecture, deployment, and/or operations of Government classified networks.

  • Experience working with L2/L3 switching/routing platforms, application networking and network protocols to include BGP, OSPF, VRRP, LACP. 
  • Experience with cloud networking implementations with preferred focus on onboarding customer infrastructure to cloud. 
  • CCNP or higher or equivalent professional certification; CompTIA Security+ certification. 
  • Ability to work in a flexible, fast-paced environment. 
  • Highly effective communication and collaboration with customers, partners, and across teams is required.

  • Excellent judgement, decision-making skills, and the ability to work under continual deadline pressure when the situation is ambiguous.

  • Experience in one or more programming languages: C#, C++, Java, Python. 
  • Experience in network automation using scripting languages such as Python.

The role partners closely with Creative Directors, Integrated Marketing leads, Product Marketing, Product Design, Retail, Digital and external agency partners to ensure creative work is expressed ambitiously and consistently across channels while maintaining the integrity of the brand. 

We're looking for a design leader with exceptional taste, an ambition to reinvigorate some of the most recognized brands on the planet, while possessing strong systems thinking. 



Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities 

Lead the design vision for Windows, Surface and Services 

  • Define and evolve the visual identity systems for Windows, Surface and Services. 

  • Establish design principles, standards and frameworks that guide creative expression across all customer-facing touchpoints. 

  • Ensure brand systems remain modern, relevant, distinctive and scalable across markets, audiences and platforms. 

  • Create cohesion across Microsoft's consumer ecosystem while preserving the unique identity and role of each brand. 

Own end-to-end brand expression 

  • Lead the development and implementation of visual identity systems across advertising, digital, social, photography, film, retail, experiential and product marketing experiences. 

  • Oversee the application of brand systems across global campaigns and launches. 

  • Ensure creative work aligns with established design principles and visual standards regardless of channel or execution partner. 

  • Partner with teams across the organization to maintain consistency while enabling flexibility and innovation. 

Build world-class design systems 

  • Develop scalable systems including typography, color, layout, motion, imagery, iconography and visual frameworks. 

  • Establish standards that enable efficient execution while maintaining exceptional quality. 

  • Create tools and frameworks that simplify execution across internal teams, agency partners and regional markets. 

  • Ensure brand systems can flex across a wide variety of business, marketing and customer needs. 

Lead and develop the design organization 

  • Recruit, mentor and lead a team of designers, brand designers, art directors and design specialists. 

  • Foster an environment centered on craft, rigor, curiosity and continuous improvement. 

  • Establish design review processes that elevate both the quality and consistency of the work. 

  • Build strong partnerships with agency, production and design partners around the world. 

Partner across the creative ecosystem 

  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional creative leadership team to ensure campaign work and brand systems reinforce one another. 

  • Partner with Integrated Marketing, Product Marketing, Retail and Communications teams to ensure cohesive execution across every customer touchpoint. 

  • Influence key business and marketing decisions through the lens of design excellence and customer experience. 

  • Serve as the primary steward of visual brand integrity across Windows, Surface and Services. 



Qualifications
 

Required/minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree or Certificate in Design, Fine Arts, Human Computer Interaction, Visual Communications or related art field AND 8+ years experience in art design or a related art field working on computer games or entertainment OR equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years people management experience (e.g., serving as a Lead Artist, Art Manager, Creative Director, etc.).

Preferred Qualificiations:

  • 12+ years of experience in brand design, visual design, design leadership or related fields. 

  • Experience building, evolving and managing brand identity systems for globally recognized brands. 

  • Proven success leading multidisciplinary design teams and large-scale design initiatives. 

  • Deep expertise across visual identity, typography, photography, motion, digital experiences and design systems. 

  • Experience scaling design systems across multiple channels, markets and customer touchpoints. 

  • Strong portfolio demonstrating excellence in identity design, brand systems and visual storytelling.  

  • Experience leading brand design organizations within technology, consumer products, retail or media. 

  • Experience partnering with advertising and creative leadership teams on large-scale campaign ecosystems. 

  • Demonstrated ability to balance long-term brand stewardship with evolving business and customer needs. 

  • Exceptional attention to craft, detail and systems thinking. 

  • Experience building and mentoring high-performing design teams.

Microsoft Cloud Operations and Innovation (CO&I) is the team behind the cloud.  Within CO&I, the Engineering Procurement & Construction (EPC) organization is responsible for delivering core datacenter infrastructure for Microsoft’s cloud business. The MS portfolio consists of complex, multi-disciplinary, large scale, multi-year datacenter construction and lease projects. We are looking for a passionate, high-energy individual to help build the cloud datacenters that power the world’s largest online services. 

The CO+I Commissioning team is responsible for managing the end-to-end delivery of new data center capacity for CO+I. Through development of leading program management and construction processes, this team is chartered with managing workflow across vertically and horizontally aligned project managers and virtual teams to successfully deliver multi-million-dollar, multi-year data center construction programs.

As a Site Commissioning Manager – Columbus, OH you will work with data center architects, engineers, construction managers, network engineers, data center operations teams and finance teams to streamline and improve data center capacity delivery. Must be capable of performing work in the field on a construction project.

Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for engineers to help achieve that mission.

 

The Compute Silicon & Manufacturing Engineering (CSME) organization within SCHIE is responsible for design, development, manufacturing and packaging of Microsoft's state-of-the-art computer chips, notably the Azure Cobalt. Our solutions provide sustainable strategic advantages to Microsoft and enable our customers to achieve more.

 

As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and hardware infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the SoC Architecture team is instrumental in defining and delivering operational measures of success for hardware manufacturing, improving the planning process, quality, delivery, scale and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware. We are looking for experienced engineers with a dedicated passion for customer focused solutions, insight and industry knowledge to envision and implement future technical solutions that will manage and optimize the Cloud infrastructure.

 

We are seeking a Senior Principal Power Management Architect to lead the definition, optimization, and implementation of power-management capabilities across advanced silicon and computing platforms.

 



Responsibilities
  • Define the end-to-end power-management architecture for complex silicon, firmware, operating-system, and platform environments.
  • Develop power-optimization strategies that balance energy efficiency, performance, thermals, reliability, and product cost.
  • Architect and guide implementation of low-power features, including dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, clock and power gating, idle-state management, workload-aware controls, and power-state transitions.
  • Specify power-management software, firmware interfaces, policies, control loops, and algorithms for real-time and predictive optimization.
  • Establish requirements for voltage, temperature, process, current, activity, and performance sensors; define their placement, calibration, accuracy, telemetry, and control-system integration.
  • Define the SoC power and performance telemetry architecture, including data models, collection paths, aggregation, accuracy, sampling, and interfaces to platform-management and fleet-level telemetry stacks.
  • Review and optimize platform voltage-regulator architecture, including rail partitioning, regulator selection, efficiency, transient response, telemetry, sequencing, control interfaces, and alignment with silicon power-state and workload requirements.
  • Lead thermal-management strategies informed by power-optimization results, silicon characterization, workload behavior, and platform constraints.
  • Define methodologies for thermal design power estimation, measurement, correlation, guard-banding, and validation across pre-silicon and post-silicon environments.
  • Use representative benchmarks and workload suites to characterize performance-per-watt, identify bottlenecks, tune policies, and validate power and performance targets.
  • Partner with architecture, RTL, physical design, validation, firmware, operating-system, performance, thermal, mechanical, and product teams to drive solutions from concept through production.
  • Conduct technical reviews, communicate tradeoffs to senior stakeholders, mentor engineers, and influence roadmap decisions through data-driven recommendations.

 



Qualifications

Required/minimum qualifications

  • Doctorate in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience OR Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field AND 10+ years technical engineering experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field AND 12+ years technical engineering experience OR equivalent experience.

 

Other Requirements

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 
  • This role will require access to information that is controlled for export under export control regulations, potentially under the U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations or Export Administration Regulations, the EU Dual Use Regulation, and/or other export control regulations.  As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to provide either proof of their country of citizenship or proof of their US. residency or other protected status (e.g., under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) for assessment of eligibility to access the export-controlled information. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport. Lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees may verify status using other documents, where applicable.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Extensive industry experience in silicon or system power architecture, with demonstrated technical leadership across multiple product generations.
  • Expert-level understanding of power-management architecture, power optimization, low-power design and implementation techniques, and hardware-software co-design.
  • Deep experience with power-management firmware, software policies, management algorithms, feedback-control techniques, telemetry, and workload-aware optimization.
  • Expertise in sensor technologies used for voltage, temperature, process, current, activity, and thermal monitoring, including calibration, accuracy, noise, sampling, and system-level use.
  • Understanding of thermal management, power delivery, silicon operating limits, reliability considerations, and the relationship between power, performance, voltage, frequency, and temperature.
  • Demonstrated experience with TDP estimation and measurement, power modeling, silicon characterization, data correlation, and production validation.
  • Solid understanding of benchmark selection and utilization for performance optimization, power-performance analysis, workload characterization, and performance-per-watt evaluation.
  • Ability to develop clear architectural specifications and to communicate complex technical decisions to engineering teams and executive stakeholders.
  • Advanced degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.
  • Experience architecting power management for CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, memory subsystems, interconnects, I/O, or heterogeneous system-on-chip designs.
  • Knowledge of pre-silicon modeling, emulation, post-silicon bring-up, telemetry analytics, and automated tuning or optimization frameworks.
  • Experience working across hardware, firmware, operating systems, drivers, platform management, and datacenter or high-performance computing environments.
  • Track record of technical innovation demonstrated through patents, publications, standards participation, or delivery of differentiated production features.

Are you passionate about AI and eager to help transform how the Federal Government delivers on its mission? Join our Cloud & AI Platform Federal team as we help government customers harness the power of cloud and AI to modernize their technology environments, strengthen mission capabilities, and accelerate innovation.

As trusted advisors and subject matter experts, we work alongside Federal customers to modernize infrastructure, optimize operations, and unlock new possibilities with Azure and AI. Whether modernizing environments to be AI-ready, accelerating innovation with AI agents and platforms, empowering developers with AI capabilities, or unifying and modernizing data estates, we help customers build secure, scalable technology solutions that support critical mission outcomes.

In this role, you'll be at the forefront of AI transformation across the Federal Government, helping customers navigate complex technology, security, compliance, and mission requirements while developing strategies that enable them to realize the full potential of cloud and AI. You'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact by helping agencies modernize, innovate, and advance some of the nation's most important missions.

As a Cloud & AI Solution Specialist, you will serve as a solution sales expert within our Federal sales organization, working with strategic government customers across a broad Azure portfolio. You will collaborate closely with technical specialists, partners, customer success, engineering, and consulting resources to advance customer priorities, accelerate cloud and AI adoption, grow Azure consumption, and achieve revenue objectives across your assigned accounts.

Responsibilities

Customer Engagement

Partners across organizations (e.g., Account Team Unit [ATU], CSU, ISD, GPS) to drive deal orchestration and ensure seamless handoffs throughout the deal lifecycle. Team Overview:

The mission of the Microsoft CISO Organization is to defend Microsoft, our customers, and our partners from cybersecurity threats. Our strategy is grounded in advanced threat intelligence, proactive threat hunting, resilient security operations, sustainable governance, and use of AI to anticipate, detect, and respond to even the most sophisticated attacks. 

The CISO Operations Security Implementation & Capability (OSIC) team plays a critical role in turning the CISO strategy into reality. OSIC is responsible for scaling, systematizing, and operationalizing cybersecurity initiatives across the CISO Organization and across Microsoft. OSIC ensures that cybersecurity programs are well-designed, consistently executed, measurable, and sustainable at Microsoft’s global scale. 

Role Overview 

We are seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to join our CISO Operations Security Implementation & Capability (OSIC) team. You will lead complex, cross-organizational cybersecurity programs from problem definition and planning through execution, adoption, and measurable outcomes. You will translate strategic priorities into clear program plans, operating mechanisms, governance, roadmaps, and success measures; use AI, telemetry, and other evidence to improve decisions and delivery; and manage priorities, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs amid ambiguity. You will partner with technical, business, and senior leadership stakeholders to build alignment, remove blockers, and drive accountability. Your work will establish repeatable capabilities that strengthen CISO operations and scale effective practices across Microsoft. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
 
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

 



Responsibilities

  • Translate CISO strategic priorities into executable programs by framing problems, defining outcomes and success measures, establishing governance, mapping dependencies, and creating clear roadmaps and delivery plans. 

  • Build repeatable processes, automated workflows, and reusable program mechanisms that improve execution across participating teams and can be adopted by adjacent programs. 

  • Lead complex, cross-organization initiatives by aligning engineering, security, operations, risk and compliance, and leadership around shared goals, decisions, dependencies, and measurable outcomes.  

  • Leverage AI, telemetry, and data-driven insights to improve speed, accuracy, and impact of program decisions, execution, and operating mechanisms. 

  • Create executive-ready materials and narratives that synthesize complex technical and operational inputs into clear program status, risks, options, tradeoffs, and recommendations for leadership decisions.

    • OR equivalent experience.

  • Citizenship & Citizenship Verification: This role will require access to information that is controlled for export under export control regulations, potentially under the U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations or Export Administration Regulations, the EU Dual Use Regulation, and/or other export control regulations. Security represents a critical priority for our customers in a world awash in digital threats, regulatory scrutiny, and estate complexity. Microsoft Security aspires to make the world a safer place for all. The Microsoft Security organization accelerates Microsoft's mission and bold ambitions to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers' heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. 

Cyber Defense Operations Detection Engineering owns the end-to-end detection system that turns adversary activity into reliable, high-signal cases for investigation at incident speed. This role sits at the center of that system. You will own a detection portfolio: a named set of threat actors, techniques, and partner platforms for which you are singularly accountable for what we detect, what we stop detecting, and whether we can defend that answer to leadership, auditors, and incident reviewers. 

This is a hands-on portfolio role, not a program management role. This role is built for someone who has worked cases. You should have sat in a SOC seat, chased real adversary activity through telemetry, and felt the cost of a noisy detection on the receiving end.  You will author and optimize detections yourself, working directly with our investigation and hunt partners to convert engagement findings into production detection logic. But the majority of your leverage comes from the decisions you make about the portfolio rather than the detections you write personally: what gets built, who builds it, what gets onboarded, and what gets turned off.

We are looking for a Senior Detection Portfolio Engineer to join the team! 

Starting February, 2026, Microsoft employees are expected to work from a designated Microsoft office at least three days a week if they live within 50 miles (U.S.) or 25 miles (non-U.S., country-specific) of that location. This expectation is subject to local law and may vary by jurisdiction.  

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day. 



Responsibilities
  • Own an assigned threat actor and partner portfolio end-to-end, including onboarding, offboarding, and tuning decisions, each with explicit written rationale.
  • Partner directly with investigation and hunt leads to translate investigation, hunt, and incident findings into detection ideas, and author high-fidelity detections against those ideas using Kusto and our detection platform.
  • Gate and approve detections and detection ideas and detection submissions from partner teams against our priorities and charter; return ideas that fail gating with clear, actionable rationale and resubmission guidance.  
  • Review detections authored by others, including partner-team submissions, for intent fidelity, query performance, and production reliability.  
  • Hold the portfolio to an investigator case budget.
  • Make explicit coverage-versus-noise tradeoffs and drive volume down without surrendering coverage on the behaviors that matter.  
  • Select, engineer, tune, and leverage AI-assisted and automation frameworks for all aspects of the detection lifecycle: tuning, gating, triage, and investigation.
  • Serve as the primary interface to partner detection teams and to our investigations partners, routing authoring work to the right owner and enforcing the engagement contract.
  • Participate in the detection workstream on-call rotation and lead the detection workstream during incidents: establish whether a detection fired and why, decide whether we author, decide whether we can leverage an existing detection, and drive that work at incident speed.
  • Maintain an evidence-backed view of detection coverage for your portfolio and produce leadership-ready updates on a regular operating rhythm.

A datacenter is a secure building that houses computer servers, storage equipment and networking technology. You do not need to be a technical expert to understand the role: you will receive guidance while learning how equipment is received, tracked, stored, returned and securely handled.

Microsoft Copilot is transforming how people work by helping them reason across information, stay in context, and accomplish more. Copilot Memory is a foundational part of that experience: it enables Copilot Chat to understand durable user context and deliver more personal, proactive, and trustworthy assistance while preserving enterprise-grade controls. 

The Copilot Work Memory team is evolving memory from user's work context & history continuity into a governed, evaluable, multi-source capability grounded in user's real communications, documents, meetings and work content. The team is solving hard product and technical problems across memory generation, freshness, retrieval, serving, evaluation, transparency, safety, privacy, latency, and cost. 

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own key product areas for Memory in Copilot Chat. This role requires strong technical fluency, excellent end-to-end product judgment, and a hands-on approach to AI quality and evaluation. You will translate customer needs, product signals, and competitive gaps into clear platform and experience requirements, then align engineering, applied science, design, research, security, privacy, and partner teams to deliver measurable customer impact. You ll also work across other teams driving critical parts of Copilot Memory (eg Chat Memory) 

The ideal candidate combines customer obsession with systems thinking: someone who can move comfortably from user scenarios and interaction flows to quality metrics, experiment design, platform tradeoffs, and executive-level decisions. You will operate with significant autonomy in a fast-moving area and help establish the product practices that allow Copilot Memory to improve safely and rapidly. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Responsibilities

  • Own product strategy, roadmap, and execution for key Work Memory capabilities in Copilot Chat, connecting customer scenarios to platform investments and measurable outcomes. 

  • Define end-to-end user experiences for how Copilot captures, refreshes, retrieves, uses, explains, and allows users to control memory across relevant Copilot Chat scenarios. 

  • Translate customer needs, usage and feedback signals, support themes, and competitive insights into durable platform-level requirements rather than one-off feature solutions. 

  • Lead the product quality and evaluation strategy for your area, including representative scenario sets, rubrics, offline evaluations, synthetic or controlled test environments, online metrics, experiment design, regression protection, and failure analysis. 

  • Partner closely with engineering and applied science on technical choices across generation, storage, retrieval, freshness, context budgeting, latency, cost, and model behavior; make clear tradeoffs and drive decisions. 

  • Establish success measures spanning relevance, freshness, personalization utility, task completion, engagement, customer satisfaction, trust, safety, performance, and operational health. 

  • Drive trustworthy product design through transparency, citations or explanations where appropriate, user controls, lifecycle clarity, auditability, privacy, Responsible AI, and enterprise compliance requirements. 

  • Build solid cross-company partnerships across Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365, Work IQ, agents, platform, design, research, security, privacy, marketing, and customer-facing teams; manage dependencies and create clarity in ambiguous spaces. 

  • Communicate strategy, quality insights, risks, and recommendations crisply to senior leaders and stakeholders; run effective product reviews and decision-making rhythms. 

  • Model AI-forward product management through rapid learning, prototyping, data-informed iteration, direct customer engagement, and mentorship of other product managers.
